1.23.s:
sanaka uvāca
idamanyatpravakṣyāmi vrataṃ trailokyaviśrutam /
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam //
1.23.d:
सनक उवाच
इदमन्यत्प्रवक्ष्यामि व्रतं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् ।
सर्वपापप्रशमनं सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ॥
1.23.m:
Sanaka said:
I shall declare this other vow, renowned in the three worlds,
which allays all sins and grants the fruit of all desires,

1.23.s:
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ caiva yopitām /
mokṣadaṃ kurvatāṃ bhaktyā viṣṇoḥ priyataraṃ dvija //
1.23.d:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां चैव योपिताम् ।
मोक्षदं कुर्वतां भक्त्या विष्णोः प्रियतरं द्विज ॥
1.23.m:
bestowing liberation on Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and women
who perform it with devotion, exceedingly dear to Viṣṇu, O twice-born.

1.23.s:
ekādaśīvrataṃ nāma sarvābhīṣṭapradaṃ nṛṇām /.
karttavyaṃ sarvathā vipraviṣṇuprītikaraṃ yataḥ //
1.23.d:
एकादशीव्रतं नाम सर्वाभीष्टप्रदं नृणाम् ॥
कर्त्तव्यं सर्वथा विप्रविष्णुप्रीतिकरं यतः ॥
1.23.m:
The vow named Ekādaśī grants all desired things to men;
it should be performed by all means, O Brahmin, since it causes delight to Viṣṇu.

1.23.s:
ekādaśyāṃ na bhuñjīta pakṣayorubhayopari /
yo bhuṅkte so 'tra pāpīyānparatra narakaṃ vrajet //
1.23.d:
एकादश्यां न भुञ्जीत पक्षयोरुभयोपरि ।
यो भुङ्क्ते सो ऽत्र पापीयान्परत्र नरकं व्रजेत् ॥
1.23.m:
One should not eat on the eleventh lunar day in either of the two fortnights;
he who eats is a sinner in this world and goes to hell in the next.

1.23.s:
upavāsaphalaṃ lipsurjahyādbhukticatuṣṭayam /
pūrvāparadine gatrāvahorātraṃ tu madhyame //
1.23.d:
उपवासफलं लिप्सुर्जह्याद्भुक्तिचतुष्टयम् ।
पूर्वापरदिने गत्रावहोरात्रं तु मध्यमे ॥
1.23.m:
Desiring the fruit of fasting, one should renounce four meals:
on the previous and following days [the meal] at night, but on the middle day [the meals of] both day and night.

1.23.s:
ekādaśīdine yastu bhoktumicchati mānavaḥ /
sa bhoktuṃ sarvalapāpāni spṛhayālurnasaṃśayaḥ //
1.23.d:
एकादशीदिने यस्तु भोक्तुमिच्छति मानवः ।
स भोक्तुं सर्वलपापानि स्पृहयालुर्नसंशयः ॥
1.23.m:
Whatever person wishes to eat on the day of Ekādaśī,
he desires to consume all sins, without a doubt.

1.23.s:
bhaveddaśamyāmekāśīdvādaśyāṃ ca munīśvara /
ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāro yadi muktimabhīpsati //
1.23.d:
भवेद्दशम्यामेकाशीद्वादश्यां च मुनीश्वर ।
एकादश्यां निराहारो यदि मुक्तिमभीप्सति ॥
1.23.m:
On the tenth day he should be eating once, and on the twelfth, O lord of sages,
[remaining] without food on the eleventh, if he desires liberation.

1.23.s:
yāni kāni ca pāpāni brahmahatyādikāni ca /
annamāśritya tiṣṭhanti tāni vipra hareśvara /
ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāro yadi muktimabhīpsati //
yāni kāni ca pāpāni brahmahakatyādikāni ca /
annamāśritya tiṣṭhanti tāni ca munīśvara /
ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāro yadi muktimabhīpsati //
yāni kāni ca pāpāni brahmahatyādikāni ca ca //
1.23.d:
यानि कानि च पापानि ब्रह्महत्यादिकानि च ।
अन्नमाश्रित्य तिष्ठन्ति तानि विप्र हरेश्वर ।
एकादश्यां निराहारो यदि मुक्तिमभीप्सति ॥
यानि कानि च पापानि ब्रह्महकत्यादिकानि च ।
अन्नमाश्रित्य तिष्ठन्ति तानि च मुनीश्वर ।
एकादश्यां निराहारो यदि मुक्तिमभीप्सति ॥
यानि कानि च पापानि ब्रह्महत्यादिकानि च च ॥
1.23.m:
Whatever sins there are, such as the killing of a Brahmin,
take refuge in food, O Brahmin, on the day of Hari.
[Remaining] without food on the eleventh, if he desires liberation,
whatever sins there are, such as the killing of a Brahmin,
take refuge in food, O lord of sages;
[remaining] without food on the eleventh, if he desires liberation,

whatever sins there are, such as the killing of a Brahmin,

take refuge in food on the day of Hari, O Brahmin.
For sins like the killing of a Brahmin there may somehow be an expiation,
but for him who eats on the eleventh, there is no expiation at all.

1.23.s:
annamāśritya tiṣṭanti tāni vipra harerdine //
brahmahatyādipāpānāṃ kathañcinniṣkṛtirbhavet /
ekādaśyāṃ tu yo bhuṅkte tasya naivāsti niṣkṛtiḥ //
1.23.d:
अन्नमाश्रित्य तिष्टन्ति तानि विप्र हरेर्दिने ॥
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापानां कथञ्चिन्निष्कृतिर्भवेत् ।
एकादश्यां तु यो भुङ्क्ते तस्य नैवास्ति निष्कृतिः ॥

1.23.s:
mahāpātakayukto vāyukto vā sarva pānakaiḥ /
ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāraḥ sthitvā yāti parāṃ gatim //
1.23.d:
महापातकयुक्तो वायुक्तो वा सर्व पानकैः ।
एकादश्यां निराहारः स्थित्वा याति परां गतिम् ॥
1.23.m:
Whether joined with great sins or joined with all wicked deeds,
by remaining without food on the eleventh, one goes to the supreme state.

1.23.s:
ekādaśī mahāpuṇyā viṣṇoḥ priyatamā tithiḥ /
saṃsevyā sarvathā vipraiḥ saṃsāracche dalipsubhiḥ //
1.23.d:
एकादशी महापुण्या विष्णोः प्रियतमा तिथिः ।
संसेव्या सर्वथा विप्रैः संसारच्छे दलिप्सुभिः ॥
1.23.m:
The eleventh lunar day is exceedingly meritorious, the lunar day dearest to Viṣṇu;
it must be observed by all means by Brahmins who desire the severance of worldly existence.

1.23.s:
daśamyāṃ prātarutthāya dantadhāvanapūrvakam /
snāpayedvidhivadviṣṇuṃ pūjayetprayatendriyaḥ //
1.23.d:
दशम्यां प्रातरुत्थाय दन्तधावनपूर्वकम् ।
स्नापयेद्विधिवद्विष्णुं पूजयेत्प्रयतेन्द्रियः ॥
1.23.m:
Having risen in the morning on the tenth day, preceded by the cleaning of teeth,
with senses self-controlled, one should bathe Viṣṇu according to rule and worship him.

1.23.s:
ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāro nigṛhītendriyo bhavet /
śayīta sannidhau viṣṇornārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.23.d:
एकादश्यां निराहारो निगृहीतेन्द्रियो भवेत् ।
शयीत सन्निधौ विष्णोर्नारायणपरायणः ॥
1.23.m:
On the eleventh day, one should remain without food, with senses restrained;
dedicated to Nārāyaṇa, one should sleep in the presence of Viṣṇu.

1.23.s:
ekādaśyāṃ tathā snātvā saṃpūjyaca ca janārdanam /
gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ samyak tatastve vasudīrayet //
1.23.d:
एकादश्यां तथा स्नात्वा संपूज्यच च जनार्दनम् ।
गन्धपुष्पादिभिः सम्यक् ततस्त्वे वसुदीरयेत् ॥
1.23.m:
And likewise having bathed on the eleventh and thoroughly worshipped Janārdana
with fragrant scents, flowers, and the like, one should then utter thus:

1.23.s:
ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāraḥ sthitvādyāhaṃ pare 'hani /
bhokṣyāmi puṇḍarīkākṣa śaraṇaṃ me bhavācyuta //
1.23.d:
एकादश्यां निराहारः स्थित्वाद्याहं परे ऽहनि ।
भोक्ष्यामि पुण्डरीकाक्ष शरणं मे भवाच्युत ॥
1.23.m:
'Having remained without food today on the eleventh day,
I shall eat on the next day, O lotus-eyed one; be my refuge, O Acyuta.'

1.23.s:
imaṃ mantraṃ samuccārthaṃ deva devasya cakriṇaḥ /
bhaktibhāvena tuṣṭātmā upavāsaṃ samarpayet //
1.23.d:
इमं मन्त्रं समुच्चार्थं देव देवस्य चक्रिणः ।
भक्तिभावेन तुष्टात्मा उपवासं समर्पयेत् ॥
1.23.m:
Having uttered this mantra before the discus-bearing God of gods,
one with a content soul should offer the fast with an attitude of devotion.

1.23.s:
devasya purataḥ kuryājjāgaraṃ niyato vratī /
gītairvādyaiśaaca nṛtyaiśca purāṇaśravaṇādibhiḥ //
1.23.d:
देवस्य पुरतः कुर्याज्जागरं नियतो व्रती ।
गीतैर्वाद्यैशअच नृत्यैश्च पुराणश्रवणादिभिः ॥
1.23.m:
The restrained practitioner of the vow should keep vigil in front of the deity
with songs, musical instruments, dances, and hearing the Purāṇas and the like.

1.23.s:
tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya dvādaśīdivase vratī /
snātvā ca vidhivadviṣṇuṃ pūjayatprayatendriyaḥ //
1.23.d:
ततः प्रातः समुत्थाय द्वादशीदिवसे व्रती ।
स्नात्वा च विधिवद्विष्णुं पूजयत्प्रयतेन्द्रियः ॥
1.23.m:
Then having arisen in the morning on the twelfth day, the practitioner of the vow,
having bathed and with senses self-controlled, should worship Viṣṇu according to rule.

1.23.s:
pañcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya ekādaśyāṃ janārddanam /
dvādaśyāṃ payasā vipra harisārupapyamaṣaśnute //
1.23.d:
पञ्चामृतेन संस्नाप्य एकादश्यां जनार्द्दनम् ।
द्वादश्यां पयसा विप्र हरिसारुपप्यमषश्नुते ॥
1.23.m:
Having bathed Janārdana with the five nectars on the eleventh day
and with milk on the twelfth, O Brahmin, one attains sameness of form with Hari.

1.23.s:
ajñānatimirāndhasya vratenānena keśava /
prasīda sumukho bhūtvā jñānadṛṣṭiprado bhava //
1.23.d:
अज्ञानतिमिरान्धस्य व्रतेनानेन केशव ।
प्रसीद सुमुखो भूत्वा ज्ञानदृष्टिप्रदो भव ॥
1.23.m:
'For me, blinded by the darkness of ignorance, through this vow, O Keśava,
be pleased, showing a gracious countenance, and become the bestower of the vision of knowledge.'

1.23.s:
evaṃ vijñāpya viprendra mādhavaṃ susamāhitaḥ /
brahmaṇānbhojayecchaktyā dadyādvai dakṣiṇāṃ tathā //
1.23.d:
एवं विज्ञाप्य विप्रेन्द्र माधवं सुसमाहितः ।
ब्रह्मणान्भोजयेच्छक्त्या दद्याद्वै दक्षिणां तथा ॥
1.23.m:
Having prayed thus to Mādhava with mind well concentrated, O chief of Brahmins,
one should feed Brahmins according to one's capacity and likewise give a priestly gift.

1.23.s:
tataḥ svabandhubhiḥ sārddhaṃ nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ /
kṛtapañcamahāyajñaḥ svayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ //
1.23.d:
ततः स्वबन्धुभिः सार्द्धं नारायणपरायणः ।
कृतपञ्चमहायज्ञः स्वयं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥
1.23.m:
Then together with his relatives, dedicated to Nārāyaṇa,
having performed the five great sacrifices, he should eat himself, with speech restrained.

1.23.s:
evaṃ yaḥ prayataḥ kuryātpuṇyamekādaśīvratam /
sa yāti viṣṇubhavanaṃ punarāvṛttidurlabham //
1.23.d:
एवं यः प्रयतः कुर्यात्पुण्यमेकादशीव्रतम् ।
स याति विष्णुभवनं पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभम् ॥
1.23.m:
He who self-controlled thus performs the sacred vow of Ekādaśī
goes to the abode of Viṣṇu, whence return is hard to obtain.

1.23.s:
upavāsavrataparo dharmakāryacaparāyaṇaḥ /
cāṇḍālānpatakitāṃścaiva nekṣedapi kadācana //
1.23.d:
उपवासव्रतपरो धर्मकार्यचपरायणः ।
चाण्डालान्पतकितांश्चैव नेक्षेदपि कदाचन ॥
1.23.m:
Devoted to the vow of fasting, intent on righteous deeds,
one should never even look upon outcasts and fallen men.

1.23.s:
nāstikānbhinnamaryodānnindakānpiśunāṃstathā /
upavāsa vrataparo nālapecca kadācana //
1.23.d:
नास्तिकान्भिन्नमर्योदान्निन्दकान्पिशुनांस्तथा ।
उपवास व्रतपरो नालपेच्च कदाचन ॥
1.23.m:
Atheists, violators of bounds, slanderers, and tale-bearers
one devoted to the vow of fasting should never converse with.

1.23.s:
vṛṣalīsūtipoṣṭāraṃ vṛṣalīpatimeva ca /
ayājyayājakaṃ caiva nālapetsarvadā vratī //
1.23.d:
वृषलीसूतिपोष्टारं वृषलीपतिमेव च ।
अयाज्ययाजकं चैव नालपेत्सर्वदा व्रती ॥
1.23.m:
The fosterer of a Śūdra woman's offspring, the husband of a Śūdra woman,
and one who sacrifices for those unfit to sacrifice, the practitioner of the vow must never converse with.

1.23.s:
kuṇḍaśinaṃ gāyakaṃ ca tathā devalakāśinam /
bhiṣajaṃ kāvyakarttāraṃ devadvijavirodhinam //
1.23.d:
कुण्डशिनं गायकं च तथा देवलकाशिनम् ।
भिषजं काव्यकर्त्तारं देवद्विजविरोधिनम् ॥
1.23.m:
An eater of an adulteress's son's food, a professional singer, likewise an eater of temple priest's offerings,
a physician, a poet, and an opponent of gods and Brahmins,

1.23.s:
parānnalolupaṃ caiva parastrīnirataṃ tathā /
vratopavāsanirato vāṅmātreṇāpi nārcayet //
1.23.d:
परान्नलोलुपं चैव परस्त्रीनिरतं तथा ।
व्रतोपवासनिरतो वाङ्मात्रेणापि नार्चयेत् ॥
1.23.m:
one greedy for another's food, and likewise one devoted to another's wife—
one devoted to vows and fasts should not honor even with words alone.

1.23.s:
ityevamādibhiḥ śuddho vaśī sarvahite rataḥ /
upavāsaparo bhūtvā parāṃ siddhimavānpuyāt //
1.23.d:
इत्येवमादिभिः शुद्धो वशी सर्वहिते रतः ।
उपवासपरो भूत्वा परां सिद्धिमवान्पुयात् ॥
1.23.m:
Pure through these and other [practices], self-controlled, delighting in the welfare of all,
becoming devoted to fasting, one attains the supreme perfection.

1.23.s:
nāsti gaṅgāsamaṃ tīrthaṃ nāsti mātṛsamoguruḥ /
nāstu viṣṇusamaṃ daivaṃ tapo nānaśanātparam //
1.23.d:
नास्ति गङ्गासमं तीर्थं नास्ति मातृसमोगुरुः ।
नास्तु विष्णुसमं दैवं तपो नानशनात्परम् ॥
1.23.m:
There is no sacred ford equal to the Gaṅgā; there is no guru equal to a mother;
there is no deity equal to Viṣṇu; there is no austerity higher than fasting.

1.23.s:
nāsti kṣamāsamā mātā nāsti kīrtisamaṃ dhanam /
nāsti jñānasamo lābho lābho na ca dharma samaḥ pitā //
1.23.d:
नास्ति क्षमासमा माता नास्ति कीर्तिसमं धनम् ।
नास्ति ज्ञानसमो लाभो लाभो न च धर्म समः पिता ॥
1.23.m:
There is no mother equal to forbearance; there is no wealth equal to fame;
there is no gain equal to knowledge; and there is no father equal to righteousness.

1.23.s:
na vivekasamo bandhurmaikādaśyāḥ paraṃ vratam /
atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam //
1.23.d:
न विवेकसमो बन्धुर्मैकादश्याः परं व्रतम् ।
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ॥
1.23.m: There is no friend equal to discrimination; there is no vow higher than the Ekādaśī. / In this connection also they recount this ancient historical account,

1.23.s:
saṃvādaṃ bhadraśīlasya tatpiturgulavasya ca /
purā higālavo nāma muniḥ satyaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.23.d:
संवादं भद्रशीलस्य तत्पितुर्गुलवस्य च ।
पुरा हिगालवो नाम मुनिः सत्यपरायणः ॥
1.23.m: the dialogue between Bhadraśīla and his father, Gālava. / In former times there lived a sage named Gālava, devoted to truth,

1.23.s:
uvā casa narmadātīrere śānto dāntastaponidhiḥ /
bahuvṛkṣasamākīrṇe gajabhalluniṣevite //
1.23.d:
उवा चस नर्मदातीरेरे शान्तो दान्तस्तपोनिधिः ।
बहुवृक्षसमाकीर्णे गजभल्लुनिषेविते ॥
1.23.m: a treasury of asceticism, calm and self-controlled, who dwelt on the bank of the Narmadā, / teeming with numerous trees and frequented by elephants and bears,

1.23.s:
siddhacāraṇagandharva yakṣavidyādharānvite /
kandamūlaphalaiḥ pūrṇe munivṛndaniṣedite //
1.23.d:
सिद्धचारणगन्धर्व यक्षविद्याधरान्विते ।
कन्दमूलफलैः पूर्णे मुनिवृन्दनिषेदिते ॥
1.23.m: accompanied by Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and Vidyādharas, / filled with tubers, roots, and fruits, and frequented by hosts of sages.

1.23.s:
gālavo nāma viprendro nivāsamakasecciram /
tasyābhavadbhadraśīla iti khyātaḥ suto vaśī //
1.23.d:
गालवो नाम विप्रेन्द्रो निवासमकसेच्चिरम् ।
तस्याभवद्भद्रशील इति ख्यातः सुतो वशी ॥
1.23.m: That foremost of brāhmaṇas, named Gālava, made his abode [there] for a long time. / He had a self-controlled son known as Bhadraśīla.

1.23.s:
jāntismaro mahābhāgo nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ /
bālakrāḍanakāle 'pi bhadraśīlo mahāmatiḥ //
1.23.d:
जान्तिस्मरो महाभागो नारायणपरायणः ।
बालक्राडनकाले ऽपि भद्रशीलो महामतिः ॥
1.23.m: Remembering his previous births, exceedingly fortunate, devoted to Nārāyaṇa, / even at the time of childhood play, the highly intelligent Bhadraśīla,

1.23.s:
mṛdā ca viṣṇoḥ pratimāṃ kṛtvā pūjayate kṣaṇam /
vayasyānbodhayeccāpi viṣṇuḥ pūjyo naraiḥ sadā //
1.23.d:
मृदा च विष्णोः प्रतिमां कृत्वा पूजयते क्षणम् ।
वयस्यान्बोधयेच्चापि विष्णुः पूज्यो नरैः सदा ॥
1.23.m: having fashioned an image of Viṣṇu out of clay, would worship it for a moment, / and he would also instruct his companions: “Viṣṇu must always be worshipped by men,

1.23.s:
ekādaśīvrataṃ caiva karttavyamapi paṇḍitaiḥ /
evaṃ te bodhitāstena śiśavo 'pi munīśvara //
1.23.d:
एकादशीव्रतं चैव कर्त्तव्यमपि पण्डितैः ।
एवं ते बोधितास्तेन शिशवो ऽपि मुनीश्वर ॥
1.23.m: and the Ekādaśī vow should also be performed by the wise.” / Thus instructed by him, even those children, O lord of sages,

1.23.s:
hariṃ mṛdaiva nirmāya pṛthaksaṃbhūya vā mudā /
arcayanti mahābhāgā viṣṇubhaktiparāyaṇāḥ //
1.23.d:
हरिं मृदैव निर्माय पृथक्संभूय वा मुदा ।
अर्चयन्ति महाभागा विष्णुभक्तिपरायणाः ॥
1.23.m: having fashioned Hari out of clay alone, individually or joined together with joy, / worshipped [Him], highly fortunate and devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu.

1.23.s:
namaskurvanbhadramati rviṣṇave sarvaviṣṇave /
sarveṣāṃ jagatāṃ svasti bhūyādityabravīdidam //
1.23.d:
नमस्कुर्वन्भद्रमति र्विष्णवे सर्वविष्णवे ।
सर्वेषां जगतां स्वस्ति भूयादित्यब्रवीदिदम् ॥
1.23.m: Bowing to Viṣṇu, who pervades everything, the noble-minded one / said this: “May there be well-being for all the worlds.”

1.23.s:
krīḍākāle muhūrtaṃ vā muhūrtārddhamathāpi vā /
ekādaśīti saṃkalpyavrataṃ yacchati keśave //
1.23.d:
क्रीडाकाले मुहूर्तं वा मुहूर्तार्द्धमथापि वा ।
एकादशीति संकल्प्यव्रतं यच्छति केशवे ॥
1.23.m: At playtime, for a muhūrta or even half a muhūrta, / having made the resolve, “It is Ekādaśī,” he would dedicate the vow to Keśava.

1.23.s:
evaṃ sucaritaṃ dṛṣṭvā tanayaṃ gālavo muniḥ /
apṛcchadvismayāviṣṭaḥ samāliṅgya taponidhiḥ //
1.23.d:
एवं सुचरितं दृष्ट्वा तनयं गालवो मुनिः ।
अपृच्छद्विस्मयाविष्टः समालिङ्ग्य तपोनिधिः ॥
1.23.m: Seeing his son's virtuous conduct thus, the sage Gālava, / filled with wonder, embraced him, a treasury of asceticism, and asked:

1.23.s:
gālava uvāca
bhadraśīla mahābhāga bhadraśīlo 'si suvrata /
caritaṃ maṅgalaṃ yatte yogināmapi durlabham //
1.23.d:
गालव उवाच
भद्रशील महाभाग भद्रशीलो ऽसि सुव्रत ।
चरितं मङ्गलं यत्ते योगिनामपि दुर्लभम् ॥
1.23.m: Gālava said: / “O Bhadraśīla of great fortune, you are indeed of auspicious conduct, steadfast in vows, / since your conduct is auspicious, difficult to attain even for yogins.

1.23.s:
haripūjāparo nityaṃ sarvabhūtahiterataḥ /
ekādaśīvrataparo niṣiddhācāravarjitaḥ /
nirddhandvo nirmamaḥ śānto haridhyānaparāyāṇaḥ //
1.23.d:
हरिपूजापरो नित्यं सर्वभूतहितेरतः ।
एकादशीव्रतपरो निषिद्धाचारवर्जितः ।
निर्द्धन्द्वो निर्ममः शान्तो हरिध्यानपरायाणः ॥
1.23.m: Always devoted to the worship of Hari, delighting in the welfare of all beings, / devoted to the Ekādaśī vow, free from prohibited conduct, / free from dualities, devoid of possessiveness, calm, intent on meditation on Hari,

1.23.s:
evametādṛśī buddhiḥ kathaṃ jātārbhakasyate /
vināpi mahatāṃ sevāṃ haribhaktirhi durlabhā //
1.23.d:
एवमेतादृशी बुद्धिः कथं जातार्भकस्यते ।
विनापि महतां सेवां हरिभक्तिर्हि दुर्लभा ॥
1.23.m: how has such intellect arisen in you, a child? / For devotion to Hari is difficult to attain without service to the great.

1.23.s:
svabhāvato janasyāsya hyavidyākāmakarmasu /
pravarttate matirvatsa kathaṃ te 'laukikī kṛtiḥ //
1.23.d:
स्वभावतो जनस्यास्य ह्यविद्याकामकर्मसु ।
प्रवर्त्तते मतिर्वत्स कथं ते ऽलौकिकी कृतिः ॥
1.23.m: By nature, the intellect of ordinary people is engaged / in ignorance, desire, and selfish actions, my child; how is your action so extraordinary?

1.23.s:
satsaṅge 'pi manuṣyāṇāṃ pūrvapuṇyātirekataḥ /
jāyate bhagavadbhaktistadahaṃ vismayaṃ gataḥ //
1.23.d:
सत्सङ्गे ऽपि मनुष्याणां पूर्वपुण्यातिरेकतः ।
जायते भगवद्भक्तिस्तदहं विस्मयं गतः ॥
1.23.m: Even with the company of the good, devotion to the Lord arises in men / [only] through an abundance of previous merit; therefore, I am filled with astonishment.

1.23.s:
pṛcchāmi prītimāpannastadbhavānvaktumarhati /
bhadraśīlo muniśreṣṭhaḥ pitraivaṃ suvikalpitaiḥ //
1.23.d:
पृच्छामि प्रीतिमापन्नस्तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ।
भद्रशीलो मुनिश्रेष्ठः पित्रैवं सुविकल्पितैः ॥
1.23.m: Filled with affection, I ask you: you ought to tell me that.” / Bhadraśīla, foremost of sages, thus thoughtfully questioned by his father,

1.23.s:
jātismaraḥ sukṛtātmā hṛṣathṭaprahasitānanaḥ /
svānabhrutaṃ yathāvrataṃ sarvaṃ pitre nyavedayat //
1.23.d:
जातिस्मरः सुकृतात्मा हृषथ्टप्रहसिताननः ।
स्वानभ्रुतं यथाव्रतं सर्वं पित्रे न्यवेदयत् ॥
1.23.m: remembering his previous births, virtuous in nature, his face cheerful with a smile, / related everything to his father, just as it had been experienced and observed by him.

1.23.s:
bhadraśīla uvāca
śṛṇu tāta muniśreṣṭha hyanubhūtaṃ mayā purā /
jātismaratvājjānāmi yamena paribhāṣitam //
1.23.d:
भद्रशील उवाच
शृणु तात मुनिश्रेष्ठ ह्यनुभूतं मया पुरा ।
जातिस्मरत्वाज्जानामि यमेन परिभाषितम् ॥
1.23.m: Bhadraśīla said: / “Listen, dear father, foremost of sages, to what was experienced by me in the past; / through my recollection of previous births, I know what was spoken by Yama.”

1.23.s:
etacchatvā mahābhāgo gālavo vismayonvitaḥ /
uvāca prītimāpanno bhadraśīlaṃ mahāmatim //
1.23.d:
एतच्छत्वा महाभागो गालवो विस्मयोन्वितः ।
उवाच प्रीतिमापन्नो भद्रशीलं महामतिम् ॥
1.23.m: Hearing this, the highly fortunate Gālava was filled with wonder, / and full of affection, he spoke to the highly intelligent Bhadraśīla.

1.23.s:
gālava uvāca
kastvaṃ pūrvaṃ mahābhāga kimuktaṃ ca yamena te /
kasya vā kena vā hetostatsarvaṃ vaktumarhasi //
1.23.d:
गालव उवाच
कस्त्वं पूर्वं महाभाग किमुक्तं च यमेन ते ।
कस्य वा केन वा हेतोस्तत्सर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
1.23.m: Gālava said: / “Who were you formerly, O fortunate one? And what was spoken to you by Yama? / For whose sake, or for what reason? You ought to tell me all of that.”

1.23.s:
bhadraśīla uvāca
ahamāsaṃ purā tāta rājā somakulodbhavaḥ /
dharmakīrtiriti khyāto dattātragheyeṇa śāsitaḥ //
1.23.d:
भद्रशील उवाच
अहमासं पुरा तात राजा सोमकुलोद्भवः ।
धर्मकीर्तिरिति ख्यातो दत्तात्रघेयेण शासितः ॥
1.23.m: Bhadraśīla said: / “In the past, father, I was a king born of the Lunar dynasty, / known as Dharmakīrti, instructed by Dattātreya.

1.23.s:
nava varṣasahasrāṇi mahīṃ kṛtstramapālayam /
adharmāśca tathā dharmā mayā tu bahavaḥ kṛtāḥ //
1.23.d:
नव वर्षसहस्राणि महीं कृत्स्त्रमपालयम् ।
अधर्माश्च तथा धर्मा मया तु बहवः कृताः ॥
1.23.m: For nine thousand years I protected the entire earth. / Yet many righteous acts as well as unrighteous acts were performed by me.

1.23.s:
tataḥ śriyā pramatto 'haṃ bahvadharmama kāripam /
pāpaṇḍajanasaṃsargātpāpaṇḍacarito 'bhavam //
1.23.d:
ततः श्रिया प्रमत्तो ऽहं बह्वधर्मम कारिपम् ।
पापण्डजनसंसर्गात्पापण्डचरितो ऽभवम् ॥
1.23.m: Then, intoxicated with wealth, I committed much unrighteousness; / through associating with heretics, I became one of heretical conduct.

1.23.s:
purārjitāni puṇyāni mayā tu subahūnyapi /
pāpaṇḍairbādhito 'haṃ tu vedamārgaṃ samatyajam //
1.23.d:
पुरार्जितानि पुण्यानि मया तु सुबहून्यपि ।
पापण्डैर्बाधितो ऽहं तु वेदमार्गं समत्यजम् ॥
1.23.m: Even though very many merits had been acquired by me previously, / oppressed by heretics, I completely abandoned the path of the Vedas.

1.23.s:
makhāśca sarve vidhvastā kūṭayuktividā mayā /
adharmanirataṃ māṃ tu dṛṣṭvā maheśajāḥ //
1.23.d:
मखाश्च सर्वे विध्वस्ता कूटयुक्तिविदा मया ।
अधर्मनिरतं मां तु दृष्ट्वा महेशजाः ॥
1.23.m: All sacrifices were destroyed by me, skilled in deceptive arguments. / Seeing me intent on unrighteousness, my subjects

1.23.s:
sadaiva duṣkṛtaṃ cakruḥ ṣaṣṭāṃśastatrame 'bhavat /
evaṃ pāpasamācāro vyasanābhirataḥ sadā //
1.23.d:
सदैव दुष्कृतं चक्रुः षष्टांशस्तत्रमे ऽभवत् ।
एवं पापसमाचारो व्यसनाभिरतः सदा ॥
1.23.m: constantly committed wicked deeds, and the sixth part of that became mine. / Thus of sinful conduct, always given over to vices,

1.23.s:
mṛgayābhirarato bhūtvā hyakadā prāviśaṃ vanam /
sasainyo 'haṃ vane tatra hatvā bahuvidhānmṛgān //
1.23.d:
मृगयाभिररतो भूत्वा ह्यकदा प्राविशं वनम् ।
ससैन्यो ऽहं वने तत्र हत्वा बहुविधान्मृगान् ॥
1.23.m: fond of hunting, I once entered a forest. / There in the forest with my army, having slain many kinds of deer,

1.23.s:
kṣuttṛṭparivṛtaḥ śrānto revātīramupāgamam /
ravitīkṣṇātapalkānto revāyāṃ snānamācaram //
1.23.d:
क्षुत्तृट्परिवृतः श्रान्तो रेवातीरमुपागमम् ।
रवितीक्ष्णातपल्कान्तो रेवायां स्नानमाचरम् ॥
1.23.m: overcome with hunger and thirst, and weary, I reached the bank of the Revā. / Exhausted by the fierce heat of the sun, I bathed in the Revā.

1.23.s: ahaṣṭasainya ekākī pīḍyamānaḥ kṣudhā bhṛśam //
1.23.d: अहष्टसैन्य एकाकी पीड्यमानः क्षुधा भृशम् ॥
1.23.m: Separated from my army, alone, exceedingly tormented by hunger,

1.23.s:
sametāstatragha ye kecidrevātīranivāsinaḥ /
ekādaśīvrataparā mayā dṛṣṭvā niśāmukhe //
1.23.d:
समेतास्तत्रघ ये केचिद्रेवातीरनिवासिनः ।
एकादशीव्रतपरा मया दृष्ट्वा निशामुखे ॥
1.23.m: at nightfall I saw certain inhabitants assembled on the bank of the Revā, / devoted to the vow of Ekādaśī.

1.23.s:
nirāhāraśca tatrāhame kākī katajjanaiḥ saha /
jāgaraṃ kṛtavāṃśvāpi senayā rahito niśi //
1.23.d:
निराहारश्च तत्राहमे काकी कतज्जनैः सह ।
जागरं कृतवांश्वापि सेनया रहितो निशि ॥
1.23.m: And there, without food, alone, in the company of those people, / separated from my army at night, I kept the vigil.

1.23.s:
adhvaśramapariśrāntaḥ kṣutpipāsāprapīḍitaḥ /
tatraiva jāgarānte 'haṃ tātapañcatvamāgataḥ //
1.23.d:
अध्वश्रमपरिश्रान्तः क्षुत्पिपासाप्रपीडितः ।
तत्रैव जागरान्ते ऽहं तातपञ्चत्वमागतः ॥
1.23.m: Exhausted from the fatigue of travel, deeply tormented by hunger and thirst, / right there at the end of the vigil, O father, I met my death.

1.23.s:
tato yamabhaṭairbaddho mahādaṃṣṭrābhayaṅkaraiḥ /
anekalkeśasaṃpannamārgeṇātpo yamāntikam /
daṃṣṭrākarālavadanamapaśyaṃ samavartinam //
1.23.d:
ततो यमभटैर्बद्धो महादंष्ट्राभयङ्करैः ।
अनेकल्केशसंपन्नमार्गेणात्पो यमान्तिकम् ।
दंष्ट्राकरालवदनमपश्यं समवर्तिनम् ॥
1.23.m: Then, bound by the soldiers of Yama, terrifying with large fangs, / brought to the presence of Yama along a path filled with many afflictions, / I beheld Samavartin, whose face was formidable with large fangs.

1.23.s:
atha kāliścitragutpamāhūyedamabhāṣata /
asya śikṣāvidhānaṃ ca yathāvadvada paṇḍitaṃ //
1.23.d:
अथ कालिश्चित्रगुत्पमाहूयेदमभाषत ।
अस्य शिक्षाविधानं च यथावद्वद पण्डितं ॥
1.23.m: Then Kāla summoned Citragupta and spoke this: / ‘Declare duly the dispensation of his punishment, O learned one.’

1.23.s:
evamuktaścitragutpo dharmarājena sattama /
ciraṃ vicārayāmāsa punaścedamabhāpata //
1.23.d:
एवमुक्तश्चित्रगुत्पो धर्मराजेन सत्तम ।
चिरं विचारयामास पुनश्चेदमभापत ॥
1.23.m: Thus addressed by the King of Justice, O most excellent one, Citragupta / deliberated for a long time, and then spoke this:

1.23.s:
asau pāparataḥ satyaṃ tathāpi śṛṇu dharmapa /
ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāraḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
1.23.d:
असौ पापरतः सत्यं तथापि शृणु धर्मप ।
एकादश्यां निराहारः सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
1.23.m: ‘This man was devoted to sin, it is true; nevertheless, listen, O guardian of justice: / one who is without food on an Ekādaśī is freed from all sins.

1.23.s:
eṣa revātaṭe ramye nirāhāro harerdine /
jāgaraṃ copavāsaṃ ca kṛtvā niṣaapāpatāṃ gataḥ //
1.23.d:
एष रेवातटे रम्ये निराहारो हरेर्दिने ।
जागरं चोपवासं च कृत्वा निषअपापतां गतः ॥
1.23.m: On the delightful bank of the Revā, without food on the day of Hari, / having observed both the vigil and the fast, he has attained sinlessness.

1.23.s:
yāni kāni ca pāpāni kṛtāni subahūni ca /
tāni sarvāṇi naṣṭāni hyupavāsaprabhāvataḥ //
1.23.d:
यानि कानि च पापानि कृतानि सुबहूनि च ।
तानि सर्वाणि नष्टानि ह्युपवासप्रभावतः ॥
1.23.m: Whatever sins were committed, even though very many, / all of them were destroyed simply by the power of that fast.’

1.23.s:
evamukto dharmarājaścitragutpena dhīmatā /'
nānāma daṇḍavadbhūmau mamāgre so 'nukaṃpitaḥ //
1.23.d:
एवमुक्तो धर्मराजश्चित्रगुत्पेन धीमता ।'
नानाम दण्डवद्भूमौ ममाग्रे सो ऽनुकंपितः ॥
1.23.m: Thus addressed by the wise Citragupta, the King of Justice / bowed down like a staff upon the ground before me, full of compassion.

1.23.s:
pūjayāmāsa māṃ tatra bhaktibhāvena dhairmarāṭ /
tataśca svabhaṭānsarvānāhūyedamuvāca ha //
1.23.d:
पूजयामास मां तत्र भक्तिभावेन धैर्मराट् ।
ततश्च स्वभटान्सर्वानाहूयेदमुवाच ह ॥
1.23.m: The King of Justice worshipped me there with devotion. / And then, summoning all his soldiers, he said this:

1.23.s:
dharmarāja uvāca
śṛṇudhvaṃ madvaco dūtā hitaṃ vakṣyāmyanuttamamam /
dharmamārgaratā nmartyānmānayadhvaṃ mamāntikam //
1.23.d:
धर्मराज उवाच
शृणुध्वं मद्वचो दूता हितं वक्ष्याम्यनुत्तममम् ।
धर्ममार्गरता न्मर्त्यान्मानयध्वं ममान्तिकम् ॥
1.23.m: The King of Justice said: / ‘Listen to my words, O messengers; I shall declare what is beneficial and unexcelled: / bring mortals devoted to the path of dharma to my presence.

1.23.s:
ye viṣṇupūjanaratāḥ prayatāḥ kṛtajñāścaikādaśīvrataparā vijitendriyāśca /
nārāyaṇācyutahare śaraṇaṃ bhaveti śāntā vadanti satataṃ tarasātyajadhvam //
1.23.d:
ये विष्णुपूजनरताः प्रयताः कृतज्ञाश्चैकादशीव्रतपरा विजितेन्द्रियाश्च ।
नारायणाच्युतहरे शरणं भवेति शान्ता वदन्ति सततं तरसात्यजध्वम् ॥
1.23.m: Those who are devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu, purified, grateful, dedicated to the Ekādaśī vow, and have conquered their senses, / calm, constantly saying, “O Nārāyaṇa, O Acyuta, O Hari, be our refuge!”—release them swiftly!

1.23.s:
nārāyaṇācyuta janārdana kṛṣṇa viṣṇo padmeśa padmajapitaḥ śiva śaṅkareti /
nityaṃ vadantyakhilaloka hitāḥ praśāntā dūradbhaṭāstyajatā tānna mamaiṣu śikṣā //
1.23.d:
नारायणाच्युत जनार्दन कृष्ण विष्णो पद्मेश पद्मजपितः शिव शङ्करेति ।
नित्यं वदन्त्यखिललोक हिताः प्रशान्ता दूरद्भटास्त्यजता तान्न ममैषु शिक्षा ॥
1.23.m: Those who, peaceful and devoted to the welfare of all the world, constantly say: / “O Nārāyaṇa, Acyuta, Janārdana, Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, Lord of Padmā, Father of the lotus-born, Śiva, Śaṅkara!”— / O soldiers, release them from afar; I have no authority to punish them!

1.23.s:
nārāyaṇārpitakṛtānharibhaktibhajaḥ svācāramārganiratān gurusevakāṃśca /
satpātradāna niratāṃśca sudīnapāllāndūtāstyajadhvamaniśaṃ harināmasaktān //
1.23.d:
नारायणार्पितकृतान्हरिभक्तिभजः स्वाचारमार्गनिरतान् गुरुसेवकांश्च ।
सत्पात्रदान निरतांश्च सुदीनपाल्लान्दूतास्त्यजध्वमनिशं हरिनामसक्तान् ॥
1.23.m: Those whose actions are offered to Nārāyaṇa, who are endowed with devotion to Hari, devoted to the path of their proper conduct, servants of their gurus, / intent on giving to worthy recipients, protectors of the very distressed, and constantly attached to the name of Hari—O messengers, release them!’”

1.23.s:
pāṣaṇḍasaṅgarahitāndvijabhaktiniṣṭhānsatsaṃgalollupatarāṃśca tathātitheyān /
śaṃbhau harau ca samabuddhimatastathaiva dūtāstyajadhvamupakāraparāñjanānām //
ye varjitā harikathāmṛtasevanaiśca nārāyaṇasmṛtiparāyaṇamānasaiśca //
1.23.d:
पाषण्डसङ्गरहितान्द्विजभक्तिनिष्ठान्सत्संगलोल्लुपतरांश्च तथातिथेयान् ।
शंभौ हरौ च समबुद्धिमतस्तथैव दूतास्त्यजध्वमुपकारपराञ्जनानाम् ॥
ये वर्जिता हरिकथामृतसेवनैश्च नारायणस्मृतिपरायणमानसैश्च ॥
1.23.m:
Those free from the company of heretics, devoted to the reverence of brāhmaṇas, exceedingly eager for the company of the virtuous, hospitable to guests, / and having an equal mind toward Śambhu and Hari, and intent on helping others—messengers, leave them alone!

Those who are destitute of enjoying the nectar of tales of Hari, whose minds are never intent on remembering Nārāyaṇa,

1.23.s: virpandrapādajalasecanato 'prahṛṣṭāṃstānpāpino mama bhaṭā gṛhamānayadhvam //
1.23.d: विर्पन्द्रपादजलसेचनतो ऽप्रहृष्टांस्तान्पापिनो मम भटा गृहमानयध्वम् ॥
1.23.m: and who are not delighted by sprinkling with the water of the feet of the foremost of brāhmaṇas—my soldiers, bring those sinners to my abode!

1.23.s:
ye mātṛtātaparibhartsanaśīlinaśca lokadviṣo hitajanāhitakarmaṇaśca /
devasvalobhaniratāñjananāśakartṛānatrānayadhvamaparādhaparāṃśca dūtāḥ //
1.23.d:
ये मातृतातपरिभर्त्सनशीलिनश्च लोकद्विषो हितजनाहितकर्मणश्च ।
देवस्वलोभनिरताञ्जननाशकर्तृआनत्रानयध्वमपराधपरांश्च दूताः ॥
1.23.m: Those who are prone to reviling their mother and father, who hate people, who perform harmful deeds against beneficent people, / who are intent on coveting the property of the gods, who bring destruction to people, and who are intent on transgressions—bring them here, messengers!

1.23.s:
ekādaśīvrataparāṅmukhamugraśīlaṃ lokāpavādanirataṃ paranindakaṃ ca /
grāmasya nāśakaramuttamavairayuktaṃ dūtāḥ samānayata vipradhaneṣu lubdham //
1.23.d:
एकादशीव्रतपराङ्मुखमुग्रशीलं लोकापवादनिरतं परनिन्दकं च ।
ग्रामस्य नाशकरमुत्तमवैरयुक्तं दूताः समानयत विप्रधनेषु लुब्धम् ॥
1.23.m: One who turns away from the Ekādaśī observance, of cruel conduct, intent on speaking ill of people, a slanderer of others, / a destroyer of his village, possessed of hostility toward the virtuous, and greedy for the wealth of brāhmaṇas—messengers, bring him here!

1.23.s:
ye viṣṇubhaktivimukhāḥ praṇamanti naiva nārāyaṇaṃ hi śaraṇāgatapālakaṃ ca /
viṣṇavālayaṃ ca nahi yānti narāḥ sumūrkhāstānānayadhvamatipāparatānprasāhya //
1.23.d:
ये विष्णुभक्तिविमुखाः प्रणमन्ति नैव नारायणं हि शरणागतपालकं च ।
विष्णवालयं च नहि यान्ति नराः सुमूर्खास्तानानयध्वमतिपापरतान्प्रसाह्य ॥
1.23.m: Those who are averse to devotion to Viṣṇu, who do not bow at all to Nārāyaṇa, the protector of those who seek refuge, / and the utterly foolish men who never go to the temple of Viṣṇu—bring them by force, those who are intent on extreme sins!

1.23.s:
evaṃ śrutaṃ yadā tatra yamena paribhāṣitam /
mayānutāpadagdhena smṛtaṃ tatkarma ninditam //
1.23.d:
एवं श्रुतं यदा तत्र यमेन परिभाषितम् ।
मयानुतापदग्धेन स्मृतं तत्कर्म निन्दितम् ॥
1.23.m: When what was spoken by Yama was heard there in this way, / that reprehensible deed was remembered by me, burning with remorse.

1.23.s:
asatkarmānutāpena saddharmaśravaṇena ca /
tatraiva sarvapāpāni niḥśeṣāṇi gatāni me //
1.23.d:
असत्कर्मानुतापेन सद्धर्मश्रवणेन च ।
तत्रैव सर्वपापानि निःशेषाणि गतानि मे ॥
1.23.m: Through remorse for bad deeds and through hearing the true Dharma, / right there all my sins vanished without a trace.

1.23.s:
pāpaśeṣādvinirmuktaṃ harisārupyatāṃ gatam /
sahasrasūryasaṃkāśaṃ praṇanāma yamaśca tam //
1.23.d:
पापशेषाद्विनिर्मुक्तं हरिसारुप्यतां गतम् ।
सहस्रसूर्यसंकाशं प्रणनाम यमश्च तम् ॥
1.23.m: Freed from the remainder of sin, having attained conformity of form with Hari, / shining like a thousand suns, Yama bowed down to him.

1.23.s:
evaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitāste yamadūtā bhayotkaṭāḥ /
viśvāsaṃ paramaṃ cakruryamena paribhāṣite //
1.23.d:
एवं दृष्ट्वा विस्मितास्ते यमदूता भयोत्कटाः ।
विश्वासं परमं चक्रुर्यमेन परिभाषिते ॥
1.23.m: Seeing this, those messengers of Yama, overwhelmed with dread, were astonished; / they developed the utmost trust in what had been spoken by Yama.

1.23.s:
tataḥ saṃpūjya māṃ kālo vimānaśatasaṃkulam /
sadyaḥ saṃpreṣayāmāsa tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam //
1.23.d:
ततः संपूज्य मां कालो विमानशतसंकुलम् ।
सद्यः संप्रेषयामास तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
1.23.m: Then, having worshipped me, Kāla immediately sent me, / crowded with hundreds of celestial chariots, to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

1.23.s:
vimānakoṭibhiḥ sārddhaṃ sarvabhogasamanvitaiḥ /
karmaṇā tena viprarṣe viṣṇuloke mayoṣitam //
1.23.d:
विमानकोटिभिः सार्द्धं सर्वभोगसमन्वितैः ।
कर्मणा तेन विप्रर्षे विष्णुलोके मयोषितम् ॥
1.23.m: Along with crores of celestial chariots endowed with all enjoyments, / because of that deed, O sage among brāhmaṇas, I dwelt in the world of Viṣṇu.

1.23.s:
kalpakoṭisahasrāṇi kalpakoṭiśatāni ca /
sthitvā viṣṇupadaṃ paścādindralokamupagamam //
1.23.d:
कल्पकोटिसहस्राणि कल्पकोटिशतानि च ।
स्थित्वा विष्णुपदं पश्चादिन्द्रलोकमुपगमम् ॥
1.23.m: Having stayed in the abode of Viṣṇu for thousands of crores of kalpas / and hundreds of crores of kalpas, I subsequently went to the world of Indra.

1.23.s:
tatrāpi sarvabhogāḍhyaḥ sarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ /
tāvatkālaṃ divisthitvā tato bhūmimupāgataḥ //
1.23.d:
तत्रापि सर्वभोगाढ्यः सर्वदेवनमस्कृतः ।
तावत्कालं दिविस्थित्वा ततो भूमिमुपागतः ॥
1.23.m: There too, enriched with all enjoyments and saluted by all the gods, / having stayed in heaven for that much time, I then came to the earth.

1.23.s:
atrāpi viṣṇubhaktānāṃ jāto 'haṃ bhavatāṃ kule /
jātismaratvāḍajjānāmi sarvametanmunīśaavara //
1.23.d:
अत्रापि विष्णुभक्तानां जातो ऽहं भवतां कुले ।
जातिस्मरत्वाडज्जानामि सर्वमेतन्मुनीशअवर ॥
1.23.m: Here too, I was born into your family, devoted to Viṣṇu; / because of remembering my previous births, I know all of this, O lord of sages.

1.23.s:
tasmādviṣṇvarcanodyogaṃ karomi saha bālakaiḥ /
ekādaśīvratamidamiti na jñātavānpurā //
1.23.d:
तस्माद्विष्ण्वर्चनोद्योगं करोमि सह बालकैः ।
एकादशीव्रतमिदमिति न ज्ञातवान्पुरा ॥
1.23.m: Therefore, I make an effort to worship Viṣṇu together with the boys; / formerly I did not know that this was the Ekādaśī observance.

1.23.s:
jātismṛtiprabhāveṇa tajjñātaṃ sāṃprataṃ mayā /
atra svenāpi yatkarma kṛtaṃ tasya phalaṃ tvidam //
1.23.d:
जातिस्मृतिप्रभावेण तज्ज्ञातं सांप्रतं मया ।
अत्र स्वेनापि यत्कर्म कृतं तस्य फलं त्विदम् ॥
1.23.m: By the power of the memory of previous births, that has now been known by me; / here, even of the deed that was done by oneself, this is the fruit.

1.23.s:
ekādaśīvrataṃ bhaktyā kurvatāṃ kimuta prabho /
tasmāccariṣye viprendra śubhamekādaśīvratam //
1.23.d:
एकादशीव्रतं भक्त्या कुर्वतां किमुत प्रभो ।
तस्माच्चरिष्ये विप्रेन्द्र शुभमेकादशीव्रतम् ॥
1.23.m: How much more so, O lord, for those who perform the Ekādaśī observance with devotion! / Therefore, O foremost of brāhmaṇas, I shall undertake the auspicious Ekādaśī observance,

1.23.s:
viṣṇupūjāṃ cāharahaḥ paramasthānakāṅkṣayā /
ekādaśīvrataṃ yattu kurvanti śraddhayā narāḥ //
1.23.d:
विष्णुपूजां चाहरहः परमस्थानकाङ्क्षया ।
एकादशीव्रतं यत्तु कुर्वन्ति श्रद्धया नराः ॥
1.23.m: and the worship of Viṣṇu day by day, desiring the supreme state. / The men who perform the Ekādaśī observance with faith,

1.23.s:
teṣāṃ tu viṣṇubhavanaṃ paramānandadāyakam /
evaṃ putravacaḥ śrutvā saṃtuṣṭo gālavo muniḥ //
1.23.d:
तेषां तु विष्णुभवनं परमानन्ददायकम् ।
एवं पुत्रवचः श्रुत्वा संतुष्टो गालवो मुनिः ॥
1.23.m: for them the abode of Viṣṇu bestows supreme bliss. / Having heard his son's words in this way, the sage Gālava was gratified;

1.23.s:
avāpa paramāṃ tuṣṭiṃ manasā cātiharṣitaḥ /
majjanma saphalaṃ jātaṃ maddhaṃśaḥ pāvanīkṛtaḥ //
1.23.d:
अवाप परमां तुष्टिं मनसा चातिहर्षितः ।
मज्जन्म सफलं जातं मद्धंशः पावनीकृतः ॥
1.23.m: he attained the utmost satisfaction and was exceedingly delighted in his mind: / “My birth has become fruitful, my lineage has been purified,

1.23.s:
yatastvaṃ madagṛhe jāto viṣṇubhaktiparāyaṇaḥ /
iti saṃtuṣṭacittastu tasya putrasya karmaṇā //
1.23.d:
यतस्त्वं मदगृहे जातो विष्णुभक्तिपरायणः ।
इति संतुष्टचित्तस्तु तस्य पुत्रस्य कर्मणा ॥
1.23.m: since you have been born in my house, intent on devotion to Viṣṇu.” / Thus, with a mind gratified by the action of that son,

1.23.s:
haripūjāvidhānaṃ ca yathāvatsamabodhayat /
ityetatte muniśreṣṭha yathāvatkathitaṃ mayā /
saṃkocavistarābhyāṃ ca kimanyacchrotumicchasi //
iti śrībṛhannāradīye purāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde vratākhyāne ekādaśīvratamahimānuvarṇanaṃ nāma trayoviṃśo 'yāyaḥ
1.23.d:
हरिपूजाविधानं च यथावत्समबोधयत् ।
इत्येतत्ते मुनिश्रेष्ठ यथावत्कथितं मया ।
संकोचविस्तराभ्यां च किमन्यच्छ्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीये पुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे व्रताख्याने एकादशीव्रतमहिमानुवर्णनं नाम त्रयोविंशो ऽयायः
1.23.m:
he explained to him the procedure for worshipping Hari according to rule. / In this way, O best of sages, this has been told to you by me as it truly is, / both concisely and in detail. What else do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, named 'The Description of the Greatness of the Ekādaśī Observance' in the narrative of observances, in the first quarter of the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.24.s:
sūta uvāca
etanniśamya sanakoditamaprameyaṃ puṇyaṃ harerdinabhavaṃ nikhilottamaṃ ca /
pāpaughaśāntikaraṇaṃ vratasāramevaṃ brahmātmajaḥ punarabhāṣata harṣayuktaḥ //
1.24.d:
सूत उवाच
एतन्निशम्य सनकोदितमप्रमेयं पुण्यं हरेर्दिनभवं निखिलोत्तमं च ।
पापौघशान्तिकरणं व्रतसारमेवं ब्रह्मात्मजः पुनरभाषत हर्षयुक्तः ॥
1.24.m:
Sūta said:
Having heard this immeasurable, foremost among all merits, arising from the day of Hari, / which pacifies the flood of sins and is the essence of observances, spoken by Sanaka, the son of Brahmā, filled with joy, spoke again.

1.24.s:
nārada uvāca
kathitaṃ bhavatā sarvaṃ mune tattvārthakovida /
vratākhyānaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ yathāvaddharibhaktidam //
1.24.d:
नारद उवाच
कथितं भवता सर्वं मुने तत्त्वार्थकोविद ।
व्रताख्यानं महापुण्यं यथावद्धरिभक्तिदम् ॥
1.24.m:
Nārada said:
Everything has been spoken by you, O sage skilled in the essential truths, / the narrative of the observance of great merit, which properly bestows devotion to Hari.

1.24.s:
idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi varṇācacāravidhiṃ mune /
tathā sarvāśramācāraṃ prāyaścittavidhiṃ tathā //
1.24.d:
इदानीं श्रोतुमिच्छामि वर्णाचचारविधिं मुने ।
तथा सर्वाश्रमाचारं प्रायश्चित्तविधिं तथा ॥
1.24.m: Now I wish to hear, O sage, the rules of conduct for the classes, / and likewise the conduct of all the stages of life, and also the rules of expiation.

1.24.s:
etatsarvaṃ mahābhāga sarvatattvārthakovida /
kṛpayā parayā mahyaṃ yathāvadvaktumarhasi //
1.24.d:
एतत्सर्वं महाभाग सर्वतत्त्वार्थकोविद ।
कृपया परया मह्यं यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
1.24.m: All this, O highly fortunate one, skilled in the true meaning of all principles, / you ought to tell me properly out of supreme compassion.

1.24.s:
sanaka uvāca
śṛṇuṣva muniśārdūla yathā bhaktapriyaṅkaraḥ /
varṇāśramācāraparaiḥ pūjyate hariravyayaḥ //
1.24.d:
सनक उवाच
शृणुष्व मुनिशार्दूल यथा भक्तप्रियङ्करः ।
वर्णाश्रमाचारपरैः पूज्यते हरिरव्ययः ॥
1.24.m:
Sanaka said:
Listen, O tiger among sages, how the imperishable Hari, who is dear to his devotees, / is worshipped by those devoted to the conduct of the classes and stages of life.

1.24.s:
manvādyairuditaṃ yacca varṇāśramanibandhanam /
tatte vakṣyāmi vidhivadbhakto 'si tvamadhokṣaje //
1.24.d:
मन्वाद्यैरुदितं यच्च वर्णाश्रमनिबन्धनम् ।
तत्ते वक्ष्यामि विधिवद्भक्तो ऽसि त्वमधोक्षजे ॥
1.24.m: The treatise on the classes and stages of life that was proclaimed by Manu and others, / that I shall declare to you according to rule, since you are a devotee of Adhokṣaja.

1.24.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāścatvāra eva te /
varṇā iti samākhyātā eteṣu brāhmaṇo 'dhikaḥ //
1.24.d:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्राश्चत्वार एव ते ।
वर्णा इति समाख्याता एतेषु ब्राह्मणो ऽधिकः ॥
1.24.m: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras—these are the four / declared as the classes; among these, the brāhmaṇa is pre-eminent.

1.24.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā dvijāḥ proktāstrayastāthā /
mātṛtaścopanayanāddi jatvaṃ prāpyate tribhiḥ //
1.24.d:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्या द्विजाः प्रोक्तास्त्रयस्ताथा ।
मातृतश्चोपनयनाद्दि जत्वं प्राप्यते त्रिभिः ॥
1.24.m: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas: these three are declared twice-born; / twice-born status is obtained by the three through the mother and through the sacred thread ceremony.

1.24.s:
etairvarṇaiḥ sarvadharmāḥ kāryā varṇānurupataḥ /
svavarṇadharmatyagena pāṣaṇḍaḥ procyate budhaiḥ //
1.24.d:
एतैर्वर्णैः सर्वधर्माः कार्या वर्णानुरुपतः ।
स्ववर्णधर्मत्यगेन पाषण्डः प्रोच्यते बुधैः ॥
1.24.m: All duties should be performed by these classes according to their class; / by abandoning the duty of one's own class, one is called a heretic by the wise.

1.24.s:
svagṛhyacoditaṃ karmadvijaḥ kurvankṛtī bhavet /
anyathā patito bhūyātsarvadharmabahiṣkṛtaḥ //
1.24.d:
स्वगृह्यचोदितं कर्मद्विजः कुर्वन्कृती भवेत् ।
अन्यथा पतितो भूयात्सर्वधर्मबहिष्कृतः ॥
1.24.m: A twice-born man performing the duty enjoined by his own domestic ritual text becomes successful; / otherwise, he would become fallen, excluded from all duties.

1.24.s:
yugadharmaḥ parigāryā verṇairetairyathocitam /
deśācārāstathāgrāhyāḥ smṛtidharmāvirodhataḥ //
1.24.d:
युगधर्मः परिगार्या वेर्णैरेतैर्यथोचितम् ।
देशाचारास्तथाग्राह्याः स्मृतिधर्माविरोधतः ॥
1.24.m: The duties of the ages should be accepted appropriately by these classes; / likewise, local customs are to be adopted provided they do not conflict with the law of the Smṛtis.

1.24.s:
karmaṇā manasā vācā yatnāddharṃmaṃ samācaret /
asvargyaṃ lokavidviṣṭaṃ dharmyamapyācarennatu //
1.24.d:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा यत्नाद्धर्ंमं समाचरेत् ।
अस्वर्ग्यं लोकविद्विष्टं धर्म्यमप्याचरेन्नतु ॥
1.24.m: One should diligently practice righteousness in action, mind, and speech; / one should not practice even what is lawful if it does not lead to heaven or is hated by people.

1.24.s:
samudrayātrāsvīkāraḥ kamaṇḍaluvidhāraṇam /
dvijānāmasavarṇāsu kanyā sūpayamastathā //
1.24.d:
समुद्रयात्रास्वीकारः कमण्डलुविधारणम् ।
द्विजानामसवर्णासु कन्या सूपयमस्तथा ॥
1.24.m: Undertaking a sea voyage; carrying a water-pot; / the marriage of twice-born men with girls not of their own class;

1.24.s:
devarācca sutotpattirmadhuparke paśorvadhaḥ /
māṃsādanaṃ tathā śrāddhe vānaprasthaāśramastathā //
1.24.d:
देवराच्च सुतोत्पत्तिर्मधुपर्के पशोर्वधः ।
मांसादनं तथा श्राद्धे वानप्रस्थआश्रमस्तथा ॥
1.24.m: procreation of a son from a brother-in-law; killing an animal at the honey-mixture reception; / eating meat at an ancestral offering; likewise, the forest-hermit stage of life;

1.24.s:
dattākṣatāyāḥ kanyāyāḥ punardānaṃ varāya ca /
naiṣṭikaṃ brahmacaryaṃ ca naramedhāścamedhakau //
1.24.d:
दत्ताक्षतायाः कन्यायाः पुनर्दानं वराय च ।
नैष्टिकं ब्रह्मचर्यं च नरमेधाश्चमेधकौ ॥
1.24.m: giving again to a groom a maiden who has been betrothed; / lifelong celibacy; human sacrifice and horse sacrifice;

1.24.s:
mahāprasthānagamanaṃ gomedhaśca tathā makhaḥ /
etāndharmānkaliyuke varjyānāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ //
1.24.d:
महाप्रस्थानगमनं गोमेधश्च तथा मखः ।
एतान्धर्मान्कलियुके वर्ज्यानाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
1.24.m: setting out on the great journey [unto death]; and likewise the cow sacrifice: / the wise declare these duties to be avoided in the Kali age.

1.24.s:
deśācārāḥ parigrāhyāstattaddeśagatairnaraiḥ /
anyathā patito jñeyaḥ sarvadharmabahiṣkṛtaḥ //
1.24.d:
देशाचाराः परिग्राह्यास्तत्तद्देशगतैर्नरैः ।
अन्यथा पतितो ज्ञेयः सर्वधर्मबहिष्कृतः ॥
1.24.m: Local customs must be adopted by men residing in those respective regions; / otherwise, one is to be known as fallen, excluded from all duties.

1.24.s:
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca dvijottamā /
kriyāḥ sāmānyato vakṣye tacchṛṇuṣva samāhitaḥ //
1.24.d:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च द्विजोत्तमा ।
क्रियाः सामान्यतो वक्ष्ये तच्छृणुष्व समाहितः ॥
1.24.m: O best of the twice-born, I shall explain in general the rituals / of brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras; listen to that with an attentive mind.

1.24.s:
dānaṃ dadyārdvahmaṇebhyastathā yajñairyajetsurān /
vṛttyarthaṃ yācayeccaiva anyānadhyāpayettathā //
1.24.d:
दानं दद्यार्द्वह्मणेभ्यस्तथा यज्ञैर्यजेत्सुरान् ।
वृत्त्यर्थं याचयेच्चैव अन्यानध्यापयेत्तथा ॥
1.24.m: He should give gifts to brāhmaṇas, and worship the gods with sacrifices; / he may solicit for livelihood, and teach others.

1.24.s:
yājayedyajane yogyānvipro nityodakī bhavet /
kuryyācca vedagrahaṇaṃ tathāgreśca parigraham //
1.24.d:
याजयेद्यजने योग्यान्विप्रो नित्योदकी भवेत् ।
कुर्य्याच्च वेदग्रहणं तथाग्रेश्च परिग्रहम् ॥
1.24.m: A brāhmaṇa should officiate at sacrifices for those worthy of sacrificing, and should perform daily water ablutions; / he should undertake the study of the Vedas, and likewise the maintenance of the sacred fire.

1.24.s:
grāhyer dvye ca pārakye samabuddhirbhavettathā /
sarvalokahitaṃ kṛryānmṛduvākyamudīrayet //
1.24.d:
ग्राह्येर् द्व्ये च पारक्ये समबुद्धिर्भवेत्तथा ।
सर्वलोकहितं कृर्यान्मृदुवाक्यमुदीरयेत् ॥
1.24.m: Likewise, he should look with an equal mind upon wealth to be received and upon that belonging to another; / he should act for the welfare of all people and speak gentle words.

1.24.s:
ṛtāvabhigamaḥ patnyāṃ śasyate brāhmaṇasya vai /
na kasyāpyahitaṃ brūyādviṣṇupūjāparo bhavet //
1.24.d:
ऋतावभिगमः पत्न्यां शस्यते ब्राह्मणस्य वै ।
न कस्याप्यहितं ब्रूयाद्विष्णुपूजापरो भवेत् ॥
1.24.m: Approaching his wife during her fertile season is indeed commended for a brāhmaṇa; / he should speak ill of no one and remain intent on the worship of Viṣṇu.

1.24.s:
dadyāddānāni viprebhyaḥ kṣatriyo 'pi dvijottama /
kuryyācca vedagrahaṇaṃ yajñairddevānyajettathā //
1.24.d:
दद्याद्दानानि विप्रेभ्यः क्षत्रियो ऽपि द्विजोत्तम ।
कुर्य्याच्च वेदग्रहणं यज्ञैर्द्देवान्यजेत्तथा ॥
1.24.m: The kṣatriya too, O best of the twice-born, should give gifts to brāhmaṇas, / master the Veda, and worship the gods with sacrifices.

1.24.s:
śastrājīvī bhaveccaiva pālayeddharmato mahīm /
duṣṭānāṃ śāsanaṃ kuryyācchiṣṭānāṃ pālanaṃ tathā //
1.24.d:
शस्त्राजीवी भवेच्चैव पालयेद्धर्मतो महीम् ।
दुष्टानां शासनं कुर्य्याच्छिष्टानां पालनं तथा ॥
1.24.m: He should also earn his livelihood by weapons and protect the earth according to dharma; / he should punish the wicked and protect the virtuous.

1.24.s:
pāśupālyaṃ ca vāṇijyaṃ kṛṃṣiśca dvijasattama /
vedasyādhyayanaṃ caiva vaiśyasyāpi prakīrttitam //
1.24.d:
पाशुपाल्यं च वाणिज्यं कृंषिश्च द्विजसत्तम ।
वेदस्याध्ययनं चैव वैश्यस्यापि प्रकीर्त्तितम् ॥
1.24.m: Rearing cattle, trade, and agriculture, O best of the twice-born, / as well as the study of the Veda, are declared for the vaiśya.

1.24.s:
kuryācca dāragrahaṇaṃ dharmāścaiva samācaret /
krayavikrayajarvāpi dhanaiḥ kārukriyodbhavaiḥ //
1.24.d:
कुर्याच्च दारग्रहणं धर्माश्चैव समाचरेत् ।
क्रयविक्रयजर्वापि धनैः कारुक्रियोद्भवैः ॥
1.24.m: He should take a wife and practice virtuous deeds; / with wealth acquired from buying and selling, or originating from artisans' crafts,

1.24.s:
dadyāddānāni śūdro 'pi pākayajñairyajenna ca /
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śuśrūṣāni rato bhavet //
1.24.d:
दद्याद्दानानि शूद्रो ऽपि पाकयज्ञैर्यजेन्न च ।
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शुश्रूषानि रतो भवेत् ॥
1.24.m: even a śūdra should give gifts, but he must not offer cooked sacrifices; / he should be devoted to serving brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas.

1.24.s:
ṛtukālābhigāmīca svadāreṣu bhavettathā /
sarvalokahitoṣitvaṃ maṅgalaṃ priyavāditā //
1.24.d:
ऋतुकालाभिगामीच स्वदारेषु भवेत्तथा ।
सर्वलोकहितोषित्वं मङ्गलं प्रियवादिता ॥
1.24.m: He should also approach only his own wife during her fertile season; / dwelling on the welfare of all people, auspicious conduct, pleasant speech,

1.24.s:
anāyāso manoharṣastitikṣā nātimānitā /
sāmānyaṃ sarvavarṇānāṃ munibhiḥ parikīrtitam //
1.24.d:
अनायासो मनोहर्षस्तितिक्षा नातिमानिता ।
सामान्यं सर्ववर्णानां मुनिभिः परिकीर्तितम् ॥
1.24.m: freedom from exertion, gladness of mind, endurance, and absence of excessive pride: / this is declared by sages to be common to all classes.

1.24.s:
sarve ca munitāṃ yānti svāśramocitakarmaṇā /
brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyācāramāśrayedāpadi dvija //
1.24.d:
सर्वे च मुनितां यान्ति स्वाश्रमोचितकर्मणा ।
ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियाचारमाश्रयेदापदि द्विज ॥
1.24.m: All attain sagehood through duties proper to their own stage of life. / In times of distress, a brāhmaṇa may adopt the conduct of a kṣatriya, O twice-born one;

1.24.s:
kṣatriyo 'pi ca viḍvṛttimatyāpadi samāśrayet /
nāśrayecchūdravṛttiṃ tu atyāpadyapi vai dvijaḥ //
1.24.d:
क्षत्रियो ऽपि च विड्वृत्तिमत्यापदि समाश्रयेत् ।
नाश्रयेच्छूद्रवृत्तिं तु अत्यापद्यपि वै द्विजः ॥
1.24.m: and in extreme distress, a kṣatriya may resort to the livelihood of a vaiśya; / but even in extreme distress, a twice-born man should never adopt the livelihood of a śūdra.

1.24.s:
yadyāśrayeddijo mūḍhastadā cāṇḍāsatāṃ vrajet /
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ trayāṇāṃ munisattama //
1.24.d:
यद्याश्रयेद्दिजो मूढस्तदा चाण्डासतां व्रजेत् ।
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां त्रयाणां मुनिसत्तम ॥
1.24.m: If a deluded twice-born man should adopt it, he would become a cāṇḍāla. / For the three classes—brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, and vaiśya—O best of sages,

1.24.s:
catvāra āśramāḥ proktāḥ pañcamo nopapadyate /
brahmacārī gṛhī vānaprastho bhikṣuśca sattama //
1.24.d:
चत्वार आश्रमाः प्रोक्ताः पञ्चमो नोपपद्यते ।
ब्रह्मचारी गृही वानप्रस्थो भिक्षुश्च सत्तम ॥
1.24.m: four stages of life are proclaimed; a fifth is impossible: / the student, the householder, the forest-dweller, and the mendicant, O virtuous one.

1.24.s:
caturbhirāśramairebhiḥ sādhyate dharma uttamaḥ /
viṣṇustuṣyati viprendra karmayogaratātmanaḥ //
1.24.d:
चतुर्भिराश्रमैरेभिः साध्यते धर्म उत्तमः ।
विष्णुस्तुष्यति विप्रेन्द्र कर्मयोगरतात्मनः ॥
1.24.m: Through these four stages of life, the highest dharma is achieved. / Viṣṇu is pleased, O lord of brāhmaṇas, with one whose self is intent on karmayoga,

1.24.s:
niḥspṛhāśāntamanasaḥ svakarmaniratasya ca /
tato yāti paraṃ sthānaṃ yato nāvarttate punaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannārāyaṇapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde sadācāro nāma caturviśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.24.d:
निःस्पृहाशान्तमनसः स्वकर्मनिरतस्य च ।
ततो याति परं स्थानं यतो नावर्त्तते पुनः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारायणपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे सदाचारो नाम चतुर्विशो ऽध्यायः
1.24.m:
who is desireless, whose mind is tranquil, and who is devoted to his own duty; / thence he goes to the supreme state from which he does not return again.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, entitled 'Virtuous Conduct', in the first quarter of the Pūrvabhāga of the illustrious Bṛhannārāyaṇa Purāṇa.

1.25.s:
sanaka uvāca
varṇāśramācāravidhiṃ pravakṣyāmi viśeṣataḥ /
śṛṇuṣva tanmuniśreṣṭha sāvadhānena cetasā //
1.25.d:
सनक उवाच
वर्णाश्रमाचारविधिं प्रवक्ष्यामि विशेषतः ।
शृणुष्व तन्मुनिश्रेष्ठ सावधानेन चेतसा ॥
1.25.m: Sanaka said: / I shall explain in detail the rules of conduct for the classes and stages of life; / listen to that, O best of sages, with an attentive mind.

1.25.s:
yaḥ svadharmaṃ parityajya paradharmaṃ samācaret /
pāṣaṇḍaḥ sa hi vijñeyaḥ sarvadharmabahiṣkṛtaḥ //
1.25.d:
यः स्वधर्मं परित्यज्य परधर्मं समाचरेत् ।
पाषण्डः स हि विज्ञेयः सर्वधर्मबहिष्कृतः ॥
1.25.m: He who abandons his own duty and performs the duty of another / is known as a heretic, excluded from all dharmas.

1.25.s:
garbhādhānādisaṃskārāḥ kāryā mantravidhānataḥ /
strīṇāmamantrataḥ kāryā yathākālaṃ yathāvidhi //
1.25.d:
गर्भाधानादिसंस्काराः कार्या मन्त्रविधानतः ।
स्त्रीणाममन्त्रतः कार्या यथाकालं यथाविधि ॥
1.25.m: The rites of passage, beginning with conception, must be performed according to the injunctions of the mantras; / for women, they must be performed without mantras, at the proper time and according to rule.

1.25.s:
sīmantakarma prathamaṃ caturthe māsi śasyate /
ṣaṣṭe vā satpame vāpi aṣṭame vāpi kārayet //
1.25.d:
सीमन्तकर्म प्रथमं चतुर्थे मासि शस्यते ।
षष्टे वा सत्पमे वापि अष्टमे वापि कारयेत् ॥
1.25.m: The rite of parting the hair is first commended in the fourth month; / or one should have it performed in the sixth, or the seventh, or even the eighth month.

1.25.s:
jāte putre pitā snātvā sacailaṃ jātakarma ca /
kuryyācca nāndīśrāddhaṃ ca svastivācanapūrvakam //
1.25.d:
जाते पुत्रे पिता स्नात्वा सचैलं जातकर्म च ।
कुर्य्याच्च नान्दीश्राद्धं च स्वस्तिवाचनपूर्वकम् ॥
1.25.m: When a son is born, the father, having bathed with his clothes on, should perform the birth rite, / and also perform the nāndīśrāddha preceded by the recitation of blessings.

1.25.s:
hemnā vā rajatenāpi vṛddhiśrāddhaṃ prakalpayet /
annena kārayedyastu sa caṇḍāla samo bhavet //
1.25.d:
हेम्ना वा रजतेनापि वृद्धिश्राद्धं प्रकल्पयेत् ।
अन्नेन कारयेद्यस्तु स चण्डाल समो भवेत् ॥
1.25.m: He should arrange the vṛddhiśrāddha with gold or with silver; / but he who has it performed with cooked food becomes equal to a caṇḍāla.

1.25.s:
kṛtvābhyudayikaṃ śrāddhaṃ pitā putraghasya vāgyataḥ /
kurvīta nāmanirddeśaṃ sūtakānte yathāvidhi //
1.25.d:
कृत्वाभ्युदयिकं श्राद्धं पिता पुत्रघस्य वाग्यतः ।
कुर्वीत नामनिर्द्देशं सूतकान्ते यथाविधि ॥
1.25.m: Having performed the auspicious śrāddha, restrained in speech, the father of the son / should duly perform the naming rite at the end of the period of birth-impurity.

1.25.s:
aspaṣṭamarthahīnaṃ ca hyatigurva kṣarānvitam /
na dadyānnāma viprenda tathā ca viṣathamākṣaram //
1.25.d:
अस्पष्टमर्थहीनं च ह्यतिगुर्व क्षरान्वितम् ।
न दद्यान्नाम विप्रेन्द तथा च विषथमाक्षरम् ॥
1.25.m: One should not give a name that is unclear, devoid of meaning, containing excessively heavy syllables, / or with an uneven number of syllables, O lord of brāhmaṇas.

1.25.s:
tṛtīyavarṣe caulaṃ ca pañcame ṣaṣṭasaṃmite /
satpame cāṣṭame vāpi kuryād gṛhyoktamārgataḥ //
1.25.d:
तृतीयवर्षे चौलं च पञ्चमे षष्टसंमिते ।
सत्पमे चाष्टमे वापि कुर्याद् गृह्योक्तमार्गतः ॥
1.25.m: In the third year, or in the fifth, sixth, / seventh, or eighth year, he should perform the tonsure according to the path taught in the Gṛhyasūtras.

1.25.s:
daivayogādatikrānte garbhādhānādikarmaṇi /
kartavyaḥ pādakṛcchro vai caule tvarddhaṃ prakalpayet //
1.25.d:
दैवयोगादतिक्रान्ते गर्भाधानादिकर्मणि ।
कर्तव्यः पादकृच्छ्रो वै चौले त्वर्द्धं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
1.25.m: If by chance the rite beginning with conception is missed, / a quarter-kṛcchra penance must be performed; for the tonsure, one should assign half.

1.25.s:
garbhāṣṭame 'ṣṭame vābde baṭukasyopanāyanam /
āṣoḍaśābdaparyantaṃ gauṇaṃ kālamuśanti ca //
1.25.d:
गर्भाष्टमे ऽष्टमे वाब्दे बटुकस्योपनायनम् ।
आषोडशाब्दपर्यन्तं गौणं कालमुशन्ति च ॥
1.25.m: The initiation of a boy should be performed in the eighth year from conception, or the eighth year [from birth]; / they desire the secondary time up to the sixteenth year.

1.25.s:
garbhaikādaśame 'bde tu rājanyasyopanāyanam /
ādvāviṃśābdaparyantaṃ kālamāhurvipaścitaḥ //
1.25.d:
गर्भैकादशमे ऽब्दे तु राजन्यस्योपनायनम् ।
आद्वाविंशाब्दपर्यन्तं कालमाहुर्विपश्चितः ॥
1.25.m: The initiation of a kṣatriya is in the eleventh year from conception; / the wise declare the time [extends] up to the twenty-second year.

1.25.s:
vaiśvopanayanaṃ proktaṃ garbhāddvādaśame tathā /
caturviṃśābdaparyantaṃ gauṇamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ //
1.25.d:
वैश्वोपनयनं प्रोक्तं गर्भाद्द्वादशमे तथा ।
चतुर्विंशाब्दपर्यन्तं गौणमाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
1.25.m: The initiation of a vaiśya is declared likewise in the twelfth year from conception; / the wise state the secondary time [extends] up to the twenty-fourth year.

1.25.s:
etatkālāvadheryasya dvijasyātikramo bhavet /
sāvitrīpatitaṃ vidyāttaṃ tu naivālapetkadā //
1.25.d:
एतत्कालावधेर्यस्य द्विजस्यातिक्रमो भवेत् ।
सावित्रीपतितं विद्यात्तं तु नैवालपेत्कदा ॥
1.25.m: If a twice-born man exceeds this time limit, / one should know him as fallen from the Sāvitrī; one should never even converse with him.

1.25.s:
dvijopanayane vipra mukhyakālavyatikrame /
dvādaśābdaṃ caretkṛcchraṃ paścājcāndrāyaṇaṃ tathā /
sāṃtapanadvayaṃ caiva kṛtvā karma samācaret //
1.25.d:
द्विजोपनयने विप्र मुख्यकालव्यतिक्रमे ।
द्वादशाब्दं चरेत्कृच्छ्रं पश्चाज्चान्द्रायणं तथा ।
सांतपनद्वयं चैव कृत्वा कर्म समाचरेत् ॥
1.25.m: When the primary time for the twice-born initiation has passed, O brāhmaṇa, / one should perform a kṛcchra penance for twelve years, and then a cāndrāyaṇa penance, / and having performed two sāṃtapana penances, he may perform the rite.

1.25.s:
anyathaā patitaṃ vidyātkarttāpi brahmahā bhavet /
rmauñjī viprasya vijñeyā dhanurjyā kṣattriyasya tu //
1.25.d:
अन्यथआ पतितं विद्यात्कर्त्तापि ब्रह्महा भवेत् ।
र्मौञ्जी विप्रस्य विज्ञेया धनुर्ज्या क्षत्त्रियस्य तु ॥
1.25.m: Otherwise, one should know him as fallen, and the performer also becomes a slayer of a brāhmaṇa. / The girdle is known to be of muñja grass for a brāhmaṇa, but a bowstring for a kṣatriya;

1.25.s:
āvī vaiśyasya vijñeyā śrūyatāmajine tathā /
viprasya coktamaiṇeyaṃ rauravaṃ kṣatriyasya tu //
1.25.d:
आवी वैश्यस्य विज्ञेया श्रूयतामजिने तथा ।
विप्रस्य चोक्तमैणेयं रौरवं क्षत्रियस्य तु ॥
1.25.m: it is known to be of wool for a vaiśya; hear likewise about the deerskin: / an antelope skin is spoken of for a brāhmaṇa, and a ruru deer skin for a kṣatriya;

1.25.s:
ājaṃ veśyasya vijñeyaṃ daṇḍānvakṣye yathākramam /
pālāśaṃ brāhmaṇasyoktaṃ nṛpasyaudumbaraṃ tathā //
1.25.d:
आजं वेश्यस्य विज्ञेयं दण्डान्वक्ष्ये यथाक्रमम् ।
पालाशं ब्राह्मणस्योक्तं नृपस्यौदुम्बरं तथा ॥
1.25.m: a goat skin is known for a vaiśya. I shall declare the staffs in due order: / a palāśa staff is declared for a brāhmaṇa, and an udumbara staff for a king;

1.25.s:
bailvaṃ vaiśyasya vijñeya tatpramāṇaṃ śṛṇuṣva me /
viprasya keśamānaṃ syādālalāṭaṃ nṛpasya ca //
1.25.d:
बैल्वं वैश्यस्य विज्ञेय तत्प्रमाणं शृणुष्व मे ।
विप्रस्य केशमानं स्यादाललाटं नृपस्य च ॥
1.25.m: a bilva staff is known for a vaiśya. Hear from me their measurements: / for a brāhmaṇa it should measure up to the hair; for a king, up to the forehead;

1.25.s:
nāsāgrasaṃmitaṃ daṇḍaṃ vaiśyasyāhurvipaścitaḥ /
tathā vāsāṃsi vakṣaghyāmi viprādīnāṃ yathākramam //
1.25.d:
नासाग्रसंमितं दण्डं वैश्यस्याहुर्विपश्चितः ।
तथा वासांसि वक्षघ्यामि विप्रादीनां यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.25.m: the wise state the staff of a vaiśya to reach the tip of the nose. / Likewise, I shall declare the garments of the brāhmaṇa and others in due order:

1.25.s:
kaṣāyaṃ caiva māñjiṣṭaṃ hāridraṃ ca prakīrtitam /
upanīto dvijo vipra paricaryāparo guroḥ //
1.25.d:
कषायं चैव माञ्जिष्टं हारिद्रं च प्रकीर्तितम् ।
उपनीतो द्विजो विप्र परिचर्यापरो गुरोः ॥
1.25.m: they are proclaimed to be dyed reddish, madder-dyed, and turmeric-dyed. / The initiated twice-born man, O brāhmaṇa, should be devoted to serving his guru;

1.25.s:
vedagrahaṇaparyantaṃ nivasedguruveśmani /
prātaḥ snāyī bhavedvarṇī samitkuśaphalādikān //
1.25.d:
वेदग्रहणपर्यन्तं निवसेद्गुरुवेश्मनि ।
प्रातः स्नायी भवेद्वर्णी समित्कुशफलादिकान् ॥
1.25.m: he should reside in the house of the guru until the completion of his study of the Veda. / The religious student should bathe in the morning; sacrificial sticks, kuśa grass, fruits, and the like,

1.25.s:
gurvarthamāharennityaṃ kalye kalye munīśvara /
yajñopavītamajinaṃ daṇḍaṃ ca munisattama //
1.25.d:
गुर्वर्थमाहरेन्नित्यं कल्ये कल्ये मुनीश्वर ।
यज्ञोपवीतमजिनं दण्डं च मुनिसत्तम ॥
1.25.m: he should fetch daily for the sake of the guru, every morning, O lord of sages. / The sacred thread, the skin, and the staff, O best of sages,

1.25.s:
naṣṭe bhraṣṭe navaṃ mantrāddhṛtvā bhraṣṭaṃ jale kṣipet /
varṇino varttanaṃ prāhurbhikṣānnenaiva kevalam //
1.25.d:
नष्टे भ्रष्टे नवं मन्त्राद्धृत्वा भ्रष्टं जले क्षिपेत् ।
वर्णिनो वर्त्तनं प्राहुर्भिक्षान्नेनैव केवलम् ॥
1.25.m: when destroyed or fallen away, he should throw the fallen one into water and put on a new one with mantras. / They declare the livelihood of a religious student to consist solely of alms-food.

1.25.s:
bhikṣā ca śrotriyāgārādāharetprayatendriyaḥ /
bhavatpūrvaṃ brāhmaṇasya bhavanmadhyaṃ nṛpasya ca //
1.25.d:
भिक्षा च श्रोत्रियागारादाहरेत्प्रयतेन्द्रियः ।
भवत्पूर्वं ब्राह्मणस्य भवन्मध्यं नृपस्य च ॥
1.25.m: With senses controlled, he should fetch alms from the house of a Vedic scholar: / with the word 'bhavat' placed first for a brāhmaṇa, in the middle for a king,

1.25.s:
bhavadatyaṃ viśaḥ proktaṃ bhikṣāharaṇakaṃ vacaḥ /
sāṃyaprātarvahnikāryaṃ yathācāraṃ jitendriyaḥ //
1.25.d:
भवदत्यं विशः प्रोक्तं भिक्षाहरणकं वचः ।
सांयप्रातर्वह्निकार्यं यथाचारं जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.25.m: and at the end for a vaiśya, is declared the formula for begging alms. / Morning and evening, with subdued senses, according to proper conduct,

1.25.s:
kuryātpratidinaṃ varṇīṃ brahmayajñaṃ ca tarpaṇam /
agnikāryaparityāgī patitaḥ procyate budhaiḥ //
1.25.d:
कुर्यात्प्रतिदिनं वर्णीं ब्रह्मयज्ञं च तर्पणम् ।
अग्निकार्यपरित्यागी पतितः प्रोच्यते बुधैः ॥
1.25.m: the religious student should daily perform the fire-ritual, the brahmayajña, and libations. / One who abandons the fire-ritual is called an outcaste by the wise,

1.25.s:
brahmayajñavihīnaśca brahmahā parikīrtitaḥ /
devatābhyarccanaṃ kuryācchuśrūṣānupadaṃ guroḥ //
1.25.d:
ब्रह्मयज्ञविहीनश्च ब्रह्महा परिकीर्तितः ।
देवताभ्यर्च्चनं कुर्याच्छुश्रूषानुपदं गुरोः ॥
1.25.m: and one destitute of the brahmayajña is declared to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa. / He should worship the deities and follow immediately behind the guru in service.

1.25.s:
bhikṣānnaṃ bhojayennityaṃ naikānnāśī kadācana /
ānīyānindyaviprāṇāṃ gṛhādbhikṣāṃ jitendriyaḥ //
1.25.d:
भिक्षान्नं भोजयेन्नित्यं नैकान्नाशी कदाचन ।
आनीयानिन्द्यविप्राणां गृहाद्भिक्षां जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.25.m: He should always eat alms-food, never eating from a single person's food. / Having brought alms with senses controlled from the houses of blameless brāhmaṇas,

1.25.s:
nivedya gurave 'śrīyādvāgyatastadanughajñayā /
madhustrīmāṃsalavaṇaṃ tāmbūlaṃ dantadhāvanam //
1.25.d:
निवेद्य गुरवे ऽश्रीयाद्वाग्यतस्तदनुघज्ञया ।
मधुस्त्रीमांसलवणं ताम्बूलं दन्तधावनम् ॥
1.25.m: and offered it to the guru, he should eat, silent, with his permission. / Honey, women, meat, salt, betel, brushing the teeth with twigs,

1.25.s:
ucchiṣṭabhojanaṃ caiva divāsvāpaṃ ca varjayet /
chātraghapāduka gandhāṃśca tathā mālyānulepanam //
1.25.d:
उच्छिष्टभोजनं चैव दिवास्वापं च वर्जयेत् ।
छात्रघपादुक गन्धांश्च तथा माल्यानुलेपनम् ॥
1.25.m: eating food remnants, and sleeping by day he must avoid, / as well as an umbrella, shoes, perfumes, garlands, and unguents.

1.25.s:
jalakeliṃ nṛtyagītavādyaṃ tu parivarjayet /
parivādaṃ copatāpaṃ vipralāpaṃ tathāñjanam //
1.25.d:
जलकेलिं नृत्यगीतवाद्यं तु परिवर्जयेत् ।
परिवादं चोपतापं विप्रलापं तथाञ्जनम् ॥
1.25.m: He should completely avoid water sports, dancing, singing, and playing musical instruments, / as well as slander, causing distress to others, idle prattle, and collyrium.

1.25.s:
pāṣaṇḍa janasaṃyogaṃ śūdrasaṃgaṃ ca varjayet /
abhivādanaśīlaḥ syād vṛddheṣu ca yathākramam //
1.25.d:
पाषण्ड जनसंयोगं शूद्रसंगं च वर्जयेत् ।
अभिवादनशीलः स्याद् वृद्धेषु च यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.25.m: He should avoid association with heretics and company with Śūdras. / He should be in the habit of saluting elders in due order.

1.25.s:
jñānavṛddhāstapovṛddhā vayovṛddhā iti trayaḥ /
ādhyātmikā diduḥkhāni nivārayati yo guruḥ //
1.25.d:
ज्ञानवृद्धास्तपोवृद्धा वयोवृद्धा इति त्रयः ।
आध्यात्मिका दिदुःखानि निवारयति यो गुरुः ॥
1.25.m: There are three kinds [of elders]: those advanced in knowledge, those advanced in austerities, and those advanced in age. / The guru who removes sorrows such as those pertaining to the self—

1.25.s:
vedaśāstropadeśena taṃ pūrvamabhivādayet /
asāvahamiti brūyāddijo vai hyabhivādane //
1.25.d:
वेदशास्त्रोपदेशेन तं पूर्वमभिवादयेत् ।
असावहमिति ब्रूयाद्दिजो वै ह्यभिवादने ॥
1.25.m: one should salute him first through instruction in the Vedas and Śāstras. / In making a salutation, a twice-born should indeed say, 'I am so-and-so.'

1.25.s:
nābhivādyāśca vipreṇa kṣaghatriyādyāḥ kathañcana /
nāstikaṃ bhinnamaryādaṃ kṛtanghaṃ grāmayājakam //
1.25.d:
नाभिवाद्याश्च विप्रेण क्षघत्रियाद्याः कथञ्चन ।
नास्तिकं भिन्नमर्यादं कृतन्घं ग्रामयाजकम् ॥
1.25.m: Kṣatriyas and others should under no circumstances be saluted by a brāhmaṇa. / An atheist, a violator of proper conduct, an ungrateful person, a village priest,

1.25.s:
stenaṃ ca kitavaṃ caiva kadācinnābhivādayet /
pāṣaṇḍaṃ patitaṃ vrātyaṃ tathā nakṣaghatrajīvinam //
1.25.d:
स्तेनं च कितवं चैव कदाचिन्नाभिवादयेत् ।
पाषण्डं पतितं व्रात्यं तथा नक्षघत्रजीविनम् ॥
1.25.m: a thief, and a gambler should never be saluted; / [nor] a heretic, an outcaste, an apostate, or an astrologer.

1.25.s:
tathā pātakinaṃ caiva kadācinnābhivādayet /
unmattaṃ ca śaṭhaṃ dhūrttaṃ dhāvantamaśuciṃ tathā //
1.25.d:
तथा पातकिनं चैव कदाचिन्नाभिवादयेत् ।
उन्मत्तं च शठं धूर्त्तं धावन्तमशुचिं तथा ॥
1.25.m: Likewise, a sinner should never be saluted; / nor one who is mad, deceitful, wicked, running, or impure,

1.25.s:
abhyaktaśirasaṃ caiva japantaṃ nābhivādayet /
vivādaśīlinaṃ cañjaṃ vamantaṃ jalamadhyagam //
1.25.d:
अभ्यक्तशिरसं चैव जपन्तं नाभिवादयेत् ।
विवादशीलिनं चञ्जं वमन्तं जलमध्यगम् ॥
1.25.m: nor one whose head is anointed with oil, nor one engaged in japa should he salute; / nor one who is quarrelsome, lame, vomiting, or standing in water,

1.25.s:
bhikṣānnadhāriṇaṃ caiva śayānaṃ nābhivādayet /
bhartṛnghīṃ puṣpiṇīṃ jārāṃ sūtikāṃ garbhapātinīm //
1.25.d:
भिक्षान्नधारिणं चैव शयानं नाभिवादयेत् ।
भर्तृन्घीं पुष्पिणीं जारां सूतिकां गर्भपातिनीम् ॥
1.25.m: nor one carrying alms-food, nor one lying down should he salute; / nor a woman who kills her husband, one who is menstruating, an adulteress, one recently delivered of a child, one who procures abortion,

1.25.s:
kṛtanghīṃ ca tathā caṇḍīṃ kadācinnābhivādayet /
sabhāyāṃ yajñaśālāyāṃ devatāyataneṣvapi //
1.25.d:
कृतन्घीं च तथा चण्डीं कदाचिन्नाभिवादयेत् ।
सभायां यज्ञशालायां देवतायतनेष्वपि ॥
1.25.m: an ungrateful woman, or a fierce woman should he ever salute. / In an assembly, in a sacrificial hall, and even in temples of deities,

1.25.s:
pratyekaṃ tu namaskāro hṝnti puṇyaṃ purākṛtam /
śrāddhaṃ vrataṃ tathā dānaṃ devatābhyārcanaṃ tathā //
1.25.d:
प्रत्येकं तु नमस्कारो हॄन्ति पुण्यं पुराकृतम् ।
श्राद्धं व्रतं तथा दानं देवताभ्यार्चनं तथा ॥
1.25.m: individual obeisance destroys formerly accumulated merit. / A śrāddha, a vow, a gift, the worship of deities,

1.25.s:
yajñaṃ ca tarpaṇaṃ caiva kurvantaṃ nābhivādayet /
kṛte 'bhivādane yastu na kuryā tprativādanam //
1.25.d:
यज्ञं च तर्पणं चैव कुर्वन्तं नाभिवादयेत् ।
कृते ऽभिवादने यस्तु न कुर्या त्प्रतिवादनम् ॥
1.25.m: a sacrifice, and a libation—one performing [any of these] he should not salute. / But he who, when saluted, does not return the greeting,

1.25.s:
nābhivādyaḥ sa vijñeyo yayā śūdrastathaiva saḥ /
prakṣālya pādāvācamya gurorabhimukhaḥ sadā //
1.25.d:
नाभिवाद्यः स विज्ञेयो यया शूद्रस्तथैव सः ।
प्रक्षाल्य पादावाचम्य गुरोरभिमुखः सदा ॥
1.25.m: is to be regarded as unworthy of salutation; he is just like a Śūdra. / Having washed both feet and sipped water, constantly facing the guru,

1.25.s:
tasya pādau ca saṃgṛhya adhīyīta vicakṣaṇaḥ /
aṣṭakāsu caturdaśyāṃ pratipatparvaṇostathā //
1.25.d:
तस्य पादौ च संगृह्य अधीयीत विचक्षणः ।
अष्टकासु चतुर्दश्यां प्रतिपत्पर्वणोस्तथा ॥
1.25.m: and grasping both of his feet, the wise man should study. / On the Aṣṭakās, on the fourteenth [day], on the first day of a fortnight, and on the junction days;

1.25.s:
mahābharaṇyāṃ vipredraṃ śravaṇadvādaśīdine /
bhādrapadāparapakṣe dvitīyāyāṃ tathaiva ca //
1.25.d:
महाभरण्यां विप्रेद्रं श्रवणद्वादशीदिने ।
भाद्रपदापरपक्षे द्वितीयायां तथैव च ॥
1.25.m: on Mahābharaṇī, O best of twice-borns, on the day of Śravaṇadvādaśī, / on the second day in the dark fortnight of Bhādrapada;

1.25.s:
māghasya śuklasatpamyāṃ navamyāmāśrinasya ca /
pariveṣaṃ gate sūrye śrotriye gṛhamāgate //
1.25.d:
माघस्य शुक्लसत्पम्यां नवम्यामाश्रिनस्य च ।
परिवेषं गते सूर्ये श्रोत्रिये गृहमागते ॥
1.25.m: on the seventh day of the bright fortnight of Māgha, on the ninth of Āśvina; / when the sun has entered a halo; when a Vedic scholar has arrived at the house;

1.25.s:
bandhite brahmaṇe caiva pravṛddhakalahe tathā /
saṃdhyāyāṃ garjite meghe hyakāle parivarṣaṇe //
1.25.d:
बन्धिते ब्रह्मणे चैव प्रवृद्धकलहे तथा ।
संध्यायां गर्जिते मेघे ह्यकाले परिवर्षणे ॥
1.25.m: when a brāhmaṇa is bound; when a dispute has broken out; / at twilight; when a cloud thunders; during unseasonal rain;

1.25.s:
ulkāśaniprapāte ca tathā vipre 'vamānite /
manvādiṣu ca devarṣe yugādiṣu caturṣvapi //
1.25.d:
उल्काशनिप्रपाते च तथा विप्रे ऽवमानिते ।
मन्वादिषु च देवर्षे युगादिषु चतुर्ष्वपि ॥
1.25.m: during the fall of a meteor or lightning; when a brāhmaṇa is insulted; / and on the Manvādi days, O divine sage, as well as on all four Yugādi days—

1.25.s:
nādhīyīta dvijaḥ kaścitsarvakarmaphalotsukaḥ /
tṛtīyā prādhave śuklā bhādre kṛṣṇā traghayodaśī //
1.25.d:
नाधीयीत द्विजः कश्चित्सर्वकर्मफलोत्सुकः ।
तृतीया प्राधवे शुक्ला भाद्रे कृष्णा त्रघयोदशी ॥
1.25.m: no twice-born who desires the fruits of all rites should study. / The third day of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, the thirteenth of the dark fortnight of Bhādrapada,

1.25.s:
kārttike navamī śuddhā māghe pañcadaśī tithiḥ /
etā yugādyāḥ kathitā dattasyākṣayakārikāḥ //
1.25.d:
कार्त्तिके नवमी शुद्धा माघे पञ्चदशी तिथिः ।
एता युगाद्याः कथिता दत्तस्याक्षयकारिकाः ॥
1.25.m: the pure ninth of Kārttika, the fifteenth lunar day of Māgha— / these are declared to be the Yugādi days, rendering gifts imperishable.

1.25.s:
manvādīṃśca pravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣva susamāhitaḥ /
akṣayukchuklanavamī kārtike dvādaśī sitā //
1.25.d:
मन्वादींश्च प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्व सुसमाहितः ।
अक्षयुक्छुक्लनवमी कार्तिके द्वादशी सिता ॥
1.25.m: And I shall proclaim the Manvādi days; listen with a composed mind: / the ninth of the bright fortnight of Āśvina, the twelfth of the bright fortnight of Kārttika,

1.25.s:
tṛtīyā caighatramāsasya tathā bhādrapadasya ca /
āṣāḍhaśukladaśamī sitā māghasya satpamī //
1.25.d:
तृतीया चैघत्रमासस्य तथा भाद्रपदस्य च ।
आषाढशुक्लदशमी सिता माघस्य सत्पमी ॥
1.25.m: the third of Caitra and likewise of Bhādrapada, / the tenth of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, the seventh of the bright fortnight of Māgha,

1.25.s:
śrāvaṇasyāṣṭamī kṛṣṇā tathāṣāḍhī ca pūrṇamā /
phaālgunasya tvamāvāsyā pauṣasyaikādaśī sitā //
1.25.d:
श्रावणस्याष्टमी कृष्णा तथाषाढी च पूर्णमा ।
फआल्गुनस्य त्वमावास्या पौषस्यैकादशी सिता ॥
1.25.m: the eighth of the dark fortnight of Śrāvaṇa, the full moon of Āṣāḍha, / the new moon of Phālguna, the eleventh of the bright fortnight of Pauṣa,

1.25.s:
kārtikī phaālgunī caighatrīṃ jyaiṣṭhī pañcadaśī sitā /
manvādayaḥ samākhyātā dattasyākṣayakārikāḥ //
1.25.d:
कार्तिकी फआल्गुनी चैघत्रीं ज्यैष्ठी पञ्चदशी सिता ।
मन्वादयः समाख्याता दत्तस्याक्षयकारिकाः ॥
1.25.m: the full moon of Kārttika, Phālguna, Caitra, and the fifteenth [day] of the bright fortnight of Jyaiṣṭha: / [these] are proclaimed to be the Manvādi days, rendering gifts imperishable.

1.25.s:
dvijaiḥ śraddhaṃ cakarttavyaṃ manvādiṣu yugādiṣu /
śrāddhe nimantrite caivagrahaṇe candrasūryayoḥ //
1.25.d:
द्विजैः श्रद्धं चकर्त्तव्यं मन्वादिषु युगादिषु ।
श्राद्धे निमन्त्रिते चैवग्रहणे चन्द्रसूर्ययोः ॥
1.25.m: Śrāddha should be performed by twice-borns on the Manvādi and Yugādi days. / When one is invited to a śrāddha, during an eclipse of the moon or the sun,

1.25.s:
ayanadvitaye caiva tathā bhūkaṃpane mune /
galagrahe durddine ca nādhīyīta kadācanā //
1.25.d:
अयनद्वितये चैव तथा भूकंपने मुने ।
गलग्रहे दुर्द्दिने च नाधीयीत कदाचना ॥
1.25.m: at the two solstices, during an earthquake, O sage, / during Galagraha days, and on a foul day, one should never study.

1.25.s:
evamādiṣu sarveṣu anadhyāyeṣu nārada /
adhīyatāṃ sumūḍhānāṃprajāṃprajñāṃyaśaḥ śriyam //
1.25.d:
एवमादिषु सर्वेषु अनध्यायेषु नारद ।
अधीयतां सुमूढानांप्रजांप्रज्ञांयशः श्रियम् ॥
1.25.m: On all such occasions forbidden for study, O Nārada, / of those fools who study, the offspring, intellect, fame, wealth,

1.25.s:
āyuṣyaṃ balamārogyaṃ nikṛntati yamaḥ svayam /
anadhyāye tu yo 'dhīte taṃ vidyādvrahmaghātakam //
1.25.d:
आयुष्यं बलमारोग्यं निकृन्तति यमः स्वयम् ।
अनध्याये तु यो ऽधीते तं विद्याद्व्रह्मघातकम् ॥
1.25.m: lifespan, strength, and health are cut down by Yama himself. / But he who studies on an occasion forbidden for study—one should know him as a slayer of Brahman.

1.25.s:
na taṃ saṃbhāṣayedviprana tena saha saṃvaset /
kuṇḍagolakayoḥ kecijjaḍādīnāṃ ca nārada //
1.25.d:
न तं संभाषयेद्विप्रन तेन सह संवसेत् ।
कुण्डगोलकयोः केचिज्जडादीनां च नारद ॥
1.25.m: A twice-born should not converse with him, nor should he reside with him. / Some say that the investiture of the sacred thread of a kuṇḍa and a golaka, and of the dull-witted and the like, O Nārada,

1.25.s:
vadanti copanayanaṃ tatputrādiṣu kecana /
anadhītya tu yo vedamanyatra kurute śramam //
1.25.d:
वदन्ति चोपनयनं तत्पुत्रादिषु केचन ।
अनधीत्य तु यो वेदमन्यत्र कुरुते श्रमम् ॥
1.25.m: belongs to their sons and others. / But he who, without having studied the Veda, exerts effort elsewhere,

1.25.s:
śūdratulyaḥ sa vijñeyo narakasya priyo 'tithiḥ /
anadhītaśrutirvipra ācāra pratipadyate //
1.25.d:
शूद्रतुल्यः स विज्ञेयो नरकस्य प्रियो ऽतिथिः ।
अनधीतश्रुतिर्विप्र आचार प्रतिपद्यते ॥
1.25.m: is to be regarded as equal to a Śūdra, a dear guest of hell. / A twice-born who has not studied the sacred revelation, [though] he undertakes proper conduct,

1.25.s:
nācāraphalamānpoti yathā śūdrastathaiva saḥ /
nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyaṃ yaccānyatkarma vaidikam //
1.25.d:
नाचारफलमान्पोति यथा शूद्रस्तथैव सः ।
नित्यं नैमित्तिकं काम्यं यच्चान्यत्कर्म वैदिकम् ॥
1.25.m: does not obtain the fruit of proper conduct; he is just like a Śūdra. / Daily, occasional, and optional [rites], and whatever other Vedic rite there is—

1.25.s:
anadhītasya viprasya sarvaṃ bhavati niṣphalam /
śabdabrahmamayo viṣṇurvedaḥ sākṣāddhāri smṛkataḥ //
1.25.d:
अनधीतस्य विप्रस्य सर्वं भवति निष्फलम् ।
शब्दब्रह्ममयो विष्णुर्वेदः साक्षाद्धारि स्मृकतः ॥
1.25.m: for a twice-born who has not studied, everything becomes fruitless. / Viṣṇu consists of the sonic Brahman; the Veda is traditionally remembered as Hari himself.

1.25.s:
vedādhyāyī tato vipraḥ sarvānkāmānavānpuyāt //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde smārtācāreṣu varṇāśramadharmeṣvadhyayanādidharmanirupaṇaṃ nāma pañcaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.25.d:
वेदाध्यायी ततो विप्रः सर्वान्कामानवान्पुयात् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे स्मार्ताचारेषु वर्णाश्रमधर्मेष्वध्ययनादिधर्मनिरुपणं नाम पञ्चविंशो ऽध्यायः
1.25.m:
Therefore, a twice-born who studies the Veda will obtain all desires.

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, named 'Determination of the Duties of Study and the Like among the Duties of Castes and Life Stages in Smārta Conduct,' in the first quarter of the earlier section of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.26.s:
sanaka uvāca
vedagrahaṇaparyantaṃ śuśrūṣāniyato guroḥ /
anujñātastatastena kuryādagniparigraham //
1.26.d:
सनक उवाच
वेदग्रहणपर्यन्तं शुश्रूषानियतो गुरोः ।
अनुज्ञातस्ततस्तेन कुर्यादग्निपरिग्रहम् ॥
1.26.m: Sanaka said: / Devoted to serving the guru until the acquisition of the Veda, / permitted then by him, he should establish the sacred fires.

1.26.s:
vedāśca dharmaśāstrāṇi vedāṅgānyapi ca dvijaḥ /
adhītya gurave dattvā dakṣiṇāṃ saṃviśedvṛham //
1.26.d:
वेदाश्च धर्मशास्त्राणि वेदाङ्गान्यपि च द्विजः ।
अधीत्य गुरवे दत्त्वा दक्षिणां संविशेद्वृहम् ॥
1.26.m: Having studied the Vedas, the Dharmaśāstras, and the Vedāṅgas, / and having given the sacrificial fee to the guru, the twice-born should enter the household.

1.26.s:
rupalāvaṇyasaṃpannāṃ saguṇāṃ sukulodbhavām /
dvijaḥ samudvahetkanyāṃ suśīlāṃ dharma cāriṇīm //
1.26.d:
रुपलावण्यसंपन्नां सगुणां सुकुलोद्भवाम् ।
द्विजः समुद्वहेत्कन्यां सुशीलां धर्म चारिणीम् ॥
1.26.m: Endowed with beauty and charm, virtuous, born of an excellent family, / of good character, and practicing righteousness—such a maiden a twice-born should marry:

1.26.s:
mātṛtaḥ pañcamīṃ dhīmānpitataḥ satpamīṃ tathā /
dvijaḥ samudvahetkanyathā gurutalparāḥ //
1.26.d:
मातृतः पञ्चमीं धीमान्पिततः सत्पमीं तथा ।
द्विजः समुद्वहेत्कन्यथा गुरुतल्पराः ॥
1.26.m: fifth on the mother's side and seventh on the father's side, / such a maiden the wise twice-born should marry, devoted to the weightiest duties.

1.26.s:
rogiṇīṃ caiva vṛttākṣīṃ sarogakulasaṃbhavām /
atikeśāmakeśāmakeśāṃ ca vācālāṃ nodvahedvudhaḥ //
1.26.d:
रोगिणीं चैव वृत्ताक्षीं सरोगकुलसंभवाम् ।
अतिकेशामकेशामकेशां च वाचालां नोद्वहेद्वुधः ॥
1.26.m: A woman who is diseased, round-eyed, born of a sickly family, / excessively hairy, hairless, or talkative, the wise man should not marry;

1.26.s:
kopānāṃ vāmanāṃ caiva dīrghadehāṃ virupiṇīm /
nyānādhikāṅgīmunmattāṃ piśunāṃ nodvahed budhaḥ //
1.26.d:
कोपानां वामनां चैव दीर्घदेहां विरुपिणीम् ।
न्यानाधिकाङ्गीमुन्मत्तां पिशुनां नोद्वहेद् बुधः ॥
1.26.m: nor an angry, dwarfish, excessively tall, or misshapen woman; / nor one with deficient or redundant limbs, insane, or malicious should the wise man marry;

1.26.s:
sthūlagulphaāṃ dīrghajaṅghāṃ tathaiva puruṣākṛtim /
śmaśruvyañjanasaṃyuktāṃ kubjāṃ caivādvahenna ca //
1.26.d:
स्थूलगुल्फआं दीर्घजङ्घां तथैव पुरुषाकृतिम् ।
श्मश्रुव्यञ्जनसंयुक्तां कुब्जां चैवाद्वहेन्न च ॥
1.26.m: nor one with thick ankles, long shanks, of masculine appearance, / bearing the marks of a beard, or hunchbacked should he marry;

1.26.s:
vṛthāhāsyamukhīṃ caiva sadānyagṛha vāsinīm /
vivādaśīlāṃ bhramitāṃ niṣṭhurāṃ nodvahedrudhaḥ //
1.26.d:
वृथाहास्यमुखीं चैव सदान्यगृह वासिनीम् ।
विवादशीलां भ्रमितां निष्ठुरां नोद्वहेद्रुधः ॥
1.26.m: nor one with a face prone to pointless laughter, constantly living in another's house, / quarrelsome, roaming about, or harsh should the wise man marry;

1.26.s:
bahvaśinīṃ sthīladantāṃ sthūloṣṭhīṃ ghurghurasvanām /
atikṛṣṇāṃ raktavarṇāṃ dhūrtāṃ naivodvahe dvudhaḥ //
1.26.d:
बह्वशिनीं स्थीलदन्तां स्थूलोष्ठीं घुर्घुरस्वनाम् ।
अतिकृष्णां रक्तवर्णां धूर्तां नैवोद्वहे द्वुधः ॥
1.26.m: nor one who eats excessively, has thick teeth, thick lips, or makes a snoring sound; / nor one who is excessively dark, blood-red, or cunning should the wise man marry;

1.26.s:
sadā rodanaśīlāṃ ca pāṇḍurābhāṃ ca kutsitām /
tāsaśvāsādisaṃyuktāṃ nidrāśīlāṃ ca nodvahet //
1.26.d:
सदा रोदनशीलां च पाण्डुराभां च कुत्सिताम् ।
तासश्वासादिसंयुक्तां निद्राशीलां च नोद्वहेत् ॥
1.26.m: nor one constantly given to weeping, pale, contemptible, / afflicted with cough, asthma, and the like, or given to excessive sleep should he marry;

1.26.s:
anarthabhāṣiṇīṃ caiva lokadveṣa parāyaṇām /
parāpavādaniratāṃ taskārāṃ nodvahedvudhaḥ //
1.26.d:
अनर्थभाषिणीं चैव लोकद्वेष परायणाम् ।
परापवादनिरतां तस्कारां नोद्वहेद्वुधः ॥
1.26.m: nor one who speaks uselessly, is devoted to hatred of the world, / intent on slandering others, or a thief should the wise man marry;

1.26.s:
dīrghanāsāṃ ca kitavāṃ tanūruhavibhūṣigatām /
garvitāṃ bakavṛttiṃ ca sarvathā nodvahedvudhaḥ //
1.26.d:
दीर्घनासां च कितवां तनूरुहविभूषिगताम् ।
गर्वितां बकवृत्तिं च सर्वथा नोद्वहेद्वुधः ॥
1.26.m: nor one with a long nose, a gambler, adorned with body-hair, / arrogant, or behaving like a heron should the wise man ever marry.

1.26.s:
bālabhāvādavijñātasvabhāvāmudvahedyadi /
pragalbhāṃ vāguṇāṃ jñātvā sarvathā tāṃ parityajet //
1.26.d:
बालभावादविज्ञातस्वभावामुद्वहेद्यदि ।
प्रगल्भां वागुणां ज्ञात्वा सर्वथा तां परित्यजेत् ॥
1.26.m: If through childishness he marries one whose nature was unknown, / upon knowing her to be insolent or defective, he should abandon her completely.

1.26.s:
bharttṛputreṣu yā nārī sarvadā niṣṭhurā bhavet /
parānukūlinī yā ca sarvathā tāṃ parityajet //
1.26.d:
भर्त्तृपुत्रेषु या नारी सर्वदा निष्ठुरा भवेत् ।
परानुकूलिनी या च सर्वथा तां परित्यजेत् ॥
1.26.m: A woman who is always cruel to her husband and sons, / and who is favorable to other men—one should completely abandon her.

1.26.s:
vivāhāścāṣṭadhā jñeyā brāhmādyā munisattama /
pūrvaḥ pūrvo varo jñeyaḥ pūrvābhāve paraḥ paraḥ //
1.26.d:
विवाहाश्चाष्टधा ज्ञेया ब्राह्माद्या मुनिसत्तम ।
पूर्वः पूर्वो वरो ज्ञेयः पूर्वाभावे परः परः ॥
1.26.m: Marriages are known to be of eight kinds, O best of sages, beginning with the Brāhma; / each preceding one is considered superior, and in the absence of a preceding one, the next in order.

1.26.s:
brāhno daivastathaivārṣaḥ prājāpatyastathāsuraḥ /
gāndharvo rākṣasaścaiva paiśācaścāṣṭamo mataḥ //
1.26.d:
ब्राह्नो दैवस्तथैवार्षः प्राजापत्यस्तथासुरः ।
गान्धर्वो राक्षसश्चैव पैशाचश्चाष्टमो मतः ॥
