1.26.m: The Brāhma, Daiva, Ārṣa, Prājāpatya, and Āsura, / the Gāndharva, Rākṣasa, and the Paiśāca is considered the eighth.

1.26.s:
brāhmeṇa ca vivāhena vaivāhyo vai dvijottamaḥ /
daivenāpyathavā vipra kecidārṣaṃ pracakṣate //
1.26.d:
ब्राह्मेण च विवाहेन वैवाह्यो वै द्विजोत्तमः ।
दैवेनाप्यथवा विप्र केचिदार्षं प्रचक्षते ॥
1.26.m: The best among the twice-born should marry by the Brāhma marriage, / or indeed by the Daiva, O brahmin; some declare the Ārṣa.

1.26.s:
prājāpatyādayo vipra vivāhāḥ pañcaja garhitāḥ /
abhāveṣu tu pūrveṣāṃ kuryādeva parānbudhaḥ //
1.26.d:
प्राजापत्यादयो विप्र विवाहाः पञ्चज गर्हिताः ।
अभावेषु तु पूर्वेषां कुर्यादेव परान्बुधः ॥
1.26.m: The five marriages beginning with the Prājāpatya, O brahmin, are censured; / yet in the absence of the former ones, a wise man may indeed resort to the latter.

1.26.s:
yajñopavītadvitayaṃ sottarīyaṃ ca dhārayet /
suvarṇakuṇḍale caiva dhautavastradvayaṃ tathā //
1.26.d:
यज्ञोपवीतद्वितयं सोत्तरीयं च धारयेत् ।
सुवर्णकुण्डले चैव धौतवस्त्रद्वयं तथा ॥
1.26.m: He should wear two sacred threads and an upper garment, / two gold earrings, and likewise two clean garments.

1.26.s:
anulepanalitpāṅgaḥ kṛttakeśanakhaḥ śuciḥ /
dhārayedvaiṇavaṃ daṇḍaṃ sodakaṃ ca kamaṇḍalum //
1.26.d:
अनुलेपनलित्पाङ्गः कृत्तकेशनखः शुचिः ।
धारयेद्वैणवं दण्डं सोदकं च कमण्डलुम् ॥
1.26.m: With his limbs smeared with ointment, his hair and nails clipped, pure, / he should carry a bamboo staff and a waterpot filled with water.

1.26.s:
uṣṇīṣamamalaṃ chatraṃ pāduke cāpyupānahau /
dhārayetpuṣpamālye ca sugandhaṃ priyadarśanaḥ //
1.26.d:
उष्णीषममलं छत्रं पादुके चाप्युपानहौ ।
धारयेत्पुष्पमाल्ये च सुगन्धं प्रियदर्शनः ॥
1.26.m: He should wear a clean turban, an umbrella, wooden sandals, and leather shoes; / pleasant to behold, he should wear fragrant flower garlands.

1.26.s:
nityaṃ svādhyāyaśīlaḥ syādyathācāraṃ samācaret /
parānnaṃ naiva bhuñjīta paravādaṃ ca varjayet //
1.26.d:
नित्यं स्वाध्यायशीलः स्याद्यथाचारं समाचरेत् ।
परान्नं नैव भुञ्जीत परवादं च वर्जयेत् ॥
1.26.m: He should be constantly devoted to scriptural recitation and should observe proper conduct; / he must never eat another's food and must avoid speaking ill of others.

1.26.s:
pādena nākrametpādamucchiṣṭaṃ naiva laṅghayet /
na saṃhatābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ kaṇḍūyedātmanaḥ śiraḥ //
1.26.d:
पादेन नाक्रमेत्पादमुच्छिष्टं नैव लङ्घयेत् ।
न संहताभ्यां हस्ताभ्यां कण्डूयेदात्मनः शिरः ॥
1.26.m: He should not press one foot against the other, nor cross over food remnants; / he should not scratch his own head with both hands joined together.

1.26.s:
pūjyaṃ devālayaṃ caiva nāpasavyaṃ vrajeddijaḥ /
devārcācamanasnānavrataśrāddhakriyādiṣu //
1.26.d:
पूज्यं देवालयं चैव नापसव्यं व्रजेद्दिजः ।
देवार्चाचमनस्नानव्रतश्राद्धक्रियादिषु ॥
1.26.m: A twice-born man should not circumambulate in a counter-clockwise direction a venerable person or a temple of God; / during worship of deities, sipping water, bathing, vows, ancestral rites, and other ceremonies,

1.26.s:
na bhavenmuktakeśaśca naikavastradharastathā /
nāroheduṣṭrayānaṃ ca śuṣkavādaṃ ca varjayet //
1.26.d:
न भवेन्मुक्तकेशश्च नैकवस्त्रधरस्तथा ।
नारोहेदुष्ट्रयानं च शुष्कवादं च वर्जयेत् ॥
1.26.m: he should not have his hair disheveled, nor should he wear a single garment; / he should not ride upon a camel-cart, and he should avoid vain disputation.

1.26.s:
anya striyaṃ na gacchecca paiśunyaṃ parivarjayet /
nāpasavyaṃ vrajedvipra goścatthānalaparvatān //
1.26.d:
अन्य स्त्रियं न गच्छेच्च पैशुन्यं परिवर्जयेत् ।
नापसव्यं व्रजेद्विप्र गोश्चत्थानलपर्वतान् ॥
1.26.m: He must not approach another man's wife, and he should completely avoid slander; / a brahmin should not circumambulate counter-clockwise a cow, a sacred fig tree, fire, or mountains,

1.26.s:
catuṣpathaṃ caityavṛkṣarṃ devakhātaṃ nṛpaṃ tathā /
asūyāṃ matsaratvaṃ ca divāsvāpaṃ ca varjayet //
1.26.d:
चतुष्पथं चैत्यवृक्षर्ं देवखातं नृपं तथा ।
असूयां मत्सरत्वं च दिवास्वापं च वर्जयेत् ॥
1.26.m: a crossroads, a sacred tree, a temple reservoir, or a king; / he should avoid malice, envy, and sleeping during the day.

1.26.s:
na vadetparapāpāni svapuṇyaṃ na prakāśayet /
svakaṃ nāma svanakṣatraṃ mānaṃ caivātigopayet //
1.26.d:
न वदेत्परपापानि स्वपुण्यं न प्रकाशयेत् ।
स्वकं नाम स्वनक्षत्रं मानं चैवातिगोपयेत् ॥
1.26.m: He should not speak of others' sins, nor display his own merit; / he should carefully conceal his own name, his birth-star, and his pride.

1.26.s:
na durjanaiḥ saha vase nnāśāstraṃ śṛṇuyāttathā /
āsavadyūtagīteṣu dvijastu na rartiṃ caret //
1.26.d:
न दुर्जनैः सह वसे न्नाशास्त्रं शृणुयात्तथा ।
आसवद्यूतगीतेषु द्विजस्तु न रर्तिं चरेत् ॥
1.26.m: He should not dwell with wicked persons, nor listen to unscriptural doctrines; / a twice-born man should take no delight in liquor, gambling, or singing.

1.26.s:
ārdrāsthi ca tathocchiṣṭaṃ śūdraṃ ca patitaṃ tathā /
sarpaṃ ca bhaṣaṇaṃ spṛṣṭvā sacailaṃ snānamācaret //
1.26.d:
आर्द्रास्थि च तथोच्छिष्टं शूद्रं च पतितं तथा ।
सर्पं च भषणं स्पृष्ट्वा सचैलं स्नानमाचरेत् ॥
1.26.m: Having touched a wet bone, food remnants, a śūdra, an outcaste, / a snake, or a dog, he should perform a bath with his clothes on.

1.26.s:
citiṃ ca citikāṣṭaṃ ca yūpaṃ cāṇḍālameva ca /
spṛṣṭvā devalakaṃ caiva savāsā jalamāviśet //
1.26.d:
चितिं च चितिकाष्टं च यूपं चाण्डालमेव च ।
स्पृष्ट्वा देवलकं चैव सवासा जलमाविशेत् ॥
1.26.m: Having touched a funeral pyre, pyre-wood, a sacrificial post, a caṇḍāla, / or a temple-priest, he should enter water with his clothes on.

1.26.s:
dīpakhaṭvātanucchāyākeśavas trakaṭodakam /
ajāmārjaṃnimārjārareṇurddaivaṃ śubhaṃ haret //
1.26.d:
दीपखट्वातनुच्छायाकेशवस् त्रकटोदकम् ।
अजामार्जंनिमार्जाररेणुर्द्दैवं शुभं हरेत् ॥
1.26.m: The shadow of a lamp, of a bed, or of a human body, hair, wash-water from cloth, / water from a broom, and dust raised by a cat or goat destroy one's accumulated auspicious fate.

1.26.s:
śūrppavātaṃ pretadhūmaṃ tathā śūdrānnabhojanam /
vṛṣalīpatisaṅgaṃ ca dūrataḥ parivarjayet //
1.26.d:
शूर्प्पवातं प्रेतधूमं तथा शूद्रान्नभोजनम् ।
वृषलीपतिसङ्गं च दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् ॥
1.26.m: Wind from a winnowing basket, smoke from a corpse, the eating of a śūdra's food, / and association with the husband of a low-caste woman—he should avoid all these from afar.

1.26.s:
asacchārstrārthamananaṃ khādanaṃ nakhakeśayoḥ /
tathaiva nagnaśayanaṃ sarvadā parivarjayet //
1.26.d:
असच्छार्स्त्रार्थमननं खादनं नखकेशयोः ।
तथैव नग्नशयनं सर्वदा परिवर्जयेत् ॥
1.26.m: Contemplation of false scriptures, biting nails or hair, / and sleeping naked—these he should always avoid.

1.26.s:
śirobhyaṅgāvaśiṣṭena tailenāṅgaṃ na lepayet /
tāṃbūlamaśuciṃ nādyāttathā suptaṃ na bodhayet //
1.26.d:
शिरोभ्यङ्गावशिष्टेन तैलेनाङ्गं न लेपयेत् ।
तांबूलमशुचिं नाद्यात्तथा सुप्तं न बोधयेत् ॥
1.26.m: He should not smear his limbs with the oil left over from anointing his head; / he should not eat impure betel, nor awaken someone who is asleep.

1.26.s:
nāśuddho 'gniṃ paricaretpūjayedgurudevatāḥ /
na vāmahastenaikena pibedvakreṇa vā jalam //
1.26.d:
नाशुद्धो ऽग्निं परिचरेत्पूजयेद्गुरुदेवताः ।
न वामहस्तेनैकेन पिबेद्वक्रेण वा जलम् ॥
1.26.m: Being impure, he must not tend the sacred fire, nor worship the guru and the deities; / he should not drink water with his left hand alone, nor directly with his mouth.

1.26.s:
na cākramedgurośchāyāṃ tadājñāṃ ca munīśvara /
na nindedyogino viprānvratino 'pi yatīṃstathā //
1.26.d:
न चाक्रमेद्गुरोश्छायां तदाज्ञां च मुनीश्वर ।
न निन्देद्योगिनो विप्रान्व्रतिनो ऽपि यतींस्तथा ॥
1.26.m: He should not step upon the shadow of his guru, nor upon his command, O lord of sages; / he should not revile yogins, brahmins, observers of vows, or ascetics.

1.26.s:
parasparasya marmāṇi na kadāpi vadeddvijaḥ /
darśe ca paurṇamāsyāṃ ca yāgaṃ kuryādyathāvidhi //
1.26.d:
परस्परस्य मर्माणि न कदापि वदेद्द्विजः ।
दर्शे च पौर्णमास्यां च यागं कुर्याद्यथाविधि ॥
1.26.m: A twice-born man should never disclose another's vulnerabilities; / on the new-moon day and on the full-moon day, he should perform sacrifice according to the rule.

1.26.s:
upasanaṃ ca hotavyaṃ sāyaṃ prātardvijātibhiḥ /
upāsanaparityāgī surāpītyucyate budhaiḥ //
1.26.d:
उपसनं च होतव्यं सायं प्रातर्द्विजातिभिः ।
उपासनपरित्यागी सुरापीत्युच्यते बुधैः ॥
1.26.m: Twice-born men must offer oblations in the domestic fire evening and morning; / one who abandons the domestic worship is called a drinker of liquor by the wise.

1.26.s:
ayane viṣuve caiva yugādiṣu caturṣvapi /
darśe ca pretapakṣe ca śrāddhaṃ kuryādgṛhī dvijaḥ //
1.26.d:
अयने विषुवे चैव युगादिषु चतुर्ष्वपि ।
दर्शे च प्रेतपक्षे च श्राद्धं कुर्याद्गृही द्विजः ॥
1.26.m: At the solstices, at the equinoxes, at the beginnings of all four yugas, / on the new-moon day, and in the fortnight of the ancestors, the twice-born householder should perform a śrāddha.

1.26.s:
manvādiṣu mṛdāhe ca aṣṭakāsu ca nārada /
nāvadhānye samāyāte gṛhī śrāddhaṃ samācaret //
1.26.d:
मन्वादिषु मृदाहे च अष्टकासु च नारद ।
नावधान्ये समायाते गृही श्राद्धं समाचरेत् ॥
1.26.m: On the beginnings of the Manvantaras, on the day of [a parent's] death, during the Aṣṭakā days, O Nārada, / and when new grain has arrived, the householder should perform a śrāddha.

1.26.s:
śrotriye gṛhamāyāte grahaṇe candrasūryoḥ /
puṇyakṣetreṣu tīrtheṣu gṛhī śrāddhaṃ samācaret //
1.26.d:
श्रोत्रिये गृहमायाते ग्रहणे चन्द्रसूर्योः ।
पुण्यक्षेत्रेषु तीर्थेषु गृही श्राद्धं समाचरेत् ॥
1.26.m: When a Vedic scholar arrives at his house, during an eclipse of the moon or the sun, / and at holy fields and sacred fords, the householder should perform a śrāddha.

1.26.s:
yajño dānaṃ tapo homaḥ svādhyāyaḥ pitṛtarpaṇam /
vṛthā bhavati tatsarvamūrddhapuṇḍraṃ vinā kṛtam //
1.26.d:
यज्ञो दानं तपो होमः स्वाध्यायः पितृतर्पणम् ।
वृथा भवति तत्सर्वमूर्द्धपुण्ड्रं विना कृतम् ॥
1.26.m: Sacrifice, giving, austerity, fire oblations, recitation of scripture, and offering to ancestors— / all that becomes futile if performed without the upward sectarian mark.

1.26.s:
urddhapuṇḍraṃ ca tulasīṃ śrāddhe necchanti kecana /
vṛthācāraḥ parityājyastasmācchreyo 'rthibhirdvijaiḥ //
1.26.d:
उर्द्धपुण्ड्रं च तुलसीं श्राद्धे नेच्छन्ति केचन ।
वृथाचारः परित्याज्यस्तस्माच्छ्रेयो ऽर्थिभिर्द्विजैः ॥
1.26.m: Some do not desire the upward sectarian mark and the tulasī plant in a śrāddha; / therefore, twice-born men seeking spiritual welfare should abandon such useless practice.

1.26.s:
ityevamādayo dharmāḥ smṛtimārgapracoditāḥ /
kāryā dvijātibhiḥ samyaksarvakarmaphalapradāḥ //
1.26.d:
इत्येवमादयो धर्माः स्मृतिमार्गप्रचोदिताः ।
कार्या द्विजातिभिः सम्यक्सर्वकर्मफलप्रदाः ॥
1.26.m: Such duties enjoined by the path of the Smṛtis / must be properly performed by the twice-born, bestowing the fruit of all rites.

1.26.s:
sadā cāraparā ye tu teṣāṃ viṣṇuḥ prasīdati /
viṣṇau prasannatāṃ yāte kimasādhyaṃ dvijottama //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde smārttadhermaṣu vedādhyayanādikasya gṛhasthadharmasya ca nirupaṇaṃ nāma ṣaḍviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.26.d:
सदा चारपरा ये तु तेषां विष्णुः प्रसीदति ।
विष्णौ प्रसन्नतां याते किमसाध्यं द्विजोत्तम ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे स्मार्त्तधेर्मषु वेदाध्ययनादिकस्य गृहस्थधर्मस्य च निरुपणं नाम षड्विंशो ऽध्यायः
1.26.m:
Viṣṇu is pleased with those who are devoted to good conduct; / when Viṣṇu is pleased, what is impossible to attain, O best of the twice-born?

Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, named 'The Determination of the Householder's Duty including Study of the Veda and Other Duties in the Smārta Codes', in the first quarter of the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.27.s:
sanaka uvāca
gṛhasthasya sadācāraṃ vakṣyāmi munisattama /
yadrūtāṃ sarvapāpāni naśyantyeva na saṃśayaḥ //
1.27.d:
सनक उवाच
गृहस्थस्य सदाचारं वक्ष्यामि मुनिसत्तम ।
यद्रूतां सर्वपापानि नश्यन्त्येव न संशयः ॥
1.27.m: Sanaka said: / I shall describe the proper conduct of a householder, O best of sages, / by the observance of which all sins are surely destroyed without doubt.

1.27.s:
brāhne muhūrte cotthāya puruṣārthāvirodhinīm /
vṛttiṃ saṃcintayedvipra kṛtakeśaprasādhanaḥ //
1.27.d:
ब्राह्ने मुहूर्ते चोत्थाय पुरुषार्थाविरोधिनीम् ।
वृत्तिं संचिन्तयेद्विप्र कृतकेशप्रसाधनः ॥
1.27.m: Having risen in the Brāhma hour, he should reflect upon a livelihood / that does not conflict with the aims of human life, O brahmin, having arranged his hair.

1.27.s:
divāsaṃdhyāsu karṇasthabrahmasūtra udaḍmukhaḥ /
kuryānmūtrapurīṣe tu rātrau ceddakṣiṇāmukhaḥ //
1.27.d:
दिवासंध्यासु कर्णस्थब्रह्मसूत्र उदड्मुखः ।
कुर्यान्मूत्रपुरीषे तु रात्रौ चेद्दक्षिणामुखः ॥
1.27.m: During the day and twilight, placing his sacred cord upon his ear, facing north, / he should evacuate urine and feces, but facing south at night.

1.27.s:
śiraḥ prāvṛtya vastreṇa hyantarddhāya tṛṇairmahīm /
vahankāṣṭaṃ kareṇaikaṃ tāvanmaunī bhaveddvijaḥ //
1.27.d:
शिरः प्रावृत्य वस्त्रेण ह्यन्तर्द्धाय तृणैर्महीम् ।
वहन्काष्टं करेणैकं तावन्मौनी भवेद्द्विजः ॥
1.27.m: Covering his head with a cloth and covering the earth with blades of grass, / holding a stick in one hand, the twice-born man should remain silent for that time.

1.27.s:
pathi goṣṭe nadītīre taḍāgagṛhasannidhau /
tathā vṛkṣasya cchāyāyāṃ kāntāre vahnisannidhau //
1.27.d:
पथि गोष्टे नदीतीरे तडागगृहसन्निधौ ।
तथा वृक्षस्य च्छायायां कान्तारे वह्निसन्निधौ ॥
1.27.m: On a path, in a cow-pen, on a riverbank, near a pond or a house, / likewise in the shade of a tree, in a forest, in the vicinity of fire,

1.27.s:
devālaye tathodyāne kṛṣṭabhūmau catuṣpathe /
brāhmaṇānāṃ samīpe ca tathā goguruyoṣitām //
1.27.d:
देवालये तथोद्याने कृष्टभूमौ चतुष्पथे ।
ब्राह्मणानां समीपे च तथा गोगुरुयोषिताम् ॥
1.27.m: in a temple, in a garden, on cultivated land, at a crossroads, / near brahmins, and near cows, teachers, and women,

1.27.s:
tuṣāṅgārakapāleṣu jalamadhye tathaiva ca /
evamādiṣu deśeṣu malamūtraṃ na kārayet //
1.27.d:
तुषाङ्गारकपालेषु जलमध्ये तथैव च ।
एवमादिषु देशेषु मलमूत्रं न कारयेत् ॥
1.27.m: on chaff, charcoal, or potsherds, and likewise in the middle of water— / in places such as these, he should not void feces or urine.

1.27.s:
śauce yatnaḥ sadā kāryaḥ śaucamūlo dvijaḥ smṛtaḥ /
śaucācāravihīnasya samastaṃ karma niṣphalam //
1.27.d:
शौचे यत्नः सदा कार्यः शौचमूलो द्विजः स्मृतः ।
शौचाचारविहीनस्य समस्तं कर्म निष्फलम् ॥
1.27.m: Effort should always be made toward purification; the twice-born is remembered as rooted in purification; / for one who lacks purification and proper conduct, every ritual act is fruitless.

1.27.s:
śaucaṃ tu dvividhaṃ proktaṃ brāhmamābhyāntaraṃ tathā /
mṛjjalābhyāṃ bahiḥ śuddhirbhāvaśuddhistathāntaram //
1.27.d:
शौचं तु द्विविधं प्रोक्तं ब्राह्ममाभ्यान्तरं तथा ।
मृज्जलाभ्यां बहिः शुद्धिर्भावशुद्धिस्तथान्तरम् ॥
1.27.m: Purification is declared to be of two kinds: the outer and the inner; / outer purity is by means of earth and water, while inner purity is purity of intention.

1.27.s:
gṛhītaśiśraścotthāya śaucārthaṃ mṛdamāharet /.
na mūṣakādikhanitāṃ phaālotkṛṣṭāṃ tathaiva ca //
1.27.d:
गृहीतशिश्रश्चोत्थाय शौचार्थं मृदमाहरेत् ॥
न मूषकादिखनितां फआलोत्कृष्टां तथैव च ॥
1.27.m: Holding his penis and rising, he should fetch earth for purification; / not that which is dug up by mice or the like, nor that which is turned up by a plow,

1.27.s:
vāpīkūpataḍāgebhyo nāharedapi mṛttikām /
śaucaṃ kuryātprayatnena samādāya śubhāṃ mṛdam //
1.27.d:
वापीकूपतडागेभ्यो नाहरेदपि मृत्तिकाम् ।
शौचं कुर्यात्प्रयत्नेन समादाय शुभां मृदम् ॥
1.27.m: nor should he take earth from step-wells, wells, or ponds; / taking auspicious earth, he should perform purification with effort.

1.27.s:
liṅge mṛdekā dātavyā tisro vā meḍhrayordvayoḥ /
etanmūtramutsarge śaucamāhūrmanīṣiṇaḥ //
1.27.d:
लिङ्गे मृदेका दातव्या तिस्रो वा मेढ्रयोर्द्वयोः ।
एतन्मूत्रमुत्सर्गे शौचमाहूर्मनीषिणः ॥
1.27.m: One portion of earth is to be applied to the penis, or three to both testicles; / this the wise call purification after discharging urine.

1.27.s:
ekā liṅge gude pañca daśa vāme tathobhayoḥ /
satpa tisraḥ pradātavyāḥ pādayormṛttikāḥ pṛthak //
1.27.d:
एका लिङ्गे गुदे पञ्च दश वामे तथोभयोः ।
सत्प तिस्रः प्रदातव्याः पादयोर्मृत्तिकाः पृथक् ॥
1.27.m: One is to be applied to the penis, five to the anus, ten to the left hand, and seven to both; / three portions of earth are to be applied to each foot separately.

1.27.s:
etacchaucaṃ viḍutsarge gandhalepāpanuttaye /
etacchaucaṃ gṛhasthasya dviguṇaṃ brahmacāriṇām //
1.27.d:
एतच्छौचं विडुत्सर्गे गन्धलेपापनुत्तये ।
एतच्छौचं गृहस्थस्य द्विगुणं ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ॥
1.27.m: This is the cleansing during evacuation of feces, to remove smell and coating. / This cleansing is for the householder; it is doubled for celibate students,

1.27.s:
triguṇāṃ tu vanasthānāṃ yatīnāṃ taccarguṇam /
svasthāne pūrṇaśaucaṃ syātpathyarddhaṃ munisattama //
1.27.d:
त्रिगुणां तु वनस्थानां यतीनां तच्चर्गुणम् ।
स्वस्थाने पूर्णशौचं स्यात्पथ्यर्द्धं मुनिसत्तम ॥
1.27.m: tripled for forest-dwellers, and quadrupled for ascetics. / Cleansing is full in one’s own place, and half on the road, O best of sages.

1.27.s:
āture niyamo nāsti mahāpadi tathaiva ca /
gandhalepakṣayakaraṃ śaurcaṃ kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ //
1.27.d:
आतुरे नियमो नास्ति महापदि तथैव च ।
गन्धलेपक्षयकरं शौर्चं कुर्याद्विचक्षणः ॥
1.27.m: There is no fixed rule for the sick, nor in times of great distress; / a discerning person should perform the cleansing so as to eliminate smell and coating.

1.27.s:
strīṇāmanupanītānāṃ gandhalepakṣayāvadhi /
vratasthānāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ yativacchaucamiṣyate //
1.27.d:
स्त्रीणामनुपनीतानां गन्धलेपक्षयावधि ।
व्रतस्थानां तु सर्वेषां यतिवच्छौचमिष्यते ॥
1.27.m: For women and the uninitiated, the limit is the elimination of smell and coating. / But for all who are observing a vow, cleansing like that of an ascetic is prescribed.

1.27.s:
vidhavānāṃ ca virpendra etadeva nigadyate /
evaṃ śaucaṃ tu nirvartya paścādvai susamāhitaḥ //
1.27.d:
विधवानां च विर्पेन्द्र एतदेव निगद्यते ।
एवं शौचं तु निर्वर्त्य पश्चाद्वै सुसमाहितः ॥
1.27.m: The very same is stated for widows as well, O best of priests. / Having thus performed cleansing, then, fully collected in mind,

1.27.s:
prāgāsya udagāsyo vāpyācāmetprayartendriyaḥ /
triścaturdhā pibedāpo gandhaphenādivarjitāḥ //
1.27.d:
प्रागास्य उदगास्यो वाप्याचामेत्प्रयर्तेन्द्रियः ।
त्रिश्चतुर्धा पिबेदापो गन्धफेनादिवर्जिताः ॥
1.27.m: facing east or north, with restrained senses, he should sip water. / Three or four times he should drink water that is free of odor, foam, and the like.

1.27.s:
dvirmārjayetkapolaṃ ca talenoṣṭhau ca sattama /
tarjanyaṅguṣṭhayogena nāsārandhradvayaṃ spṛśet //
1.27.d:
द्विर्मार्जयेत्कपोलं च तलेनोष्ठौ च सत्तम ।
तर्जन्यङ्गुष्ठयोगेन नासारन्ध्रद्वयं स्पृशेत् ॥
1.27.m: Twice he should wipe his cheek, and his lips with the palm, O best of men; / with the thumb joined to the forefinger he should touch both nostrils.

1.27.s:
aguṃṣṭānāmikābhyāṃ ca cakṣuḥ śrotre yathākramam /
kaniṣṭāṅguṣṭayogena nābhideśe spṛśeddvijaḥ //
1.27.d:
अगुंष्टानामिकाभ्यां च चक्षुः श्रोत्रे यथाक्रमम् ।
कनिष्टाङ्गुष्टयोगेन नाभिदेशे स्पृशेद्द्विजः ॥
1.27.m: With the thumb and ring finger [he should touch] the eyes and ears respectively; / joining the little finger and the thumb, the twice-born should touch the region of the navel.

1.27.s:
talenoraḥsthalaṃ caiva aṅgulyagraiḥ śiraḥ spṛśet /
talena cāṅgulāgrairvā spṛśedaṃsau vicakṣaṇaḥ //
1.27.d:
तलेनोरःस्थलं चैव अङ्गुल्यग्रैः शिरः स्पृशेत् ।
तलेन चाङ्गुलाग्रैर्वा स्पृशेदंसौ विचक्षणः ॥
1.27.m: With the palm [he should touch] the chest, and with the tips of the fingers he should touch the head; / with the palm or with the fingertips the discerning person should touch the shoulders.

1.27.s:
evamācamya vipredra śuddhimānpotyanuttamām /
dantakāṣṭaṃ tataḥ khādetsatvacaṃ śastavṛkṣajam //
1.27.d:
एवमाचम्य विप्रेद्र शुद्धिमान्पोत्यनुत्तमाम् ।
दन्तकाष्टं ततः खादेत्सत्वचं शस्तवृक्षजम् ॥
1.27.m: Having sipped water in this way, O best of priests, he attains supreme purity. / Then he should chew a tooth-stick with bark, produced from an auspicious tree,

1.27.s:
bilvāsanāpāmārgaṇāṃ nimbānmārkādiśākhinām /
prakṣālya vāriṇā caiva mantreṇāpyabhimantritam //
1.27.d:
बिल्वासनापामार्गणां निम्बान्मार्कादिशाखिनाम् ।
प्रक्षाल्य वारिणा चैव मन्त्रेणाप्यभिमन्त्रितम् ॥
1.27.m: from the bilva, asana, apāmārga, nimba, arka, and other trees. / Having washed it with water and consecrated it with the mantra:

1.27.s:
āyurbalaṃ yaśo varcaḥ prajāḥ paśuvasūni ca /
brahma prajñāṃ ca medhāṃ ca tvanno dhehi vanaspate //
1.27.d:
आयुर्बलं यशो वर्चः प्रजाः पशुवसूनि च ।
ब्रह्म प्रज्ञां च मेधां च त्वन्नो धेहि वनस्पते ॥
1.27.m: “O lord of the forest, bestow upon us lifespan, strength, renown, radiant energy, / offspring, cattle, wealth, sacred knowledge, wisdom, and retentive intellect.”

1.27.s:
kaniṣṭāgrasamaṃ sthaulye vipraḥ khādeddaśāṅgulam /
navāṅgulaṃ kṣatriyaśca vaiśyaścāṣṭāṅgulonmitam //
1.27.d:
कनिष्टाग्रसमं स्थौल्ये विप्रः खादेद्दशाङ्गुलम् ।
नवाङ्गुलं क्षत्रियश्च वैश्यश्चाष्टाङ्गुलोन्मितम् ॥
1.27.m: A brāhmaṇa should chew [a stick] ten finger-breadths [long], equal in thickness to the tip of the little finger; / a kṣatriya [one of] nine finger-breadths, and a vaiśya one measured at eight finger-breadths.

1.27.s:
śūdro vedāṅgulamitaṃ vanitā ca munīśvara /
alābhe daitakāṣṭānāṃ gaṇḍūṣairbhānusaṃmitaiḥ //
1.27.d:
शूद्रो वेदाङ्गुलमितं वनिता च मुनीश्वर ।
अलाभे दैतकाष्टानां गण्डूषैर्भानुसंमितैः ॥
1.27.m: A śūdra [should chew one] measuring four finger-breadths, and likewise a woman, O lord of sages. / In the absence of tooth-sticks, by mouthfuls [of water] numbering twelve,

1.27.s:
muthaśuddhirvidhīyeta tṛṇapatrasamanvitaiḥ /
kareṇādāya vāmena saṃcarvedvāmadaṃṣṭrayā //
1.27.d:
मुथशुद्धिर्विधीयेत तृणपत्रसमन्वितैः ।
करेणादाय वामेन संचर्वेद्वामदंष्ट्रया ॥
1.27.m: cleansing of the mouth should be performed, accompanied by blades of grass or leaves. / Taking it with the left hand, he should chew it with the left molar.

1.27.s:
dvijānsaṃgharṣya godohaṃ tataḥ prakṣālya pāṭayet /
jihvāmullikhya tābhyāṃ tu dalubhyāṃ niyatendriyaḥ //
1.27.d:
द्विजान्संघर्ष्य गोदोहं ततः प्रक्षाल्य पाटयेत् ।
जिह्वामुल्लिख्य ताभ्यां तु दलुभ्यां नियतेन्द्रियः ॥
1.27.m: Having rubbed the teeth for the milking-time of a cow, he should then wash it and split it; / having scraped the tongue with those two halves, with senses controlled,

1.27.s:
prakṣālya prakṣipedū dūre bhūyaścācamya pūrvavat /
tataḥ snānaṃ prakurvīta nadyādau vimale jale //
1.27.d:
प्रक्षाल्य प्रक्षिपेदू दूरे भूयश्चाचम्य पूर्ववत् ।
ततः स्नानं प्रकुर्वीत नद्यादौ विमले जले ॥
1.27.m: he should wash it and throw it far away, and sip water again as before. / Then he should take a bath in the pure water of a river or the like.

1.27.s:
taṭaṃ prakṣālya darbhāśca vinyasya praviśejjalam /
praṇamya tatra tīrthāni āvāhya ravimaṇḍalāt //
1.27.d:
तटं प्रक्षाल्य दर्भाश्च विन्यस्य प्रविशेज्जलम् ।
प्रणम्य तत्र तीर्थानि आवाह्य रविमण्डलात् ॥
1.27.m: Having washed the bank and spread darbha-grass, he should enter the water; / having bowed down there, having invoked the sacred fords from the solar orb,

1.27.s:
gandhādyairmaṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā dhyātvā devaṃ janārdanam /
snāyānmantrānsmaranpuṇyāṃstīrthāni ca viriñcija //
1.27.d:
गन्धाद्यैर्मण्डलं कृत्वा ध्यात्वा देवं जनार्दनम् ।
स्नायान्मन्त्रान्स्मरन्पुण्यांस्तीर्थानि च विरिञ्चिज ॥
1.27.m: having made a sacred diagram with fragrances and the like, and meditated upon the god Janārdana, / he should bathe while recollecting sacred mantras and sacred fords, O born of Brahmā:

1.27.s:
gaṅge ca yamune caiva godāvari sarasvati /
narmade siṃdhukāveri jale 'sminsannidhiṃ kuru //
1.27.d:
गङ्गे च यमुने चैव गोदावरि सरस्वति ।
नर्मदे सिंधुकावेरि जले ऽस्मिन्सन्निधिं कुरु ॥
1.27.m: “O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī, / Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī, enter into this water!

1.27.s:
puṣkarādyāni tīrthāni gaṅgādyāḥ saritastathā /
āgacchantu mahābhāgāḥ snānakāle sadā mama //
1.27.d:
पुष्कराद्यानि तीर्थानि गङ्गाद्याः सरितस्तथा ।
आगच्छन्तु महाभागाः स्नानकाले सदा मम ॥
1.27.m: May the sacred fords such as Puṣkara, and the rivers such as the Gaṅgā, / auspicious ones, always come at the time of my bathing!

1.27.s:
ayodhyā mathurā māyā kāśīṃ kāñcī hyavantikā /
purī dvārāvatī jñeyā satpaitā mokṣadāyikāḥ //
1.27.d:
अयोध्या मथुरा माया काशीं काञ्ची ह्यवन्तिका ।
पुरी द्वारावती ज्ञेया सत्पैता मोक्षदायिकाः ॥
1.27.m: Ayodhyā, Mathurā, Māyā, Kāśī, Kāñcī, Avantikā, / and the city of Dvārāvatī—these seven should be known as givers of liberation.”

1.27.s:
tato 'dhamarṣaṇa japtvā yatāsurvārisaṃplutaḥ /
snānāṅgaṃ tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvācamyārdhyaṃ bhānaver'payet //
1.27.d:
ततो ऽधमर्षण जप्त्वा यतासुर्वारिसंप्लुतः ।
स्नानाङ्गं तर्पणं कृत्वाचम्यार्ध्यं भानवेर्ऽपयेत् ॥
1.27.m: Then, having recited the aghamarṣaṇa mantra with breath restrained while immersed in the water, / having made libations as a limb of the bath, and sipped water, he should offer water-offerings to the sun.

1.27.s:
tato dhyātvā vivasvantaṃ jalānnirgatya nārada /
paridhāyāhataṃ dhautaṃ dvitīyaṃ parivīya ca //
1.27.d:
ततो ध्यात्वा विवस्वन्तं जलान्निर्गत्य नारद ।
परिधायाहतं धौतं द्वितीयं परिवीय च ॥
1.27.m: Then, having meditated on Vivasvat, having emerged from the water, O Nārada, / having put on an unwashed new cloth and wrapped a second one around himself,

1.27.s:
kuśāsane samāviśya saṃdhyākarma samārabhet /
īśānābhimukho vipra gāyatryācamya vai dvija //
1.27.d:
कुशासने समाविश्य संध्याकर्म समारभेत् ।
ईशानाभिमुखो विप्र गायत्र्याचम्य वै द्विज ॥
1.27.m: having seated himself upon a kuśa-grass mat, he should commence the twilight rites. / Facing northeast, O twice-born priest, having sipped water with the gāyatrī,

1.27.s:
ṛtamityabhimantryārtha punarevāmed budhaḥ /
tatastu vāriṇātmānaṃ veṣṭayitvā samukṣya ca //
1.27.d:
ऋतमित्यभिमन्त्र्यार्थ पुनरेवामेद् बुधः ।
ततस्तु वारिणात्मानं वेष्टयित्वा समुक्ष्य च ॥
1.27.m: having consecrated the water with “ṛtam”, the wise one should sip water again. / Then, having encircled himself with water and sprinkled it,

1.27.s:
saṃkalpya praṇavānte tu ṛṣicchandaḥ surānsmaran /
bhūrādibhirvyāhṛtibhiḥ satpabhiḥ prokṣya mastakam //
1.27.d:
संकल्प्य प्रणवान्ते तु ऋषिच्छन्दः सुरान्स्मरन् ।
भूरादिभिर्व्याहृतिभिः सत्पभिः प्रोक्ष्य मस्तकम् ॥
1.27.m: having made the resolve, and recollecting the seer, meter, and deities at the end of the praṇava, / having sprinkled his head with the seven sacred utterances beginning with bhūḥ,

1.27.s:
nyāsaṃ samācarenmantrī pṛthageva karāṅgayoḥ /
vinyasya hṛdaye tāraṃ bhūḥ śirasyatha vinyaset //
1.27.d:
न्यासं समाचरेन्मन्त्री पृथगेव कराङ्गयोः ।
विन्यस्य हृदये तारं भूः शिरस्यथ विन्यसेत् ॥
1.27.m: the possessor of the mantra should perform ritual placement separately on the hands and limbs: / having placed the praṇava in the heart, he should then place bhūḥ on the head,

1.27.s:
bhuvaḥ śikhāyāṃ svaścaiva kavaye bhūrbhuvo 'kṣiṣu /
bhūrbhuvaḥ svastathātrāstraṃ dikṣu tālatrayaṃ nyaset //
1.27.d:
भुवः शिखायां स्वश्चैव कवये भूर्भुवो ऽक्षिषु ।
भूर्भुवः स्वस्तथात्रास्त्रं दिक्षु तालत्रयं न्यसेत् ॥
1.27.m: bhuvaḥ on the tuft of hair, svaḥ on the armor, bhūrbhuvaḥ on the eyes, / and bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ as the weapon; he should make three claps in the directions.

1.27.s:
tata āvāhayetsaṃdhyāṃ prātaḥ kokanasthitām /
āgaccha varade devi tryakṣare brahmavādini //
1.27.d:
तत आवाहयेत्संध्यां प्रातः कोकनस्थिताम् ।
आगच्छ वरदे देवि त्र्यक्षरे ब्रह्मवादिनि ॥
1.27.m: Then he should invoke the morning twilight deity seated upon a red lotus: / “Come, O boon-granting goddess, three-syllabled expounder of Brahman,

1.27.s:
gāyatri cchandasāṃ mātarbrahmayone namo 'stu te /
madhyāhne vṛṣabhāruḍhāṃ śuklāṃbarasamāvṛtām //
1.27.d:
गायत्रि च्छन्दसां मातर्ब्रह्मयोने नमो ऽस्तु ते ।
मध्याह्ने वृषभारुढां शुक्लांबरसमावृताम् ॥
1.27.m: Gāyatrī, mother of meters, origin of Brahman, homage be to you!” / At noon, mounted on a bull, clothed in white garments,

1.27.s:
sāvitrīṃ rudrayoniṃ cāvāhayedrudravādinīm /
sāyaṃ tu garuḍāruḍhāṃ pītāṃbarasamāvṛttām //
1.27.d:
सावित्रीं रुद्रयोनिं चावाहयेद्रुद्रवादिनीम् ।
सायं तु गरुडारुढां पीतांबरसमावृत्ताम् ॥
1.27.m: he should invoke Sāvitrī, originating from Rudra, expounding Rudra. / In the evening, mounted on Garuḍa, wrapped in yellow garments,

1.27.s:
sarasvatīṃ viṣṇuyonimāhvayedviṣṇuvādinīm /
tāraṃ ca vyāhṛtīḥ satpa tripadāṃ ca samuccaran //
1.27.d:
सरस्वतीं विष्णुयोनिमाह्वयेद्विष्णुवादिनीम् ।
तारं च व्याहृतीः सत्प त्रिपदां च समुच्चरन् ॥
1.27.m: he should call upon Sarasvatī, originating from Viṣṇu, expounding Viṣṇu. / Reciting the praṇava, the seven sacred utterances, and the three-footed verse,

1.27.s:
śiraḥ śikhāṃ ca saṃpūrya kubhayitvā virecayet /
vāmamadhyātparairvāyuṃ krameṇa prāṇasaṃyame //
1.27.d:
शिरः शिखां च संपूर्य कुभयित्वा विरेचयेत् ।
वाममध्यात्परैर्वायुं क्रमेण प्राणसंयमे ॥
1.27.m: filling the head and the tuft, holding it, he should exhale / the breath gradually from the left nostril through others during breath-control.

1.27.s:
dvirācāmettataḥ paścātprātaḥ sūryaścameti ca /
āpaḥ punantu madhyāhne sāyamagniścameti ca //
1.27.d:
द्विराचामेत्ततः पश्चात्प्रातः सूर्यश्चमेति च ।
आपः पुनन्तु मध्याह्ने सायमग्निश्चमेति च ॥
1.27.m: Thereafter he should sip water twice: in the morning with “May Sūrya…”, / at noon with “May the waters purify…”, and in the evening with “May Agni…”.

1.27.s:
āpo hiṣṭheti tisṛbhirmārjanaṃ ca tataścaret /
sumutriyā na ityuktvā nāsāspṛṣṭajalena ca //
1.27.d:
आपो हिष्ठेति तिसृभिर्मार्जनं च ततश्चरेत् ।
सुमुत्रिया न इत्युक्त्वा नासास्पृष्टजलेन च ॥
1.27.m: Then he should perform sprinkling with the three verses beginning “āpo hi ṣṭhā”; / having said “sumitrīyā naḥ”, and with water touched to the nose,

1.27.s:
dviṣadvargaṃ samutsārya drupadāṃ śirasi kṣipet /
ṛtaṃ ca satyametena kṛtvā caivādhamarṣaṇam //
1.27.d:
द्विषद्वर्गं समुत्सार्य द्रुपदां शिरसि क्षिपेत् ।
ऋतं च सत्यमेतेन कृत्वा चैवाधमर्षणम् ॥
1.27.m: having driven away the host of enemies, he should cast [water] on his head with the drupadā verse; / and having performed breath-purification with “ṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ ca…”,

1.27.s:
antaścarasi mantreṇa sakṛdeva pibedapaḥ /
tataḥ sūryāya vidhivadgandhaṃ puṣpaṃ jalāñjalim //
1.27.d:
अन्तश्चरसि मन्त्रेण सकृदेव पिबेदपः ।
ततः सूर्याय विधिवद्गन्धं पुष्पं जलाञ्जलिम् ॥
1.27.m: he should drink water only once with the mantra “antaś carasi…”. / Then, having duly cast fragrance, flowers, and a water-offering to the sun,

1.27.s:
kṣiptvopatiṣṭheddevarṣe bhāskaraṃ svastikāñjalim /
ūrddhūbāhuradhobāhuḥ kramātkalyādike trike //
1.27.d:
क्षिप्त्वोपतिष्ठेद्देवर्षे भास्करं स्वस्तिकाञ्जलिम् ।
ऊर्द्धूबाहुरधोबाहुः क्रमात्कल्यादिके त्रिके ॥
1.27.m: he should stand before the sun, O divine sage, with hands folded in svastika-shape, / with arms raised or arms lowered, respectively, during the triad of morning, noon, and evening.

1.27.s:
uhutyaṃ citraṃ taccakṣurityetattritayaṃ japet /
saurāñchaivānvaiṣṇavāṃśca mantrānanyāṃśca nārada //
1.27.d:
उहुत्यं चित्रं तच्चक्षुरित्येतत्त्रितयं जपेत् ।
सौराञ्छैवान्वैष्णवांश्च मन्त्रानन्यांश्च नारद ॥
1.27.m: He should recite this triad: “ud u tyaṃ”, “citraṃ”, and “tac cakṣuḥ”, / as well as solar, Śaiva, and Vaiṣṇava mantras and others, O Nārada.

1.27.s:
tejo 'si gāyatryasīti prārthayetsaviturmahaḥ /
tato 'ṅgāni trirāvartya dhyāyecchaktīstadātmikāḥ //
1.27.d:
तेजो ऽसि गायत्र्यसीति प्रार्थयेत्सवितुर्महः ।
ततो ऽङ्गानि त्रिरावर्त्य ध्यायेच्छक्तीस्तदात्मिकाः ॥
1.27.m: With “tejo ’si” and “gāyatry asi” he should pray to the splendor of Savitṛ. / Then, revolving around his limbs three times, he should meditate upon the energies consisting of it:

1.27.s:
brahmaṇī caturānanākṣavalayā kumbhaṃ karaiḥ srukstravau bibhrāṇā tvaruṇendukāntivadanā ṛgrūpiṇī bālikā /
haṃsārohaṇakelikhaṇkhaṇmaṇerbibārcitā bhūṣitā gāyatrī paribhāvitā bhavatu naḥ saṃpatsamṛddhyai sadā //
1.27.d:
ब्रह्मणी चतुराननाक्षवलया कुम्भं करैः स्रुक्स्त्रवौ बिभ्राणा त्वरुणेन्दुकान्तिवदना ऋग्रूपिणी बालिका ।
हंसारोहणकेलिखण्खण्मणेर्बिबार्चिता भूषिता गायत्री परिभाविता भवतु नः संपत्समृद्ध्यै सदा ॥
1.27.m: Brahmāṇī, four-faced, holding a rosary, a water-pot, a ladle, and a spoon in her hands, her face having the luster of the morning sun and moon, having the form of the Ṛgveda, a young girl, / adorned and worshipped by jewels tinkling in the sport of riding a swan—may Gāyatrī, thus meditated upon, be ever for our prosperity and abundance!

1.27.s:
rudrāṇī navayauvanā trinayanā vaiyāghnacarmāṃbarā khaṭvāṅgatraghiśikhākṣasūtravalayābhītiśriyai cāstu naḥ /
vidyuddāmajaṭākalāpavilasadvārledumaulirmudā sāvitrī vṛṣavāhanā sitatanurdhyeyā yajūrūpiṇī //
1.27.d:
रुद्राणी नवयौवना त्रिनयना वैयाघ्नचर्मांबरा खट्वाङ्गत्रघिशिखाक्षसूत्रवलयाभीतिश्रियै चास्तु नः ।
विद्युद्दामजटाकलापविलसद्वार्लेदुमौलिर्मुदा सावित्री वृषवाहना सिततनुर्ध्येया यजूरूपिणी ॥
1.27.m: Rudrāṇī, in fresh youth, three-eyed, clad in a tiger skin, holding a club, a trident, a spear, a rosary, and the gesture of fearlessness—may she be for our prosperity! / Sāvitrī, her crest adorned with the crescent moon gleaming in the mass of her matted locks resembling lightning flashes, mounted on a bull, white-bodied, having the form of the Yajurveda, is to be meditated upon with joy.

1.27.s:
dhyeyā sā ca sarasvatī bhagavatī pītāṃbarālaṅkṛtā śyāmā śyāmatanurjaroparilasadgātrāñcitā vaiṣṇavī /
tārkṣyasthā maṇinūpurāṅgadalasadgraiveyabhūṣojjvalā hastālaṅkṛtaśaṅkhacakrasugadāpahmāśriyai cāstu naḥ //
1.27.d:
ध्येया सा च सरस्वती भगवती पीतांबरालङ्कृता श्यामा श्यामतनुर्जरोपरिलसद्गात्राञ्चिता वैष्णवी ।
तार्क्ष्यस्था मणिनूपुराङ्गदलसद्ग्रैवेयभूषोज्ज्वला हस्तालङ्कृतशङ्खचक्रसुगदापह्माश्रियै चास्तु नः ॥
1.27.m: And that venerable Sarasvatī is to be meditated upon: adorned with yellow garments, dark, her dark body embellished with limbs gleaming upon the water, belonging to Viṣṇu, / standing upon Garuḍa, radiant with ornaments—jeweled anklets, armlets, and a gleaming necklace—holding in her hands a conch, a discus, an excellent mace, and a lotus—may she be for our prosperity!

1.27.s:
evaṃ dhyātvā japettiṣṭhanprātarmadhyāhnake tathā /
sāyaṅkāle samāsīno bhaktyā tadgatamānasaḥ //
1.27.d:
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेत्तिष्ठन्प्रातर्मध्याह्नके तथा ।
सायङ्काले समासीनो भक्त्या तद्गतमानसः ॥
1.27.m: Having meditated thus, he should recite while standing in the morning and at midday; / in the evening he should do so seated, with devotion, his mind fixed on her,

1.27.s:
sahasraparamāṃ devīṃ śatamadhyāṃ daśāvarām /
tripadāṃ praṇavopetāṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svarupakramām //
1.27.d:
सहस्रपरमां देवीं शतमध्यां दशावराम् ।
त्रिपदां प्रणवोपेतां भूर्भुवः स्वरुपक्रमाम् ॥
1.27.m: reciting the goddess [gāyatrī] a thousand times at best, a hundred times as middling, ten times as least, / possessing three feet, accompanied by the praṇava, and preceded by 'bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ'.

1.27.s:
ṣaṭtāraḥ saṃpuṭo vāpi vratinaśca yaterjapaḥ /
gṛhasthasya sattāraḥ syājjapya evaṃvidho mune //
1.27.d:
षट्तारः संपुटो वापि व्रतिनश्च यतेर्जपः ।
गृहस्थस्य सत्तारः स्याज्जप्य एवंविधो मुने ॥
1.27.m: The recitation of an ascetic or an ascetic wanderer has six praṇavas or is enclosed [by them]; / for a householder it should have seven praṇavas; such is the recitation, O sage.

1.27.s:
tato japtvā yathāśakti savitre vinivedya ca /
gāyatryai ca savitre ca prakṣipedañjalidrūyam //
1.27.d:
ततो जप्त्वा यथाशक्ति सवित्रे विनिवेद्य च ।
गायत्र्यै च सवित्रे च प्रक्षिपेदञ्जलिद्रूयम् ॥
1.27.m: Then, having recited according to his ability and having offered it to Savitṛ, / he should offer two handfuls of water to the gāyatrī and to Savitṛ.

1.27.s:
tato visṛjya tāṃ vipra uttare iti mantrataḥ /
brahmaṇeśena hariṇānujñātā gaccha sādaram //
1.27.d:
ततो विसृज्य तां विप्र उत्तरे इति मन्त्रतः ।
ब्रह्मणेशेन हरिणानुज्ञाता गच्छ सादरम् ॥
1.27.m: Then, dismissing her, O twice-born, with the mantra beginning 'uttare': / 'Permitted by Brahmā, Īśa, and Hari, depart with honour.'

1.27.s:
dirabhyo digdevatābhyaśca namaskṛtya kṛtāñjaliḥ /
prātarādeḥ paraṃ karma kuryādapi vidhānataḥ //
1.27.d:
दिरभ्यो दिग्देवताभ्यश्च नमस्कृत्य कृताञ्जलिः ।
प्रातरादेः परं कर्म कुर्यादपि विधानतः ॥
1.27.m: Having bowed to the directions and to the deities of the directions with folded hands, / he should also perform the subsequent duties beginning with the morning rite according to the rule.

1.27.s:
prātarmadhyandine caiva gṛhasthaḥ snānamācaret /
vānaprasthaśca devarṣe snāyātrniṣavaṇaṃ yatiḥ //
1.27.d:
प्रातर्मध्यन्दिने चैव गृहस्थः स्नानमाचरेत् ।
वानप्रस्थश्च देवर्षे स्नायात्र्निषवणं यतिः ॥
1.27.m: A householder should bathe in the morning and at midday, / and a forest-dweller, O divine sage; an ascetic wanderer should bathe at the three junctures.

1.27.s:
āturāṇāṃ tu rogadyaiḥ pānthānāṃ ca sakṛnmatam /
brahmayajñaṃ tataḥ kuryāddarbhapāṇirmunīśvara //
1.27.d:
आतुराणां तु रोगद्यैः पान्थानां च सकृन्मतम् ।
ब्रह्मयज्ञं ततः कुर्याद्दर्भपाणिर्मुनीश्वर ॥
1.27.m: For those afflicted with disease and the like, and for travellers, once is prescribed. / Then, holding kuśa grass in hand, O lord of sages, he should perform the Brahmayajña.

1.27.s:
divoditāni karmāṇi pramādādakṛtāni cet /
śarvaryāḥ prathame yāme tāni kuryādyathākramam //
1.27.d:
दिवोदितानि कर्माणि प्रमादादकृतानि चेत् ।
शर्वर्याः प्रथमे यामे तानि कुर्याद्यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.27.m: If the rites prescribed for the day are left undone through negligence, / he should perform them in proper order during the first watch of the night.

1.27.s:
nopāste yo dvijaḥ saṃdhyāṃ dhūrtabuddhiranāpadi /
pāṣaṇḍaḥ sa hi vijñeyaḥ sarvadharmabahiṣkṛtaḥ //
1.27.d:
नोपास्ते यो द्विजः संध्यां धूर्तबुद्धिरनापदि ।
पाषण्डः स हि विज्ञेयः सर्वधर्मबहिष्कृतः ॥
1.27.m: The twice-born who does not attend to the twilight devotion out of wicked intent, when not in distress, / is known to be a heretic, excluded from all religious duties.

1.27.s:
yastu saṃdhyādikarmāṇi kūṭayuktiviśāradaḥ /
parityajati taṃ vidyānmahāpātakināṃ varam //
1.27.d:
यस्तु संध्यादिकर्माणि कूटयुक्तिविशारदः ।
परित्यजति तं विद्यान्महापातकिनां वरम् ॥
1.27.m: He who abandons rites such as the twilight devotion, being skilled in false arguments, / should be known as the foremost of great sinners.

1.27.s:
ye dvijā abhibhāṣante tyaktasaṃdhyādikarmaṇaḥ /
te yānti narakānghorānyāvaccandrārkatārakam //
1.27.d:
ये द्विजा अभिभाषन्ते त्यक्तसंध्यादिकर्मणः ।
ते यान्ति नरकान्घोरान्यावच्चन्द्रार्कतारकम् ॥
1.27.m: Those twice-born who speak [favourably] with those who have abandoned the rites of the twilight devotion and the like, / go to dreadful hells as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure.

1.27.s:
devārcanaṃ tataḥ kuryādvaiśvadevaṃ yathāvidhi /
tatrātyamatithiṃ samyagannādyaiśca prapūjayet //
1.27.d:
देवार्चनं ततः कुर्याद्वैश्वदेवं यथाविधि ।
तत्रात्यमतिथिं सम्यगन्नाद्यैश्च प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.27.m: Then he should perform the worship of the deities and the vaiśvadeva rite according to rule; / there he should properly honour a guest who arrives with food and other offerings.

1.27.s:
vaktavyā madhurā vāṇī teṣvapyabhyāgateṣu tu /
jalānnakandamūlairvā gṛhadānena cārcayet //
1.27.d:
वक्तव्या मधुरा वाणी तेष्वप्यभ्यागतेषु तु ।
जलान्नकन्दमूलैर्वा गृहदानेन चार्चयेत् ॥
1.27.m: Sweet speech should be spoken when they arrive; / he should honour them with water, food, roots, fruits, or the provision of shelter.

1.27.s:
atithiryasya bhagnāśo gṛhatpratinivartite /
satasmaiduṣkṛtaṃ dattvā puṇyamādāya gacchati //
1.27.d:
अतिथिर्यस्य भग्नाशो गृहत्प्रतिनिवर्तिते ।
सतस्मैदुष्कृतं दत्त्वा पुण्यमादाय गच्छति ॥
1.27.m: A guest from whose house he turns away with his hopes broken / departs after transferring his evil deed to him and taking away his merit.

1.27.s:
ajñātagotranāmānamanyagrāmādupāgatam /
vipaścito 'tithiṃ prāhurviṣṇuvattaṃ prapūjayet //
1.27.d:
अज्ञातगोत्रनामानमन्यग्रामादुपागतम् ।
विपश्चितो ऽतिथिं प्राहुर्विष्णुवत्तं प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.27.m: The wise call one whose lineage and name are unknown and who has arrived from another village a guest; / one should worship him like Viṣṇu.

1.27.s:
svagrāmavāsinaṃ tvekaṃ śrotriyaṃ viṣṇutatparam /
annādyaiḥ pratyahaṃ viprapitṝnuddiśya tarpayet //
1.27.d:
स्वग्रामवासिनं त्वेकं श्रोत्रियं विष्णुतत्परम् ।
अन्नाद्यैः प्रत्यहं विप्रपितॄनुद्दिश्य तर्पयेत् ॥
1.27.m: Designating the ancestors, O twice-born, he should daily satisfy / a single Vedic scholar living in his own village, devoted to Viṣṇu, with food and the like.

1.27.s:
pañcayajñaparityāgī brahmāhetyucyate budhaiḥ /
kuryādaharahastasmātpañcayajñānprayantataḥ //
1.27.d:
पञ्चयज्ञपरित्यागी ब्रह्माहेत्युच्यते बुधैः ।
कुर्यादहरहस्तस्मात्पञ्चयज्ञान्प्रयन्ततः ॥
1.27.m: One who abandons the five daily sacrifices is called a slayer of a brāhmaṇa by the wise; / therefore, he should zealously perform the five sacrifices every day.

1.27.s:
devayajño bhūtayajñaḥ titṛyajñastathaiva ca /
nṛpajño brahmayajñaśca pañcayajñānpracakṣate //
1.27.d:
देवयज्ञो भूतयज्ञः तितृयज्ञस्तथैव च ।
नृपज्ञो ब्रह्मयज्ञश्च पञ्चयज्ञान्प्रचक्षते ॥
1.27.m: The sacrifice to the gods, the sacrifice to beings, the sacrifice to the ancestors, / the sacrifice to men, and the sacrifice to Brahman—these are called the five sacrifices.

1.27.s:
bhṛtyamitrādisaṃyuktaḥ svayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ /
dvijānāṃ bhojyamaśrī yātpātraṃ naiva parityajet //
1.27.d:
भृत्यमित्रादिसंयुक्तः स्वयं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ।
द्विजानां भोज्यमश्री यात्पात्रं नैव परित्यजेत् ॥
1.27.m: Accompanied by servants, friends, and others, he should eat restraining his speech; / he should consume food fit for the twice-born and never discard the vessel.

1.27.s:
saṃsthāpya svāsame pādau vastrārddhaṃ paridhāya ca /
mukhena vamitaṃ bhuktvā surāpītyucyate budhaiḥ //
1.27.d:
संस्थाप्य स्वासमे पादौ वस्त्रार्द्धं परिधाय च ।
मुखेन वमितं भुक्त्वा सुरापीत्युच्यते बुधैः ॥
1.27.m: Placing his feet on his seat, wearing half a garment, / or eating what has been vomited from the mouth, he is called a drinker of liquor by the wise.

1.27.s:
khāditārddhaṃ punaḥ khādenmodakāṃśca phalāni ca /
pratyakṣaṃ lavaṇaṃ caiva gomāṃsaśīti gadyate //
1.27.d:
खादितार्द्धं पुनः खादेन्मोदकांश्च फलानि च ।
प्रत्यक्षं लवणं चैव गोमांसशीति गद्यते ॥
1.27.m: One who eats sweetmeats and fruits of which half has already been eaten, / and [eats] visible salt, is spoken of as an eater of beef.

1.27.s:
apośāne vācamane adyadravyeṣu ca dvijaḥ /
śabda na kārayedviprastaṃ kurvannārakī bhavet //
1.27.d:
अपोशाने वाचमने अद्यद्रव्येषु च द्विजः ।
शब्द न कारयेद्विप्रस्तं कुर्वन्नारकी भवेत् ॥
1.27.m: During sipping, rinsing the mouth, and consuming edible substances, / a twice-born should make no noise, O brāhmaṇa; making it, he becomes a denizen of hell.

1.27.s:
pathyamannaṃ prabhuñjīta vāgyato 'nnamasutsayanam /
amṛtopastaraṇamasi apośānaṃ bhujeḥ puraḥ //
1.27.d:
पथ्यमन्नं प्रभुञ्जीत वाग्यतो ऽन्नमसुत्सयनम् ।
अमृतोपस्तरणमसि अपोशानं भुजेः पुरः ॥
1.27.m: Restraining his speech and not despising the food, he should eat wholesome food. / Before eating, the sipping [is done with the mantra]: 'You are the spread of nectar.'

1.27.s:
amṛtāpidhānamasi bhojyānte 'paḥ sakṛtpibet /
prāṇādyā āhutīrdattvācamya bhojanamācaret //
1.27.d:
अमृतापिधानमसि भोज्यान्ते ऽपः सकृत्पिबेत् ।
प्राणाद्या आहुतीर्दत्त्वाचम्य भोजनमाचरेत् ॥
1.27.m: At the conclusion of the meal, he should drink water once with: 'You are the covering of nectar.' / Having offered oblations to the vital airs and the rest, and having sipped water, he should conclude his meal.

1.27.s:
tataścācamya viprendra śāstracintāparo bhavet /
rātrāvapi yathāśakti śayanāsanabhojanaiḥ //
1.27.d:
ततश्चाचम्य विप्रेन्द्र शास्त्रचिन्तापरो भवेत् ।
रात्रावपि यथाशक्ति शयनासनभोजनैः ॥
1.27.m: Then, having sipped water, O best of the twice-born, he should engage in reflection upon the scriptures, / and also at night according to his capacity, with regard to sleeping, sitting, and food.

1.27.s:
evaṃ gṛhī sadācāraṃ kuryātpratidinaṃ mune /
yadā'cāraparityāgī prāyaścittī tadā bhavet //
1.27.d:
एवं गृही सदाचारं कुर्यात्प्रतिदिनं मुने ।
यदाऽचारपरित्यागी प्रायश्चित्ती तदा भवेत् ॥
1.27.m: Thus a householder should follow correct conduct daily, O sage; / whenever he abandons correct conduct, he must undergo expiation.

1.27.s:
dūṣitāṃ svatanuṃ dṛṣṭvā pālitādyaiśca sattama /
putreṣu bhāryāṃ niḥkṣipya vanaṃ gacchetsahaiva vā //
1.27.d:
दूषितां स्वतनुं दृष्ट्वा पालिताद्यैश्च सत्तम ।
पुत्रेषु भार्यां निःक्षिप्य वनं गच्छेत्सहैव वा ॥
1.27.m: Seeing his body impaired by gray hairs and the like, O best of men, / he should commit his wife to his sons and go to the forest, or go together with her.

1.27.s:
bhavetriṣavaṇasnāyī nakhaśmaśrujaṭādharaḥ /
adhaḥ śāyī brahmacārī pañcayajñaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.27.d:
भवेत्रिषवणस्नायी नखश्मश्रुजटाधरः ।
अधः शायी ब्रह्मचारी पञ्चयज्ञपरायणः ॥
1.27.m: He should bathe at the three junctures, maintain nails, beard, and matted locks, / sleep on the ground, practice celibacy, and be devoted to the five daily sacrifices.

1.27.s:
phalamūlāśano nityaṃ svādhyāyaniratāstathā /
dayāvānsarvabhūteṣu nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.27.d:
फलमूलाशनो नित्यं स्वाध्यायनिरतास्तथा ।
दयावान्सर्वभूतेषु नारायणपरायणः ॥
1.27.m: Constantly eating fruits and roots, devoted to Vedic recitation, / compassionate toward all beings, and dedicated to Nārāyaṇa,

1.27.s:
varjaye dgrāmajātāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca /
aṣṭau grāsāṃśca bhuñjīta na kuryādrātribhojanam //
1.27.d:
वर्जये द्ग्रामजातानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च ।
अष्टौ ग्रासांश्च भुञ्जीत न कुर्याद्रात्रिभोजनम् ॥
1.27.m: he should avoid flowers and fruits grown in villages; / he should eat eight mouthfuls and should not eat at night.

1.27.s:
atyantaṃ varjayettailaṃ vānaprasthasamāśramī /
vyavāyaṃ varjayeccaiva nidrālasye tathaiva ca //
1.27.d:
अत्यन्तं वर्जयेत्तैलं वानप्रस्थसमाश्रमी ।
व्यवायं वर्जयेच्चैव निद्रालस्ये तथैव च ॥
1.27.m: One in the stage of a forest-dweller should strictly avoid oil; / he should likewise avoid sexual intercourse, sleep, and lethargy.

1.27.s:
śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇiṃ nityaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ smaret /
vānaprasthaḥ prakurvīta tapaścāndrāyaṇādikam //
1.27.d:
शङ्खचक्रगदापाणिं नित्यं नारायणं स्मरेत् ।
वानप्रस्थः प्रकुर्वीत तपश्चान्द्रायणादिकम् ॥
1.27.m: He should constantly remember Nārāyaṇa holding the conch, discus, and mace in hand; / the forest-dweller should perform austerities such as the Cāndrāyaṇa penance.

1.27.s:
saheta śītatāpādivahniṃ paricaretsadā /
yadā manasi vairāgyaṃ jātaṃ sarveṣu vastuṣu //
1.27.d:
सहेत शीततापादिवह्निं परिचरेत्सदा ।
यदा मनसि वैराग्यं जातं सर्वेषु वस्तुषु ॥
1.27.m: He should endure cold, heat, and the like, and constantly tend the sacred fire. / When detachment arises in his mind toward all objects,

1.27.s:
tadaiva saṃnyasedvipra patitastvanyathā bhavet /
vedāntābhyāsanirataḥ śānto dānto jitendriyaḥ //
1.27.d:
तदैव संन्यसेद्विप्र पतितस्त्वन्यथा भवेत् ।
वेदान्ताभ्यासनिरतः शान्तो दान्तो जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.27.m: only then should he renounce the world, O twice-born; otherwise he would become fallen. / Devoted to the study of Vedānta, calm, self-restrained, with senses conquered,

1.27.s:
nirdvedvo nirahṝṅkāro nirmamaḥ sarvadā bhavet /
śamādiguṇasaṃyuktaḥ kāmakrodhavivarjitaḥ //
1.27.d:
निर्द्वेद्वो निरहॄङ्कारो निर्ममः सर्वदा भवेत् ।
शमादिगुणसंयुक्तः कामक्रोधविवर्जितः ॥
1.27.m: he should always be free from dualities, devoid of ego, free from possessiveness, / endowed with virtues such as tranquility, and free from desire and anger.

1.27.s:
nagno vā jīrṇakaupīnau bhavenmuṇḍo yatirdvijaḥ /
samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ //
1.27.d:
नग्नो वा जीर्णकौपीनौ भवेन्मुण्डो यतिर्द्विजः ।
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः ॥
1.27.m: The twice-born ascetic should be naked or wear a ragged loincloth, with shaven head, / impartial toward enemy and friend, and likewise in honour and dishonour.

1.27.s:
ekarātraṃ vasedgrāme trirātraṃ nagare tathā /
bhaikṣeṇa varttayennityaṃ naikānnādībhavedyatiḥ //
1.27.d:
एकरात्रं वसेद्ग्रामे त्रिरात्रं नगरे तथा ।
भैक्षेण वर्त्तयेन्नित्यं नैकान्नादीभवेद्यतिः ॥
1.27.m: He should dwell for one night in a village and for three nights in a city; / he should constantly sustain himself by alms, and the ascetic should not eat food from a single person.

1.27.s:
aninditadvijagṛhe vyaṅgāre bhuktivarjite /
vivādarahite caiva bhikṣārthaṃ paryaṭedyatiḥ //
1.27.d:
अनिन्दितद्विजगृहे व्यङ्गारे भुक्तिवर्जिते ।
विवादरहिते चैव भिक्षार्थं पर्यटेद्यतिः ॥
1.27.m: In the house of an unblamable twice-born, where the cooking fires are extinguished, when eating is finished, / and which is free from dispute, the ascetic should wander for alms.

1.27.s:
bhavetriṣavaṇasnāyī nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ /
japecca praṇavaṃ nityaṃ jitātmā vijitendriyaḥ //
1.27.d:
भवेत्रिषवणस्नायी नारायणपरायणः ।
जपेच्च प्रणवं नित्यं जितात्मा विजितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.27.m: He should bathe at the three junctures, be dedicated to Nārāyaṇa, / constantly recite the praṇava, having subdued his self and conquered his senses.

1.27.s:
ekānnādī bhavedyastu kadācillaṃpaṭo yatiḥ /
na tasya niṣkṛtirddaṣṭā prāyaścittāyutairapi //
1.27.d:
एकान्नादी भवेद्यस्तु कदाचिल्लंपटो यतिः ।
न तस्य निष्कृतिर्द्दष्टा प्रायश्चित्तायुतैरपि ॥
1.27.m: If an ascetic ever becomes dissolute and eats food from a single house, / no atonement is seen for him, even through ten thousand expiations.

1.27.s:
lobhādyadi yatirvipra tanupoṣaparo bhavet /
sa caṇḍālasamo jñeyo varṇāśramavigarhitaḥ //
1.27.d:
लोभाद्यदि यतिर्विप्र तनुपोषपरो भवेत् ।
स चण्डालसमो ज्ञेयो वर्णाश्रमविगर्हितः ॥
1.27.m: If out of greed an ascetic becomes intent on nourishing his body, O twice-born, / he is to be known as equal to an outcaste, reviled by the classes and stages of life.

1.27.s:
ātmānāṃ cintayeddrevaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam /
nirdvandraṃ nirmamaṃśāntaṃ māyātītamamatsaram //
1.27.d:
आत्मानां चिन्तयेद्द्रेवं नारायणमनामयम् ।
निर्द्वन्द्रं निर्ममंशान्तं मायातीतममत्सरम् ॥
1.27.m: He should meditate on the Self, the taintless deity Nārāyaṇa, / free from dualities, devoid of possessiveness, peaceful, beyond māyā, and free from envy,

1.27.s:
avyayaṃ paripūrṇaṃ ca sadānandaikavigraham /
jñānasvarupamamalaṃ paraṃ jyotiḥ sanātanam //
1.27.d:
अव्ययं परिपूर्णं च सदानन्दैकविग्रहम् ।
ज्ञानस्वरुपममलं परं ज्योतिः सनातनम् ॥
1.27.m: imperishable, full, whose form is sheer eternal bliss, / whose nature is knowledge, stainless, the supreme, eternal light,

1.27.s:
avikāramanādyantaṃ jagaccaitanyakāraṇam /
nirguṇaṃ paramaṃ dhyāyedātmānaṃ parataḥ param //
1.27.d:
अविकारमनाद्यन्तं जगच्चैतन्यकारणम् ।
निर्गुणं परमं ध्यायेदात्मानं परतः परम् ॥
1.27.m: changeless, without beginning or end, the cause of universal consciousness, / devoid of qualities, the supreme, he should meditate on the Self, higher than the high.

1.27.s:
paṭhedupaniṣadvākyaṃ vedāntārthāṃśca cintayet /
sahasraśīrṣaṃ devaṃ ca sadā dhyāyejjitendriyaḥ //
1.27.d:
पठेदुपनिषद्वाक्यं वेदान्तार्थांश्च चिन्तयेत् ।
सहस्रशीर्षं देवं च सदा ध्यायेज्जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.27.m: He should recite the statements of the Upaniṣads and reflect on the meaning of the Vedānta; / with senses subdued, he should constantly meditate on the thousand-headed God.

1.27.s:
evaṃ dhyānaparo yastu yatirvigatamatsaraḥ /
sa yāti paramānandaṃ paraṃ jyotiḥ sanātanam //
1.27.d:
एवं ध्यानपरो यस्तु यतिर्विगतमत्सरः ।
स याति परमानन्दं परं ज्योतिः सनातनम् ॥
1.27.m: The ascetic who is thus devoted to meditation and free from envy / attains supreme bliss, the supreme, eternal light.

1.27.s:
ityevamāśramācārānyaḥ karoti dvijaḥ kramāt /
sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra gatvā na śocayati //
1.27.d:
इत्येवमाश्रमाचारान्यः करोति द्विजः क्रमात् ।
स याति परमं स्थानं यत्र गत्वा न शोचयति ॥
1.27.m: The twice-born who thus observes the duties of the stages of life in sequence / goes to the supreme station, having reached which he does not grieve.

1.27.s:
varṇāśramācāraratāḥ sarvapāpavivarjitāḥ /
nārāyaṇaparā yānti tadviṣṇaḥ paramaṃ padam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde sadācāreṣu gṛhasthaāvānaprasthayatidharmnirupaṇaṃ nāma satpaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.27.d:
वर्णाश्रमाचाररताः सर्वपापविवर्जिताः ।
नारायणपरा यान्ति तद्विष्णः परमं पदम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे सदाचारेषु गृहस्थआवानप्रस्थयतिधर्म्निरुपणं नाम सत्पविंशो ऽध्यायः
1.27.m:
Devoted to the conduct of their class and stage of life, free from all sin, / and focused upon Nārāyaṇa, they attain that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, entitled 'Determination of the Duties of Householders, Forest-dwellers, and Renouncers among Proper Conduct', in the first quarter of the first part in the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.28.s:
sanaka uvāca
śṛṇuṣva muniśārdūla śrāddhasya vidhimuttamam /
yacchrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.28.d:
सनक उवाच
शृणुष्व मुनिशार्दूल श्राद्धस्य विधिमुत्तमम् ।
यच्छ्रुत्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.28.m: Sanaka said: / Listen, tiger among sages, to the supreme rule of the ancestral rite, / hearing which one is freed from all sins; of this there is no doubt.

1.28.s:
kṣayāhapūrvadivase snātvā caikāśano bhavet /
adhaḥ śāyī brahmacārī niśi viprānnimantrayet //
1.28.d:
क्षयाहपूर्वदिवसे स्नात्वा चैकाशनो भवेत् ।
अधः शायी ब्रह्मचारी निशि विप्रान्निमन्त्रयेत् ॥
1.28.m: On the day before the death anniversary, having bathed, he should eat only once; / sleeping on the ground and observing chastity, he should invite the twice-born in the evening.

1.28.s:
dantadhāvanatāṃbūle tailābhyaṅgaṃ tathaiva ca /
ratyoṣadhiparānnāni śrāddhakarttāvivarjayet //
1.28.d:
दन्तधावनतांबूले तैलाभ्यङ्गं तथैव च ।
रत्योषधिपरान्नानि श्राद्धकर्त्ताविवर्जयेत् ॥
1.28.m: Tooth-brushing, betel, and likewise oil massage, / sexual intercourse, medicines, and food belonging to another—the performer of an ancestral rite must avoid these.

1.28.s:
adhvānaṃ kalahaṃ krodhaṃ vyavāyaṃ ca dhuraṃ tathā /
śrāddhakarttā ca bhoktā ca divāsvāpaṃ ca varjayet //
1.28.d:
अध्वानं कलहं क्रोधं व्यवायं च धुरं तथा ।
श्राद्धकर्त्ता च भोक्ता च दिवास्वापं च वर्जयेत् ॥
1.28.m: A journey, quarreling, anger, sexual union, carrying a load, / and sleeping by day—both the performer of an ancestral rite and the eater must avoid these.

1.28.s:
śrāddhe nimantrito yastu vyavāyaṃ kurute yadi /
brahmahatyāmavānpoti narakaṃ cāpi gacchati //
1.28.d:
श्राद्धे निमन्त्रितो यस्तु व्यवायं कुरुते यदि ।
ब्रह्महत्यामवान्पोति नरकं चापि गच्छति ॥
1.28.m: If one who is invited to an ancestral rite engages in sexual union, / he incurs [the sin of] murdering a brāhmaṇa and goes to hell.

1.28.s:
śrāddhe niyojayedvipraṃ śrotriya viṣṇutatparam /
yathāsvācāranirataṃ praśāntaṃ satkulodbagavam //
1.28.d:
श्राद्धे नियोजयेद्विप्रं श्रोत्रिय विष्णुतत्परम् ।
यथास्वाचारनिरतं प्रशान्तं सत्कुलोद्बगवम् ॥
1.28.m: At an ancestral rite one should engage a brāhmaṇa who is learned in the Veda, devoted to Viṣṇu, / intent upon his own proper conduct, tranquil, and born of a noble family,

1.28.s:
rāgadveṣavihīnaṃ ca purāṇārthaviśāradam /
trimadhutrisuparṇajñaṃ sarvabhūtadayāparam //
1.28.d:
रागद्वेषविहीनं च पुराणार्थविशारदम् ।
त्रिमधुत्रिसुपर्णज्ञं सर्वभूतदयापरम् ॥
1.28.m: free from passion and hatred, proficient in the meaning of the Purāṇas, / knowledgeable of the Trimadhu and the Trisuparṇa, and devoted to compassion for all beings,

1.28.s:
devapūjārataṃ caiva smṛtitattvaviśāradam /
vedāntatattvasaṃpannaṃ sarvalokahite ratam //
1.28.d:
देवपूजारतं चैव स्मृतितत्त्वविशारदम् ।
वेदान्ततत्त्वसंपन्नं सर्वलोकहिते रतम् ॥
1.28.m: intent on worshipping the deities, skilled in the principles of the Smṛtis, / endowed with the truth of Vedānta, and delighting in the welfare of all people,

1.28.s:
kṛtajñaṃ guṇasaṃpannaṃ guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratam /
paropadeśanirataṃ sacchāstrakathanaistathā //
1.28.d:
कृतज्ञं गुणसंपन्नं गुरुशुश्रूषणे रतम् ।
परोपदेशनिरतं सच्छास्त्रकथनैस्तथा ॥
1.28.m: grateful, endowed with good qualities, devoted to serving his guru, / and intent on instructing others through narrations of the true scriptures.

1.28.s:
ete niyojitavyā vai śrāddhe viprā munīśvara /
śrāddhe varjyānmavakṣyāmi śṛṇu tānmusamāhitaḥ //
1.28.d:
एते नियोजितव्या वै श्राद्धे विप्रा मुनीश्वर ।
श्राद्धे वर्ज्यान्मवक्ष्यामि शृणु तान्मुसमाहितः ॥
1.28.m: These brāhmaṇas are indeed to be engaged in an ancestral rite, lord of sages. / I shall declare those to be avoided at an ancestral rite; listen to them attentively:

1.28.s:
npūnāṅgaścādhikāṅgaśca kadaryo rogitastathā /
kuṣṭī ca kunakhī caiva laṃbakarṇaḥ kṣatavrataḥ //
1.28.d:
न्पूनाङ्गश्चाधिकाङ्गश्च कदर्यो रोगितस्तथा ।
कुष्टी च कुनखी चैव लंबकर्णः क्षतव्रतः ॥
1.28.m: one with a deficient limb, one with an excess limb, a miser, one who is diseased, / a leper, one with deformed nails, one with dangling ears, one who has broken his vow,

1.28.s:
nakṣatrapāṭhajīvī ca tathā ca śavadāhakaḥ /
kuvādī parirvattā ca tathā devalakaḥ khalaḥ //
1.28.d:
नक्षत्रपाठजीवी च तथा च शवदाहकः ।
कुवादी परिर्वत्ता च तथा देवलकः खलः ॥
1.28.m: one who lives by reciting astrology, and likewise a burner of corpses, / a malicious disputant, a younger brother married before his elder, a temple-priest, a rogue,

1.28.s:
nindako 'marṣaṇo dhūrtastathaiva grāmayājakaḥ /
asacchāstrābhinirataḥ parānnanigatastathā //
1.28.d:
निन्दको ऽमर्षणो धूर्तस्तथैव ग्रामयाजकः ।
असच्छास्त्राभिनिरतः परान्ननिगतस्तथा ॥
1.28.m: a slanderer, an intolerant person, a rogue, and likewise a village priest, / one devoted to false treatises, and one dependent on another's food,

1.28.s:
vṛṣalīsūti poṣṭā ca vṛṣalīpatireva ca /
kuṇḍaśca golakaścaiva hyayājyānāṃ ca yājakaḥ //
1.28.d:
वृषलीसूति पोष्टा च वृषलीपतिरेव च ।
कुण्डश्च गोलकश्चैव ह्ययाज्यानां च याजकः ॥
1.28.m: one who rears the offspring of a Śūdra woman, a husband of a Śūdra woman, / a kuṇḍa, a golaka, and a sacrificer for those not entitled to sacrifice,

1.28.s:
daṃbhācāro vṛthāmuṇḍī hyanyastrīdhanatatparaḥ /
viṣṇubhaktivihīnaśca śivabhaktiparāḍmukhaḥ //
1.28.d:
दंभाचारो वृथामुण्डी ह्यन्यस्त्रीधनतत्परः ।
विष्णुभक्तिविहीनश्च शिवभक्तिपराड्मुखः ॥
1.28.m: one whose conduct is hypocritical, one who is shaven-headed in vain, one intent on another's wife and wealth, / one devoid of devotion to Viṣṇu, and one averse to devotion to Śiva,

1.28.s:
vedavikrayiṇaścaiva vratavikrayiṇastathā /
smṛtivikrayiṇaścaiva mantravikrayiṇastathā //
1.28.d:
वेदविक्रयिणश्चैव व्रतविक्रयिणस्तथा ।
स्मृतिविक्रयिणश्चैव मन्त्रविक्रयिणस्तथा ॥
1.28.m: sellers of the Veda, sellers of vows, / sellers of Smṛti, and sellers of mantras,

1.28.s:
gāyakāḥ kāvyakarttāro bhiṣakchāstropajīvinaḥ /
vedanindāparaścaiva grāmāpaṇyapradāhakaḥ //
1.28.d:
गायकाः काव्यकर्त्तारो भिषक्छास्त्रोपजीविनः ।
वेदनिन्दापरश्चैव ग्रामापण्यप्रदाहकः ॥
1.28.m: singers, poets, those who make a living by medical treatises, / one devoted to reviling the Veda, and an incendiary of village shops,

1.28.s:
tathātikāmukaścaiva rasavikrayakārakaḥ /
kūṭayuktirataścaiva śrāddhe varjyāḥ prayatnataḥ //
1.28.d:
तथातिकामुकश्चैव रसविक्रयकारकः ।
कूटयुक्तिरतश्चैव श्राद्धे वर्ज्याः प्रयत्नतः ॥
1.28.m: as well as one who is excessively lustful, a vendor of juices, / and one who delights in false reasoning—these must be avoided at an ancestral rite with great effort.

1.28.s:
niṃmatrayīta pūrvedyustasminneva dine 'thavā /
nimantrito bhavedvipro brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ //
1.28.d:
निंमत्रयीत पूर्वेद्युस्तस्मिन्नेव दिने ऽथवा ।
निमन्त्रितो भवेद्विप्रो ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.28.m: One should invite [the brāhmaṇa] on the previous day, or else on that very day. / Once invited, the brāhmaṇa should remain celibate and have his senses conquered.

1.28.s:
śrāddhe kṣaṇastu karttavyaḥ prasādaśceti sattama /
nimantrayeddvijaṃ prājñaṃ darbhapāṇirjitendriyaḥ //
1.28.d:
श्राद्धे क्षणस्तु कर्त्तव्यः प्रसादश्चेति सत्तम ।
निमन्त्रयेद्द्विजं प्राज्ञं दर्भपाणिर्जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.28.m: The request for time should be made at the ancestral rite with the words 'By your grace', O best of men; / with darbha-grass in hand and senses conquered, he should invite the wise brāhmaṇa.

1.28.s:
tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya prātaḥ kṛtyaṃ samāpya ca /
śrāddhaṃ samācaredvidvānkāle kutapasaṃjñite //
1.28.d:
ततः प्रातः समुत्थाय प्रातः कृत्यं समाप्य च ।
श्राद्धं समाचरेद्विद्वान्काले कुतपसंज्ञिते ॥
1.28.m: Then, rising in the morning and finishing the morning duties, / the wise man should perform the ancestral rite at the time called kutapa.

1.28.s:
divasasyāṣṭame kāle yadā mandāyate raviḥ /
sa kālaḥ kutapastatra pitṝṇāṃ dattamakṣayam //
1.28.d:
दिवसस्याष्टमे काले यदा मन्दायते रविः ।
स कालः कुतपस्तत्र पितॄणां दत्तमक्षयम् ॥
1.28.m: At the eighth period of the day, when the sun slackens, / that time is kutapa; what is given to the ancestors then becomes imperishable.

1.28.s:
aparāhnaḥ pitṝṇāṃ tu dattaḥ kālaḥ svayaṃbhuvā /
tatkāla eva dātavyaṃ kavyaṃ tasmāddvijottamaiḥ //
1.28.d:
अपराह्नः पितॄणां तु दत्तः कालः स्वयंभुवा ।
तत्काल एव दातव्यं कव्यं तस्माद्द्विजोत्तमैः ॥
1.28.m: The afternoon was assigned to the ancestors by the Self-born; / therefore the ancestral food must be offered at that very time by the best of the twice-born.

1.28.s:
yatkāvyaṃ dīyate dvavyairakāle munisattama /
rākṣasaṃ taddhi vijñeyaṃ pitṝṇāṃ nopatiṣṭati //
1.28.d:
यत्काव्यं दीयते द्वव्यैरकाले मुनिसत्तम ।
राक्षसं तद्धि विज्ञेयं पितॄणां नोपतिष्टति ॥
1.28.m: The ancestral food that is offered by the twice-born at an improper time, O best of sages, / is known to belong to demons; it does not reach the ancestors.

1.28.s:
kāvyaṃ prattaṃ tu sāyāhne rākṣasaṃ tadbhavedapi /
dātā narakamānpoti bhoktā ca narakaṃ vrajet //
1.28.d:
काव्यं प्रत्तं तु सायाह्ने राक्षसं तद्भवेदपि ।
दाता नरकमान्पोति भोक्ता च नरकं व्रजेत् ॥
1.28.m: Ancestral food given in the evening also becomes demonic; / the giver incurs hell and the eater goes to hell.

1.28.s:
kṣayāhasya tithairvipra yadi daṇḍamitirbhavet /
viddhāparāhni kāyāṃ tu śrāddhaṃ kāryaṃ vijānatā //
1.28.d:
क्षयाहस्य तिथैर्विप्र यदि दण्डमितिर्भवेत् ।
विद्धापराह्नि कायां तु श्राद्धं कार्यं विजानता ॥
1.28.m: If the lunar day of the death-anniversary extends [only] for a measure of daṇḍas, O brāhmaṇa, / one who knows should perform the ancestral rite in the overlapping afternoon.

1.28.s:
kṣayāhasya tithiryā tu hyaparāhnadvaye yadi /
pūrvā kṣaye tu karttavyā vṛdvau kāryā tathottarā //
1.28.d:
क्षयाहस्य तिथिर्या तु ह्यपराह्नद्वये यदि ।
पूर्वा क्षये तु कर्त्तव्या वृद्वौ कार्या तथोत्तरा ॥
1.28.m: If the lunar day of the death-anniversary occurs in both afternoons, / the former is to be observed during a decrease, and the latter during an increase.

1.28.s:
muhūrtta dvitaye pūrvadine syādapare 'hani /
tithiḥ sāyāhnagā yatra parā kāvyasya viśrutā //
1.28.d:
मुहूर्त्त द्वितये पूर्वदिने स्यादपरे ऽहनि ।
तिथिः सायाह्नगा यत्र परा काव्यस्य विश्रुता ॥
1.28.m: When it lasts for two muhūrtas on the previous day and on the following day / the lunar day extends to the evening, the latter is renowned for the ancestral food.

1.28.s:
kiñcitpūrvadine prāhurmuhūrttadvitaye sati /
naitanmataṃ hi sarveṣāṃ kāvyadāne munīśvara //
1.28.d:
किञ्चित्पूर्वदिने प्राहुर्मुहूर्त्तद्वितये सति ।
नैतन्मतं हि सर्वेषां काव्यदाने मुनीश्वर ॥
1.28.m: Some say it should be on the previous day when there are two muhūrtas; / this is not the opinion of all in the offering of ancestral food, O lord of sages.

1.28.s:
nimantriteṣau vipreṣu militeṣu dvijottama /
prāyaścittaviśuddhātmā tebhyo 'nujñāṃ samāharet //
1.28.d:
निमन्त्रितेषौ विप्रेषु मिलितेषु द्विजोत्तम ।
प्रायश्चित्तविशुद्धात्मा तेभ्यो ऽनुज्ञां समाहरेत् ॥
1.28.m: When the invited brāhmaṇas have assembled, O best of the twice-born, / he, purified in mind through expiation, should obtain permission from them.

1.28.s:
śrāddhārthaṃ samanujñāto viprānbhūyo nimantrayet //u
ubhau ca viśvedevārthaṃ pighatrarthaṃ trīnyathāvidhi //
1.28.d:
श्राद्धार्थं समनुज्ञातो विप्रान्भूयो निमन्त्रयेत् ॥उ
उभौ च विश्वेदेवार्थं पिघत्रर्थं त्रीन्यथाविधि ॥
1.28.m: Permitted for the ancestral rite, he should invite the brāhmaṇas again: / two for the sake of the Viśvedevas, and three for the sake of the ancestors according to rule,

1.28.s:
devatārthaṃ ca pitrarthamekaikaṃ vā nimantrayet /
śrāddhārthaṃ samanujñātaḥ kārayenmaṇḍaladvayam //
1.28.d:
देवतार्थं च पित्रर्थमेकैकं वा निमन्त्रयेत् ।
श्राद्धार्थं समनुज्ञातः कारयेन्मण्डलद्वयम् ॥
1.28.m: or he may invite one for the deities and one for the ancestors. / Permitted for the ancestral rite, he should have two diagrams drawn:

1.28.s:
caturastraṃ brāhmaṇasya trikoṇaṃ kṣatriyasya vai /
vaiśyasya vartulaṃ jñeyaṃ śūdrasyābhyābhyukṣaṇaṃ bhavet //
1.28.d:
चतुरस्त्रं ब्राह्मणस्य त्रिकोणं क्षत्रियस्य वै ।
वैश्यस्य वर्तुलं ज्ञेयं शूद्रस्याभ्याभ्युक्षणं भवेत् ॥
1.28.m: a square for a brāhmaṇa, a triangle for a kṣatriya, / a circle is known for a vaiśya, and for a śūdra there should be sprinkling [of water].

1.28.s:
brāhmaṇānāmabhāve tu bhrātaraṃ putrameva ca /
ātmānaṃ vā niyuñjīta na vipraṃ vedavarjitam //
1.28.d:
ब्राह्मणानामभावे तु भ्रातरं पुत्रमेव च ।
आत्मानं वा नियुञ्जीत न विप्रं वेदवर्जितम् ॥
1.28.m: In the absence of brāhmaṇas, one should employ a brother, a son, / or oneself, but never a brāhmaṇa devoid of the Veda.

1.28.s:
prakṣālya viprapādāṃśaaca hyācāṃnānupaveśya ca /
yathāvadarcanaṃ kuryātsmarannārāyaṇaṃ prabhum //
1.28.d:
प्रक्षाल्य विप्रपादांशअच ह्याचांनानुपवेश्य च ।
यथावदर्चनं कुर्यात्स्मरन्नारायणं प्रभुम् ॥
1.28.m: Having washed the feet of the brāhmaṇas, had them sip water, and seated them, / he should perform worship according to rule, remembering Lord Nārāyaṇa.

1.28.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ tu madhye ca dvāradeśe tathaiva ca /
apahatā ityṛcā vai karttā tu vikirettilān //
1.28.d:
ब्राह्मणानां तु मध्ये च द्वारदेशे तथैव च ।
अपहता इत्यृचा वै कर्त्ता तु विकिरेत्तिलान् ॥
1.28.m: Between the brāhmaṇas and at the doorway, / the performer should scatter sesame seeds with the verse 'Apahatāḥ...'.

1.28.s:
yavairdarbhaghaiśca viśveṣāṃ devānāmidamāsanam /
dattveti bhūyo dadyacca daive kṣaṇapratīkṣaṇam //
1.28.d:
यवैर्दर्भघैश्च विश्वेषां देवानामिदमासनम् ।
दत्त्वेति भूयो दद्यच्च दैवे क्षणप्रतीक्षणम् ॥
1.28.m: Saying 'This is the seat for the Viśvedevas', / having given [it] with barley and darbha-grass, he should once more offer the waiting upon the allotted time in the divine rite.

1.28.s:
akṣayyāsanayoḥ ṣaṣṭī dvitīyāvāhane smṛtā /
annadāne caturthī syāccheṣāḥ saṃpuddhayaḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.28.d:
अक्षय्यासनयोः षष्टी द्वितीयावाहने स्मृता ।
अन्नदाने चतुर्थी स्याच्छेषाः संपुद्धयः स्मृताः ॥
1.28.m: The genitive case is taught for the inexhaustible [water] and the seat; the accusative in the invocation; / the dative should be used in the offering of food; the rest are taught to be vocatives.

1.28.s:
āsādya pātradvitayaṃ darbhaśākhāsamanvitam /
tatpātre secayettoyaṃ śannodevītyṛcā tataḥ //
1.28.d:
आसाद्य पात्रद्वितयं दर्भशाखासमन्वितम् ।
तत्पात्रे सेचयेत्तोयं शन्नोदेवीत्यृचा ततः ॥
1.28.m: Having procured two vessels accompanied by blades of darbha-grass, / he should then pour water into that vessel with the verse 'Śaṃ no devī...'.

1.28.s:
yavosīti ti yavān kṣitpvā gandhapuṣpe ca vāgyataḥ /
āvāhayettato devānviśve devāḥsa ityṛcā //
1.28.d:
यवोसीति ति यवान् क्षित्प्वा गन्धपुष्पे च वाग्यतः ।
आवाहयेत्ततो देवान्विश्वे देवाःस इत्यृचा ॥
1.28.m: Having thrown barley seeds with 'Yavo 'si...' along with scent and flowers while restraining speech, / he should then invoke the gods with the verse 'Viśve devāsaḥ...'.

1.28.s:
yā divyā iti mantreṇa dadyādarghyaṃ samāhitaḥ /
gandhaiśca patrapuṣpaiśca dhūpairdīpairyajettataḥ //
1.28.d:
या दिव्या इति मन्त्रेण दद्यादर्घ्यं समाहितः ।
गन्धैश्च पत्रपुष्पैश्च धूपैर्दीपैर्यजेत्ततः ॥
1.28.m: With a concentrated mind he should offer the water-offering with the mantra 'Yā divyāḥ...'; / then he should worship with scents, leaves, flowers, incenses, and lamps.

1.28.s:
devaiśca samanujñāto yajetpitṛgaṇāṃstathā /
tilasaṃyuktadarbhaiśca dadyātteṣāṃ sadāsanam //
1.28.d:
देवैश्च समनुज्ञातो यजेत्पितृगणांस्तथा ।
तिलसंयुक्तदर्भैश्च दद्यात्तेषां सदासनम् ॥
1.28.m: Permitted by the gods, he should likewise worship the host of ancestors; / he should give them their true seat with darbha-grass joined with sesame seeds.

1.28.s:
pātrāṇyāsādayettrīṇi hyarghātha pūrvavaddvijaḥ /
śannodevyā jalaṃ kṣiptvā tilosīti tilānkṣaghipet //
1.28.d:
पात्राण्यासादयेत्त्रीणि ह्यर्घाथ पूर्ववद्द्विजः ।
शन्नोदेव्या जलं क्षिप्त्वा तिलोसीति तिलान्क्षघिपेत् ॥
1.28.m: The twice-born should procure three vessels for the water-offering as before; / having poured water with 'Śaṃ no devī...', he should throw sesame seeds with 'Tilo 'si...'.

1.28.s:
uśanta ityṛcāvāhya pitṝnvipraḥ samāhitaḥ /
yā divyā iti mantreṇa dadyādarghyaṃ ca pūrvavat //
1.28.d:
उशन्त इत्यृचावाह्य पितॄन्विप्रः समाहितः ।
या दिव्या इति मन्त्रेण दद्यादर्घ्यं च पूर्ववत् ॥
1.28.m: Having invoked the ancestors with the verse 'Uśantas...', the brāhmaṇa, collected in mind, / should offer the water-offering as before with the mantra 'Yā divyāḥ...'.

1.28.s:
gandhaiśca patrapuṣpaiśca dhūpairdīpaiśaaca sattama /
vāsorbhibhūṣaṇaiśvaiva yathāvibhavamarcayet //
1.28.d:
गन्धैश्च पत्रपुष्पैश्च धूपैर्दीपैशअच सत्तम ।
वासोर्भिभूषणैश्वैव यथाविभवमर्चयेत् ॥
1.28.m: With scents, leaves, flowers, incenses, and lamps, O best of men, / and with garments and ornaments, he should worship according to his means.

1.28.s:
tato 'nnāgraṃ samādāya ghṛtayuktaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ /
agnau kariṣya ityuktvā tebhyo 'nujñāṃ samāharet //
1.28.d:
ततो ऽन्नाग्रं समादाय घृतयुक्तं विचक्षणः ।
अग्नौ करिष्य इत्युक्त्वा तेभ्यो ऽनुज्ञां समाहरेत् ॥
1.28.m: Then, taking the foremost portion of the food mixed with clarified butter, the wise man, / saying 'I shall perform [it] in the fire', should obtain permission from them.

1.28.s:
karavai karavāṇīti cāpṛṣṭā brāhmaṇā mune /
kuruṣva kriyatāṃ veti kurviti brūyureva ca //
1.28.d:
करवै करवाणीति चापृष्टा ब्राह्मणा मुने ।
कुरुष्व क्रियतां वेति कुर्विति ब्रूयुरेव च ॥
1.28.m: When asked, 'Shall I do [it]? May I do [it]?' O sage, the brāhmaṇas / should indeed say, 'Do [it],' 'Let it be done,' or 'Perform [it].'

1.28.s:
upāsanāgnimādhāya svagṛhyoktavidhānataḥ /
sāmāya ca pitṛmate svadhā nama itīrayet //
1.28.d:
उपासनाग्निमाधाय स्वगृह्योक्तविधानतः ।
सामाय च पितृमते स्वधा नम इतीरयेत् ॥
1.28.m: Having established the domestic sacred fire according to the rule declared in his own Gṛhyasūtra, / he should say, 'To Soma accompanied by the ancestors, svadhā, obeisance!'

1.28.s:
agnaye kavyavāhanāya svadhā nama itīha vā /
svāhāntenāpi vā prājño juhuyātpitṛyajñavat //
1.28.d:
अग्नये कव्यवाहनाय स्वधा नम इतीह वा ।
स्वाहान्तेनापि वा प्राज्ञो जुहुयात्पितृयज्ञवत् ॥
1.28.m: Or here, 'To Agni the bearer of funeral offerings, svadhā, obeisance!' / Or ending with 'svāhā', the wise man should offer the oblation as in an ancestral sacrifice.

1.28.s:
ābhyāmevāhutibhyāṃ tu pitṝṇāṃ tṛtpirakṣayā /
agnyabhāve tu viprasya pāṇau homo vidhīyate //
1.28.d:
आभ्यामेवाहुतिभ्यां तु पितॄणां तृत्पिरक्षया ।
अग्न्यभावे तु विप्रस्य पाणौ होमो विधीयते ॥
1.28.m: By these two oblations alone, the satisfaction of the ancestors is imperishable; / but in the absence of fire, the fire oblation is prescribed in the hand of a brāhmaṇa.

1.28.s:
yathācāraṃ prakurvīta pāṇāvagnau ca vā dvija /
nahyagnirdūragaḥ kāryaḥ pārvaṇe samupasthaite //
1.28.d:
यथाचारं प्रकुर्वीत पाणावग्नौ च वा द्विज ।
नह्यग्निर्दूरगः कार्यः पार्वणे समुपस्थैते ॥
1.28.m:
One should perform it according to customary practice, O twice-born, either in the hand or in the fire;
for the fire must not be kept far away when the [time for] Pārvaṇa-śrāddha has arrived.

1.28.s:
saṃdhāyāgniṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ kṛtvā taṃ visṛjetkṛtī /
yadyāgnirdūrago vipra pārvaṇe samupasthite //
1.28.d:
संधायाग्निं ततः कार्यं कृत्वा तं विसृजेत्कृती ।
यद्याग्निर्दूरगो विप्र पार्वणे समुपस्थिते ॥
1.28.m:
Having established the fire, having then performed the rite, the wise man should discard it,
if the fire is far away, O twice-born, when the [time for] Pārvaṇa-śrāddha has arrived.

1.28.s:
bhrātṛbhiḥ kārayecchrāddhaṃ sāgnikairvidhivaddvijaiḥ /
kṣayāhe caiva saṃprātpe svasyāgnirdūrago yadi //
1.28.d:
भ्रातृभिः कारयेच्छ्राद्धं साग्निकैर्विधिवद्द्विजैः ।
क्षयाहे चैव संप्रात्पे स्वस्याग्निर्दूरगो यदि ॥
1.28.m:
He should have the śrāddha performed by his brothers, twice-borns keeping fire, according to the rule;
and when the anniversary of death has arrived, if one's own fire is far away,

1.28.s:
tathaiva bhrātarastatra laukikāgnāvapi sthitāḥ /
upāsanāngau dūrasthe samīpebhrātari sthaite //
1.28.d:
तथैव भ्रातरस्तत्र लौकिकाग्नावपि स्थिताः ।
उपासनान्गौ दूरस्थे समीपेभ्रातरि स्थैते ॥
1.28.m:
in the very same way, his brothers there, even remaining in the domestic fire;
when the Upāsana fire is far away, while a brother is near,

1.28.s:
yadyagnau juhuyādvāpi pāṇau vā sa hi pātakī /
upāsanāgnā dūrasthe kecidicchanti vai dvijāḥ //
1.28.d:
यद्यग्नौ जुहुयाद्वापि पाणौ वा स हि पातकी ।
उपासनाग्ना दूरस्थे केचिदिच्छन्ति वै द्विजाः ॥
1.28.m:
if he should make fire oblation in fire or in the hand, he is indeed a sinner.
When the Upāsana fire is far away, indeed some twice-borns desire [this]:

1.28.s:
tacchaṣa viprapātreṣu vikiretsaṃsmaranharim /
bhakṣyairbhojyaiśaaca lehyaiśca svādyairviprānprapūjayat //
1.28.d:
तच्छष विप्रपात्रेषु विकिरेत्संस्मरन्हरिम् ।
भक्ष्यैर्भोज्यैशअच लेह्यैश्च स्वाद्यैर्विप्रान्प्रपूजयत् ॥
1.28.m:
He should scatter that remainder into the vessels of the twice-borns, meditating on Hari.
He should honor the twice-borns with chewable foods, eatables, lickables, and relishes.

1.28.s:
annatyāgaṃ tataḥ kuryyādubhayatra samāhitaḥ /
āgacchantu mahābhāgāviśvedevā mahābalāḥ //
1.28.d:
अन्नत्यागं ततः कुर्य्यादुभयत्र समाहितः ।
आगच्छन्तु महाभागाविश्वेदेवा महाबलाः ॥
1.28.m:
Then, composed in mind, he should make the renunciation of food in both places:
"May the exalted, very mighty Viśvedevas arrive!

1.28.s:
ye yatra vihitāḥ śrāddhe sāvadhānāṃ bhavantu te /
iti saṃprārthayeddevānye devāsa ṛcā nu vai //
1.28.d:
ये यत्र विहिताः श्राद्धे सावधानां भवन्तु ते ।
इति संप्रार्थयेद्देवान्ये देवास ऋचा नु वै ॥
1.28.m:
Those who are enjoined here in the śrāddha, may they be attentive!"
Thus he should pray to the gods with the verse "Ye devāsaḥ".

1.28.s:
tathāsaṃprārthayadviprānye ca heti ṛcā pitṝn /
amūrtānāṃ mūrtānāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ dītpatejasām //
1.28.d:
तथासंप्रार्थयद्विप्रान्ये च हेति ऋचा पितॄन् ।
अमूर्तानां मूर्तानां च पितॄणां दीत्पतेजसाम् ॥
1.28.m:
Likewise, he should pray to the twice-borns, and to the ancestors with the verse "Ye ca ha".
"To the formless and to the formed ancestors of blazing splendor,

1.28.s:
namasyāmi sadā teṣāṃ dhvānināṃ yogacajakṣuṣām /
evaṃ pitṝnnamaskṛtya nārāyaṇa parāyaṇaḥ //
1.28.d:
नमस्यामि सदा तेषां ध्वानिनां योगचजक्षुषाम् ।
एवं पितॄन्नमस्कृत्य नारायण परायणः ॥
1.28.m:
I always bow to them, the meditators whose eyes are yoga."
Having thus bowed to the ancestors, devoted to Nārāyaṇa,

1.28.s:
dattaṃ haviśca tatkarṇa viṣṇave vinivedayet /
tataste brāhmaṇāḥ sarve bhuñjīranvāgyatā dvijāḥ //
1.28.d:
दत्तं हविश्च तत्कर्ण विष्णवे विनिवेदयेत् ।
ततस्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे भुञ्जीरन्वाग्यता द्विजाः ॥
1.28.m:
he should offer that given oblational food, through that ear, to Viṣṇu.
Then all those brāhmaṇas, restrained in speech, twice-borns, should eat.

1.28.s:
hasato vadate ko 'pi rākṣaghasaṃ tadbhaveddhaviḥ /
yathaācāra pradeyaṃ ca madhunāṃsādikaṃ tathā //
1.28.d:
हसतो वदते को ऽपि राक्षघसं तद्भवेद्धविः ।
यथआचार प्रदेयं च मधुनांसादिकं तथा ॥
1.28.m:
If someone laughs or speaks, that oblational food becomes demonic.
Honey, meat, and so forth should also be given according to customary practice.

1.28.s:
pākādiṃ ca praśaṃseran vāgyatā dhṛtabhaghājanāḥ /
yadi pātraṃ tyajetko 'pi brāhmaṇaḥ śrāddhayojitaḥ //
1.28.d:
पाकादिं च प्रशंसेरन् वाग्यता धृतभघाजनाः ।
यदि पात्रं त्यजेत्को ऽपि ब्राह्मणः श्राद्धयोजितः ॥
1.28.m:
Restrained in speech and holding their dishes, they should praise the cooking and the like.
If any brāhmaṇa engaged for the śrāddha abandons his plate,

1.28.s:
śrāddhahṝntā sa vijñeyo narakāyopapadyate /
bhañjāneṣu ca vipreṣu hyanyonyaṃ saṃspuśedyadi //
1.28.d:
श्राद्धहॄन्ता स विज्ञेयो नरकायोपपद्यते ।
भञ्जानेषु च विप्रेषु ह्यन्योन्यं संस्पुशेद्यदि ॥
1.28.m:
he should be known as a destroyer of the śrāddha; he is destined for hell.
And if the twice-borns, while eating, touch each other,

1.28.s:
tadannamatyajanbhuktvā gāyatryaṣṭaśataṃ japet /
bhujyamāneṣu vipreṣu karttā śraddhāparāyaṇaḥ //
1.28.d:
तदन्नमत्यजन्भुक्त्वा गायत्र्यष्टशतं जपेत् ।
भुज्यमानेषु विप्रेषु कर्त्ता श्रद्धापरायणः ॥
1.28.m:
having eaten without abandoning that food, one should recite the gāyatrī one hundred and eight times.
While the twice-borns are eating, the performer, devoted to faith,

1.28.s:
smarennārāyaṇaṃ devamanantamaparājitam /
rakṣoghnānvaiṣṇavāṃścaiva paitṛkāṃścaviśeṣataḥ //
1.28.d:
स्मरेन्नारायणं देवमनन्तमपराजितम् ।
रक्षोघ्नान्वैष्णवांश्चैव पैतृकांश्चविशेषतः ॥
1.28.m:
should meditate on Lord Nārāyaṇa, the endless, unconquered one;
and especially on verses that destroy demons, those dedicated to Viṣṇu, and those dedicated to the ancestors.

1.28.s:
japecca pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ nāciketatrayaṃ tathā /
trimadhu trisuparṇaṃ ca pāvamānaṃ yajūṃṣi ca //
1.28.d:
जपेच्च पौरुषं सूक्तं नाचिकेतत्रयं तथा ।
त्रिमधु त्रिसुपर्णं च पावमानं यजूंषि च ॥
1.28.m:
And he should recite the Pauruṣasūkta, likewise the three Nāciketa verses,
the Trimadhu, the Trisuparṇa, the Pāvamāna, and the Yajus mantras,

1.28.s:
sāmānyapitathoktāni vadetpuṇyapradāṃ stathā /
itihāsapurāṇāni dharmaśāstrāṇi caiva hi //
1.28.d:
सामान्यपितथोक्तानि वदेत्पुण्यप्रदां स्तथा ।
इतिहासपुराणानि धर्मशास्त्राणि चैव हि ॥
1.28.m:
and likewise those Sāman hymns that are mentioned, which confer merit, he should utter,
as well as the Itihāsas, Purāṇas, and treatises on dharma.

1.28.s:
bhuñjīranbrahmaṇā yāvattāvadetāñjapeddvija /
brāhmaṇeṣu ca bhukteṣu vikiraṃ vikṣipettathā //
1.28.d:
भुञ्जीरन्ब्रह्मणा यावत्तावदेताञ्जपेद्द्विज ।
ब्राह्मणेषु च भुक्तेषु विकिरं विक्षिपेत्तथा ॥
1.28.m:
As long as the brāhmaṇas eat, so long should he recite these, O twice-born.
And when the brāhmaṇas have eaten, he should scatter the scattered offering.

1.28.s:
śeṣamannaṃ vadeccaiva madhusūktaṃ ca vai japet /
svayaṃ ca pādau prakṣaghālya samyagācamya nārada //
1.28.d:
शेषमन्नं वदेच्चैव मधुसूक्तं च वै जपेत् ।
स्वयं च पादौ प्रक्षघाल्य सम्यगाचम्य नारद ॥
1.28.m:
And he should speak [of] the remainder of the food, and recite the Madhusūkta.
And having himself washed his feet and properly sipped water, O Nārada,

1.28.s:
ācānteṣu ca vipreṣu piṇḍaṃ nirvāpayettataḥ /
svastivā canakaṃ kuryādakṣayyodakameva ca //
1.28.d:
आचान्तेषु च विप्रेषु पिण्डं निर्वापयेत्ततः ।
स्वस्तिवा चनकं कुर्यादक्षय्योदकमेव च ॥
1.28.m:
when the twice-borns have sipped water, he should then offer the ancestral rice-ball.
He should perform the svastivācana and give the imperishable water,

1.28.s:
dattvā samāhitaḥ kuryāttathā viprābhivādanam /
acālayitvā pātraṃ tu svasti kurvanti ye dvijāḥ //
1.28.d:
दत्त्वा समाहितः कुर्यात्तथा विप्राभिवादनम् ।
अचालयित्वा पात्रं तु स्वस्ति कुर्वन्ति ये द्विजाः ॥
1.28.m:
and having given it, composed in mind, he should salute the twice-borns.
Those twice-borns who utter svasti without moving the plate,

1.28.s:
vatsaraṃ pitarasteṣāṃ bhavantyucchiṣṭabhojinaḥ /
dātāro no 'bhivarddhantāmityādyaiḥ smṛtibhāṣitaiḥ //
1.28.d:
वत्सरं पितरस्तेषां भवन्त्युच्छिष्टभोजिनः ।
दातारो नो ऽभिवर्द्धन्तामित्याद्यैः स्मृतिभाषितैः ॥
1.28.m:
their ancestors become eaters of leftovers for a year.
With "May our donors prosper!" and other words stated in the Smṛtis,

1.28.s:
āśīrvaco labhettebhyo namaskāraṃ carettataḥ /
dadyācca dakṣiṇāṃ śaktyā tāṃbūlaṃ gandhasaṃyutam //
1.28.d:
आशीर्वचो लभेत्तेभ्यो नमस्कारं चरेत्ततः ।
दद्याच्च दक्षिणां शक्त्या तांबूलं गन्धसंयुतम् ॥
1.28.m:
he should obtain words of blessing from them, and then perform obeisance.
And he should give a sacrificial fee according to his capacity, along with betel and fragrant perfume.

1.28.s:
nyubjapātramathānīya svadhākāramudīrayet /
vājevāje iti ṛcā pitṝndevānvisarjayet //
1.28.d:
न्युब्जपात्रमथानीय स्वधाकारमुदीरयेत् ।
वाजेवाजे इति ऋचा पितॄन्देवान्विसर्जयेत् ॥
1.28.m:
Then, bringing the plate turned downward, he should utter the word "svadhā".
With the verse "Vāje vāje", he should dismiss the ancestors and the gods.

1.28.s:
bhoktā ca śrāddhakṛttasyāṃ rajanyāṃ maithunaṃ tyajet /
tathā svādhyāyamadhvānaṃ prayatnena parityajet //
1.28.d:
भोक्ता च श्राद्धकृत्तस्यां रजन्यां मैथुनं त्यजेत् ।
तथा स्वाध्यायमध्वानं प्रयत्नेन परित्यजेत् ॥
1.28.m:
The eater and the performer of the śrāddha should avoid sexual intercourse on that night;
likewise, he should zealously avoid study of the Veda and travel.

1.28.s:
adhvagaścāturaścaiva vihīnaśca dhanaistathā /
āmaśrāddhaṃ prakurvīta hemnā vāstṛśyabhāryakaḥ //
1.28.d:
अध्वगश्चातुरश्चैव विहीनश्च धनैस्तथा ।
आमश्राद्धं प्रकुर्वीत हेम्ना वास्तृश्यभार्यकः ॥
1.28.m:
A traveler, one who is sick, one devoid of wealth,
or one whose wife is in her monthly course should perform an Āmaśrāddha or [a śrāddha] with gold.

1.28.s:
dravyābhāve dvijābhāve hyannamātraṃ ca pācayet /
paitṛkena tu sūktena homaṃ kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ //
1.28.d:
द्रव्याभावे द्विजाभावे ह्यन्नमात्रं च पाचयेत् ।
पैतृकेन तु सूक्तेन होमं कुर्याद्विचक्षणः ॥
1.28.m:
In the absence of material goods or twice-borns, one should cook only grain.
The discerning man should make the fire oblation with the hymn to the ancestors.

1.28.s:
