The body is of the nature of torment, defiled by filth and the like;

1.31.s:
tasminyo yāti viśvāsaṃ taṃ vidyādātmaghātakam /
sarveṣu prāṇinaḥ śreṣṭhāsteṣu vai buddhijīvinaḥ //
1.31.d:
तस्मिन्यो याति विश्वासं तं विद्यादात्मघातकम् ।
सर्वेषु प्राणिनः श्रेष्ठास्तेषु वै बुद्धिजीविनः ॥
1.31.m:
he who places trust in it should be known as a slayer of the self.
Living beings are superior among all things; among them, those who live by intellect;

1.31.s:
buddhimastu narāḥ śreṣṭhā nareṣu brāhmaṇāstathā /
brāhmaṇeṣu ca vidvāṃso vidvatsu kṛtabuddhayaḥ //
1.31.d:
बुद्धिमस्तु नराः श्रेष्ठा नरेषु ब्राह्मणास्तथा ।
ब्राह्मणेषु च विद्वांसो विद्वत्सु कृतबुद्धयः ॥
1.31.m:
men are superior among the intelligent; among men, Brahmins;
among Brahmins, the learned; among the learned, those of resolved intellect;

1.31.s:
kṛtabuddhiṣu karttāraḥ kartṛṣu brahmavādinaḥ /
brahmavādiṣvapi tathā śreṣṭho nirmama ucyate //
1.31.d:
कृतबुद्धिषु कर्त्तारः कर्तृषु ब्रह्मवादिनः ।
ब्रह्मवादिष्वपि तथा श्रेष्ठो निर्मम उच्यते ॥
1.31.m:
among those of resolved intellect, the doers [of duty]; among doers, expounders of Brahman;
among expounders of Brahman also, he who is free from possessiveness is said to be superior.

1.31.s:
etebhyo 'pi paro jñeyo nityaṃ dhyānaparāyaṇaḥ /
tasmātsarvaprayatnena karttavyo dharmasaṃgrahaḥ //
1.31.d:
एतेभ्यो ऽपि परो ज्ञेयो नित्यं ध्यानपरायणः ।
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन कर्त्तव्यो धर्मसंग्रहः ॥
1.31.m:
Higher even than these is to be known he who is ever devoted to meditation.
Therefore, with every effort, a store of virtue must be accumulated.

1.31.s:
sarvatra pūjyate janturdharmavānnātra saṃśayaḥ /
gaccha svapuṇyairmatsthānaṃ sarvabhogasamanvitam //
1.31.d:
सर्वत्र पूज्यते जन्तुर्धर्मवान्नात्र संशयः ।
गच्छ स्वपुण्यैर्मत्स्थानं सर्वभोगसमन्वितम् ॥
1.31.m:
Everywhere a righteous living being is worshipped; there is no doubt in this.
Go, by your own merits, to my abode endowed with all enjoyments.

1.31.s:
asti cedduṣkṛtaṃ kiñcitpaścādatraiva bhokṣyase /
evaṃ yamastamabhyarcya prāpayitvā ca sadgatim //
1.31.d:
अस्ति चेद्दुष्कृतं किञ्चित्पश्चादत्रैव भोक्ष्यसे ।
एवं यमस्तमभ्यर्च्य प्रापयित्वा च सद्गतिम् ॥
1.31.m:
If there is any misdeed, you will experience it right here afterward.'
Having thus honored him and caused him to attain the good path,

1.31.s:
āhūya pāpinaścaiva kāladaṇḍena tarjayet /
pralayāṃbudanirghoṣo hyañjanādrisamaprabhaḥ //
1.31.d:
आहूय पापिनश्चैव कालदण्डेन तर्जयेत् ।
प्रलयांबुदनिर्घोषो ह्यञ्जनाद्रिसमप्रभः ॥
1.31.m:
and having summoned the sinners, Yama threatens them with the rod of death.
Having a roar like the clouds of dissolution, having the luster like a mountain of collyrium,

1.31.s:
vidyutpra bhāyurghorbhīmo dvātriṃśadbhujasaṃyutaḥ /
yojanatrayavistāro raktākṣo dīrghanāsikaḥ //
1.31.d:
विद्युत्प्र भायुर्घोर्भीमो द्वात्रिंशद्भुजसंयुतः ।
योजनत्रयविस्तारो रक्ताक्षो दीर्घनासिकः ॥
1.31.m:
having terrible weapons with the radiance of lightning, thirty-two-armed,
three yojanas in width, red-eyed, long-nosed,

1.31.s:
daṃṣṭrākarālavadano vāpītulyogralocanaḥ /
mṛtyujvarādibhiryuktaścitragutpo 'pi bhīṣaṇaḥ //
1.31.d:
दंष्ट्राकरालवदनो वापीतुल्योग्रलोचनः ।
मृत्युज्वरादिभिर्युक्तश्चित्रगुत्पो ऽपि भीषणः ॥
1.31.m:
with a face dreadful with fangs, with fierce eyes resembling water-reservoirs,
accompanied by death, fever, and others, terrifying Citragupta also [is present].

1.31.s:
sarve dūtāśca garjanti yamatulyavibhīṣaṇāḥ /
tato bravīti tānsarvānkaṃpamānāṃśca pāpinaḥ //
1.31.d:
सर्वे दूताश्च गर्जन्ति यमतुल्यविभीषणाः ।
ततो ब्रवीति तान्सर्वान्कंपमानांश्च पापिनः ॥
1.31.m:
And all the messengers roar, terrifying like Yama.
Then Citragupta, by Yama's command, addresses all those trembling sinners

1.31.s:
śocantaḥ svāni karmāṇi citragutpo yamājñayā /
bho bho pāpā durācārā ahṝṅkārapradūṣitāḥ //
1.31.d:
शोचन्तः स्वानि कर्माणि चित्रगुत्पो यमाज्ञया ।
भो भो पापा दुराचारा अहॄङ्कारप्रदूषिताः ॥
1.31.m:
who are lamenting their own deeds:
'O sinners, of evil conduct, corrupted by egoism!

1.31.s:
kimarthamarjitaṃ pāpaṃ yuṣmābhiravivekibhiḥ /
kāmaktodhādidṛṣṭena sagarveṇa tu cetasā //
1.31.d:
किमर्थमर्जितं पापं युष्माभिरविवेकिभिः ।
कामक्तोधादिदृष्टेन सगर्वेण तु चेतसा ॥
1.31.m:
Why was sin accumulated by you, destitute of discernment,
with a mind clouded by desire, anger, and the like, and full of pride?

1.31.s:
yadyatpāpataraṃ tattatkimarthaṃ caritaṃ janāḥ /
kṛtavantaḥ purā pāpānyatyantaharṣitāḥ //
1.31.d:
यद्यत्पापतरं तत्तत्किमर्थं चरितं जनाः ।
कृतवन्तः पुरा पापान्यत्यन्तहर्षिताः ॥
1.31.m:
Why were various most sinful deeds performed by you, O people?
Formerly you committed sins being exceedingly delighted;

1.31.s:
tathaiva yātanā bhojyāḥ kiṃ vṛthā hyatidurivatāḥ /
bhṛtyamitrakalatrārthaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ caritaṃ yathā //
1.31.d:
तथैव यातना भोज्याः किं वृथा ह्यतिदुरिवताः ।
भृत्यमित्रकलत्रार्थं दुष्कृतं चरितं यथा ॥
1.31.m:
in the very same way torments must be endured; why lament in vain, O sinners?
Just as evil deeds were performed for the sake of servants, friends, and wives,

1.31.s:
tathā karmavaśātprātpā yūyamatrātiduḥkhitāḥ /
yuṣmābhiḥ poṣitā ye tu putrādyā anyatogatāḥ //
1.31.d:
तथा कर्मवशात्प्रात्पा यूयमत्रातिदुःखिताः ।
युष्माभिः पोषिता ये तु पुत्राद्या अन्यतोगताः ॥
1.31.m:
so by the force of karma you have arrived here exceedingly miserable.
Those sons and others who were nourished by you have gone elsewhere;

1.31.s:
yuṣmākameva tatpāpaṃ prātpaṃ kiṃ duḥkhakāraṇam /
yathā kṛtāni pāpāni yuṣmābhiḥ subahūni vai //
1.31.d:
युष्माकमेव तत्पापं प्रात्पं किं दुःखकारणम् ।
यथा कृतानि पापानि युष्माभिः सुबहूनि वै ॥
1.31.m:
that sin has fallen upon you alone; why [seek] a cause for sorrow?
Just as very numerous sins were committed by you,

1.31.s:
tathā prātpāni duḥkhāni kimarthamiha duḥkhitāḥ /
vicārayadhvaṃ yūyaṃ tu yuṣmābhiścāritaṃ purā //
1.31.d:
तथा प्रात्पानि दुःखानि किमर्थमिह दुःखिताः ।
विचारयध्वं यूयं तु युष्माभिश्चारितं पुरा ॥
1.31.m:
so miseries have been obtained; why be grieved here?
Reflect upon what was previously performed by you!

1.31.s:
yamaḥ kariṣyate daṇḍamiti kiṃ na vicāritam /
daridre 'pi ca mūrkhe ca paṇḍite vā śriyānvite //
1.31.d:
यमः करिष्यते दण्डमिति किं न विचारितम् ।
दरिद्रे ऽपि च मूर्खे च पण्डिते वा श्रियान्विते ॥
1.31.m:
Why did you not consider that Yama will inflict punishment?
Toward the poor and the fool, or the learned and the one endowed with fortune,

1.31.s:
kāndiśīke ca vīre ca samavartīḥ yamaḥ smṛtaḥ /
citragutperitaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvā te pāpinastadā //
1.31.d:
कान्दिशीके च वीरे च समवर्तीः यमः स्मृतः ।
चित्रगुत्पेरितं वाक्यं श्रुत्वा ते पापिनस्तदा ॥
1.31.m:
toward the fugitive and the hero, Yama is known to be impartial.'
Having heard the words uttered by Citragupta, those sinners then,

1.31.s:
śaucantaḥ svāni karmaṇi tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭanti bhīṣitāḥ /
yamājñākāriṇaḥ krūraścaṇḍā dūtā bhayānakāḥ //
1.31.d:
शौचन्तः स्वानि कर्मणि तूष्णीं तिष्टन्ति भीषिताः ।
यमाज्ञाकारिणः क्रूरश्चण्डा दूता भयानकाः ॥
1.31.m:
lamenting their own deeds, remain silent, terrified.
The cruel, fierce, dreadful messengers who execute Yama's command,

1.31.s:
caṇḍalādyāḥ prasahyaitānnarakeṣu kṣipanti ca /
svaduṣkarmaphalaṃ te tu bhuktvānte pāpaśeṣataḥ //
1.31.d:
चण्डलाद्याः प्रसह्यैतान्नरकेषु क्षिपन्ति च ।
स्वदुष्कर्मफलं ते तु भुक्त्वान्ते पापशेषतः ॥
1.31.m:
outcastes and the like, violently cast them into the hells.
Having experienced the fruit of their own evil deeds, at the end, from the remnant of sin,

1.31.s:
mahītalaṃ ca saṃprāpya bhavanti sthaāvarādayaḥ /
nārada uvāca
bhagavansaṃśayo jāto maccetasi dayānidhe //
1.31.d:
महीतलं च संप्राप्य भवन्ति स्थआवरादयः ।
नारद उवाच
भगवन्संशयो जातो मच्चेतसि दयानिधे ॥

1.31.s:
tvaṃ samartho 'si tacchettuṃ yato no hyagrajo bhavān /
dharmāśca vividhāḥ proktāḥ pāpānyapi bahūni ca //
1.31.d:
त्वं समर्थो ऽसि तच्छेत्तुं यतो नो ह्यग्रजो भवान् ।
धर्माश्च विविधाः प्रोक्ताः पापान्यपि बहूनि च ॥
1.31.m:
you are able to sever it, since you are indeed our elder brother.
Diverse virtues have been spoken of, and also many sins;

1.31.s:
cirabhojyaṃ phalaṃ teṣāmuktaṃ bahuvidā tvayā /
dinānte brahmaṇaḥ prokto nāśo lokatrayasya vai //
1.31.d:
चिरभोज्यं फलं तेषामुक्तं बहुविदा त्वया ।
दिनान्ते ब्रह्मणः प्रोक्तो नाशो लोकत्रयस्य वै ॥
1.31.m:
their fruit to be enjoyed for a long time has been stated by you who know many things.
At the end of Brahmā's day, the destruction of the three worlds is declared;

1.31.s:
parārddhadvitayānte tu brahmāṇḍasyāpi saṃkṣayaḥ /
grāmadānādipuṇyānāṃ tvayaiva vidhinandana //
1.31.d:
परार्द्धद्वितयान्ते तु ब्रह्माण्डस्यापि संक्षयः ।
ग्रामदानादिपुण्यानां त्वयैव विधिनन्दन ॥
1.31.m:
and at the end of two parārdhas, the complete destruction of the cosmic egg [takes place].
Of the merits such as the gift of a village [spoken of] by you, O son of Brahmā,

1.31.s:
kalpakoṭisahasreṣu mahānbhoga udāhṛtaḥ /
sarveṣāmeva lokānāṃ vināśaḥ prākṛte laye //
1.31.d:
कल्पकोटिसहस्रेषु महान्भोग उदाहृतः ।
सर्वेषामेव लोकानां विनाशः प्राकृते लये ॥
1.31.m: A great enjoyment is described throughout thousands of crores of aeons; / yet in the elemental dissolution, all the worlds are indeed destroyed.

1.31.s:
ekaḥ śiṣyata eveti tvayā proktaṃ janārdanaḥ /
eṣa me saṃśayo jātastaṃ bhavāñchettumarhati //
1.31.d:
एकः शिष्यत एवेति त्वया प्रोक्तं जनार्दनः ।
एष मे संशयो जातस्तं भवाञ्छेत्तुमर्हति ॥
1.31.m: You have stated that Janārdana alone remains. / This doubt has arisen in me; you ought to resolve it,

1.31.s:
puṇyapāpopabhogānāṃ samātpirnāsya saṃplave /
sanaka uvāca
sādhu sādhau mahāprājña guhyādguhyatamaṃ tvidam //
1.31.d:
पुण्यपापोपभोगानां समात्पिर्नास्य संप्लवे ।
सनक उवाच
साधु साधौ महाप्राज्ञ गुह्याद्गुह्यतमं त्विदम् ॥
1.31.m:
since the experience of merit and demerit has not reached an end at the cosmic dissolution.
Sanaka said:
Well said, well said, O greatly wise one! This is the most secret of secrets.

1.31.s:
pṛṣṭaṃ tatte 'bhidhāsyāmi śṛṇuṣva susamāhitaḥ /
nārāyaṇo 'kṣaro 'nantaḥ paraṃ jyotiḥ sanātanaḥ //
1.31.d:
पृष्टं तत्ते ऽभिधास्यामि शृणुष्व सुसमाहितः ।
नारायणो ऽक्षरो ऽनन्तः परं ज्योतिः सनातनः ॥
1.31.m: Since it has been asked, I shall explain it to you; listen with a well-concentrated mind. / Nārāyaṇa is the imperishable, the endless, the supreme light, the eternal.

1.31.s:
viśuddho nirguṇo nityo māyāmohavivarjitaḥ /
nirguṇo 'pi parānando guṇavāniva bhāti yaḥ //
1.31.d:
विशुद्धो निर्गुणो नित्यो मायामोहविवर्जितः ।
निर्गुणो ऽपि परानन्दो गुणवानिव भाति यः ॥
1.31.m:
He who is pure, devoid of attributes, eternal, free from the delusion of māyā,
who, though devoid of attributes and supreme bliss, appears as if possessed of attributes;

1.31.s:
brahmaviṣṇuśivādyaistu bhedavāniva lakṣyate /
guṇopādhikabhedeṣu triṣveteṣu sanātana //
1.31.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवाद्यैस्तु भेदवानिव लक्ष्यते ।
गुणोपाधिकभेदेषु त्रिष्वेतेषु सनातन ॥
1.31.m:
who is perceived as if differentiated through Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others,
O Sanātana, in these three distinctions conditioned by the attributes;

1.31.s:
saṃyojya māyāmakhilaṃ jagatkāryaṃ karoti ca /
brahmarupeṇa sṛjati viṣṇurupeṇa pāti ca //
1.31.d:
संयोज्य मायामखिलं जगत्कार्यं करोति च ।
ब्रह्मरुपेण सृजति विष्णुरुपेण पाति च ॥
1.31.m:
and having united with māyā, performs all the cosmic work:
in the form of Brahmā he creates, and in the form of Viṣṇu he protects;

1.31.s:
ante ca rudrarupeṇa sarvamattīti niścitam /
prasayānte samutthāya brahmarupī janārdanaḥ //
1.31.d:
अन्ते च रुद्ररुपेण सर्वमत्तीति निश्चितम् ।
प्रसयान्ते समुत्थाय ब्रह्मरुपी जनार्दनः ॥
1.31.m:
and at the end, in the form of Rudra, he devours everything—this is certain.
Having arisen at the end of the dissolution, Janārdana in the form of Brahmā

1.31.s:
carācarātmakaṃ viśvaṃ yathāpūrvamakalpayat /
sthāvarādyāśaaca viprendra yatra yatra vyavasthitāḥ //
1.31.d:
चराचरात्मकं विश्वं यथापूर्वमकल्पयत् ।
स्थावराद्याशअच विप्रेन्द्र यत्र यत्र व्यवस्थिताः ॥
1.31.m:
fashioned the universe consisting of the moving and unmoving just as before.
And wherever the stationary objects and others were situated, O best of Brahmins,

1.31.s:
brahmā tattajjagatsarvaṃ yathāpūrvaṃ karoti vai /
tasmātkṛtānāṃ pāpānāṃ puṇyānāṃ caiva sattama //
1.31.d:
ब्रह्मा तत्तज्जगत्सर्वं यथापूर्वं करोति वै ।
तस्मात्कृतानां पापानां पुण्यानां चैव सत्तम ॥
1.31.m:
Brahmā verily makes all that universe just as before.
Therefore, of sins and merits committed, O best of virtuous men,

1.31.s:
avaśyameva bhoktavyaṃ karmaṇāṃ hyakṣayaṃ phalam /
nābhuktaṃ kṣīyate karma kalpakoṭiśatairapi //
1.31.d:
अवश्यमेव भोक्तव्यं कर्मणां ह्यक्षयं फलम् ।
नाभुक्तं क्षीयते कर्म कल्पकोटिशतैरपि ॥
1.31.m:
the imperishable fruit of actions must inevitably be experienced;
for unexperienced karma does not diminish even after hundreds of crores of kalpas.

1.31.s:
avaśyameva bhoktavyaṃ kṛtaṃ karma śubhāśubham /
yo devaḥ sarvalokānāmantarātmā jaganmayaḥ /
sarvakarmaphalaṃ bhukte paripūrṇaḥ sanātanaḥ //
1.31.d:
अवश्यमेव भोक्तव्यं कृतं कर्म शुभाशुभम् ।
यो देवः सर्वलोकानामन्तरात्मा जगन्मयः ।
सर्वकर्मफलं भुक्ते परिपूर्णः सनातनः ॥
1.31.m:
Action performed, whether auspicious or inauspicious, must inevitably be experienced.
The God who is the inner Self of all worlds, composed of the universe,
enjoys the fruit of all karma, [being] complete and eternal.

1.31.s:
yo 'sau viśvaṃbharo devo guṇamedavyavasthitaḥ /
sūjatyavati cāttyetatsarvaṃ sarvabhugavyayaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde yamadūtakṛtyanirupaṇaṃ nāmaikatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.31.d:
यो ऽसौ विश्वंभरो देवो गुणमेदव्यवस्थितः ।
सूजत्यवति चात्त्येतत्सर्वं सर्वभुगव्ययः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे यमदूतकृत्यनिरुपणं नामैकत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.31.m:
He who is the all-supporting God, established in the distinctions of the attributes,
creates, protects, and devours all this, the all-consuming, imperishable one.

Thus ends the thirty-first chapter, entitled 'Determination of the Duties of the Messengers of Yama', in the first quarter of the Pūrvabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.
